pool.title: Entanglement-induced resilience of quantum dynamics.
pool.abstract: Quantum many-body devices suffer from imperfections that destabilize dynamics and limit scalability. We show that the dynamical growth of entanglement can intrinsically protect generic quantum dynamics against coherent noise and local perturbative noise. Through rigorous theoretical analysis of general quantum dynamics and numerical simulations of spin chains and fermionic lattices, we prove that entanglement entropy growth confines the influence of local Hamiltonian perturbations, thereby suppressing dynamical errors. The degree of protection correlates quantitatively with the entanglement entropy of subsystems, on which the perturbations act, and applies broadly to both analog quantum simulators and real-time control protocols. This entanglement-induced resilience is conceptually distinct from quantum error correction or dynamical decoupling: It passively leverages native many-body correlations without additional qubits, measurements, or control overhead. Our results reveal a generic mechanism linking entanglement growth to dynamical stability and provide practical guidelines for designing noise-resilient quantum devices.
pool.authors: Feng T, Cao Y, Yu W, Zeng J, Li X, Deng XH, Zhao Q

pool.title: Single-gate, multipartite entanglement on a room-temperature quantum register.
pool.abstract: Multipartite entanglement is an essential aspect of quantum systems, needed to execute quantum algorithms, implement error correction and achieve quantum-enhanced sensing. In solid-state quantum registers such as nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond, entangled states are typically created using sequential, pairwise gates between the central electron and individual nuclear qubits. This sequential approach is slow and suffers from crosstalk errors. Here we demonstrate a parallelized multi-qubit entangling gate to generate a four-qubit Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state using a room-temperature nitrogen-vacancy centre in only 14.8 μs-ten times faster than that using sequences of two-qubit gates and close to the fundamental limit set by the hyperfine coupling frequencies. Parallel three-qubit gates are also realized with all-nuclear-qubit subsets. The entangled states are verified by measuring multiple quantum coherences. The four-qubit parallel gate has a fidelity of 0.92(4), whereas the sequential four-qubit gate fidelity is only 0.69(3). The approach is generalizable to other solid-state platforms, and it lays the foundation for scalable generation and control of entanglement in practical devices.
pool.authors: Minnella JD, Ouellet M, Klein AR, Bassett LC

pool.title: 13C and 19F nucleus-electron correlation and self-energies.
pool.abstract: We present a theoretical and numerical study of the correlation between electrons and the fermionic 13C and 19F nuclei. We use the random-phase approximation (RPA) as a valuable tool in obtaining these correlation energies. A special connection between the RPA and second-order perturbation theory for the inter-fermionic interaction is outlined. Subsequently, Green's function-based GW self-energies are evaluated for the nuclear densities. The strong influence of self-interaction errors is demonstrated, and vertex corrections are shown to be strictly necessary to obtain reasonable results. The theoretical and technical requirements for a quantum mechanical treatment of 13C and 19F nuclei are also addressed in this study, thereby facilitating further research in this area.
pool.authors: Vohdin J, Holzer C

pool.title: Radiative Corrections to Inverse Beta Decay: Precision Analysis for Reactor Neutrinos.
pool.abstract: We present a complete calculation of radiative corrections to the inverse beta decay reaction, ν[over ¯]_{e}+p→e^{+}+n, at reactor antineutrino energies using heavy-baryon chiral perturbation theory. Our analysis consistently incorporates quantum electrodynamics, chromodynamics, and electroweak contributions for the first time within this framework. We provide updated, high-precision cross-section predictions with a full error budget and present the positron energy spectrum, including radiative effects. The results are essential for normalizing the reactor antineutrino flux, determining neutrino oscillation parameters with subpercent accuracy, and searching for new physics at nuclear power plants.
pool.authors: Tomalak O

pool.title: Quantified convergence of general homodyne measurements with applications to continuous variable quantum computing.
pool.abstract: In E. Shojaee et al (2025 Phys. Rev. A 112 063708) we introduced broadband pulsed (BBP) homodyne measurements as a generalization of standard pulsed homodyne quadrature measurements. BBP can take advantage of detectors such as calorimeters that have the potential for high efficiency over a broad spectral range. BBP homodyne retains the advantages of standard pulsed homodyne, enabling measurement of arbitrary quadratures in the limit of large amplitude local oscillators (LO). Here we quantify the convergence of standard and BBP homodyne quadrature measurements to those of the quadrature of interest. We obtain lower bounds on the fidelity of the post-measurement classical-quantum state of outcomes and unmeasured modes, and the fidelity of the states obtained after applying operations conditional on measurement outcomes. The bounds depend on the LO amplitude and the moments of number operators. We demonstrate the practical relevance of these bounds by evaluating them for standard pulsed homodyne used for estimating values of the characteristic function of the Wigner distribution, expectations of moments, for quantum teleportation and for continuous variable error correction with GKP codes.
pool.authors: Knill E, Shojaee E, van Meter JR, Kyle A, Glancy S

metadata.venue: Journal of physics. A, Mathematical and theoretical

pool.title: Solid-state spin dynamics of a molecular qubit of Ce3.
pool.abstract: A Ce3+ ion is the qubit of a molecular coordination compound with a [ErCeEr] core that was reported as a platform for the implementation of the three qubit (TQC) repetition code for quantum error correction, by exploiting its interaction with two Er3+ ancillary qubits. We report here a detailed study of the spin dynamics of this Ce3+ qubit by embedding it within [LuCeLu] derivatives of a molecular analogue of the error protected qubit. In these novel molecules the magnetic influence of the Er3+ ancillary qubits is suppressed by replacing them with diamagnetic Lu3+ ions. The pure site-selective heterometallic nature of these molecules is demonstrated and their magnetization dynamics is studied with SQUID measurements. Most notably, the spin dynamics of the qubits are investigated with X-band pulsed EPR in the solid state and their quantum coherence thus quantified. This is achieved by doping molecules of the qubit within an isostructural diamagnetic crystal lattice made of the [LuLaLu] analogue. The solid solution is accessed by co-crystallization of two different [LnLn'Ln] molecules. Their required stability in solution is here unambiguously demonstrated by paramagnetic 1H NMR and mass spectrometry. The influence of the ligand scaffold around the [LuCeLu] metal core on the quantum coherence of the Ce3+ center is discussed.
pool.authors: Serrano-Guarinos J, Hosseinzadeh Z, Swain A, Aguilà D, Barrios LA, Nelyubina Y, Ribas-Ariño J, Roubeau O, Novikov V, Aromí G

pool.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning Correction of Variational Quantum Eigensolver Energies for Molecular Ground States.
pool.abstract: The variational quantum Eigensolver (VQE) provides a scalable route to molecular ground-state energies on near-term quantum hardware, but its accuracy degrades rapidly as system size grows because hardware-efficient ansätze cannot span the full correlation subspace. We introduce a physics-informed ridge regression correction that is trained on the difference between VQE and Hartree-Fock (HF) energies and applied as a postprocessing step requiring no additional quantum resources. The feature setthe VQE-HF energy gap ΔE, its square ΔE 2, the active-space qubit count, the number of active electrons, and two cross-term interactionscaptures the dominant drivers of ansatz error in a low-dimensional, interpretable form. The model is benchmarked on H2, H2O, NH3, CH4, C2H6, and CH3OH using the STO-3G basis set and a state vector VQE simulator using a two-layer Ry-CNOT hardware-efficient ansatz. To assess cross-molecule generalizability, the corrected framework is further tested on CO2, N2, and HCN under both untrained and trained conditions. Absolute energy errors fall from a range of 0.02-0.79 Ha (raw VQE) to 0.0007-0.094 Ha after correction, corresponding to improvement factors of 3× to 640× relative to CASCI reference values. Zero-shot generalization tests yield factors of 9-58×, and including molecules in training improves results by a further order of magnitude in several cases. The three extended molecules exhibit improvement factors of 4-6× in untrained settings and 5-6× after training, providing preliminary evidence of transferability across chemically distinct systems. These findings suggest that the VQE-HF energy gap encodes physically transferable information about correlation-energy saturation, and that even the smallest training set can produce practically useful corrections for near-term quantum chemistry.
pool.authors: Sree KCS, Shankar V

pool.title: Error-Correction Transitions in Finite-Depth Quantum Channels.
pool.abstract: We study error-correction protocols in which a quantum channel encodes logical information into an enlarged Hilbert space through a one-dimensional random circuit with local gates. We consider both noise acting after the encoding step and noise affecting the encoding circuit itself. Using the coherent information, we show that in both settings the infinite-depth limit is governed by a universal random-matrix transition at a critical noise rate, separating a recoverable phase from one where information is lost. We then characterize the leading finite-depth deviations from this universal regime. When noise acts only after a unitary encoder, convergence to perfect encoding is exponential in circuit depth, although boundary effects can delay saturation beyond the design time. When the encoder itself is noisy, the relevant control parameter becomes the circuit fidelity, which replaces the Hashing bound, and convergence is only polynomial in depth.
pool.authors: Sauliere A, Lami G, Ribeiro P, De Luca A, De Nardis J

profiles.intent: Perovskite photovoltaic absorbers, interfaces, device efficiency and operational stability.

pool.title: Bifunctional Modulation of Nucleation and Phase Transformation by TFMBT for Efficient Carbon-Based CsPbI3-xBrx Perovskite Solar Cells.
pool.abstract: All-inorganic CsPbI3-xBrx perovskites have emerged as promising photovoltaic materials owing to their excellent thermal stability and tunable bandgap. However, solution-processed CsPbI3-xBrx films continue to suffer from sluggish crystallization kinetics and poor phase stability, which severely limit device performance. Herein, we introduce 6-(trifluoromethyl)-2(3H)-benzothiazolethione (TFMBT) as a multifunctional additive to regulate nucleation and phase transformation. The N-H and C=S groups of TFMBT synergistically weaken the DMSO-[PbI6]4- coordination via hydrogen bonding and Lewis acid-base interactions, facilitating solvent removal and lowering the nucleation barrier. Meanwhile, the CF3 group engages the N-H group of DMA+ in N-H···F contacts, accelerating DMA+ deintercalation and Cs+ incorporation to expedite phase transformation. This synergistic effect cooperatively accelerates the crystallization kinetics, yielding high-quality films with enlarged, uniform grains and suppressed defects. Benefiting from the optimized crystallization regulation and improved film quality, the TFMBT-modified carbon-based CsPbI3-xBrx perovskite solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 15.34%, significantly outperforming the control devices (12.75%), along with excellent stability.
pool.authors: Liu G, Wu S, Xu Z, Qian Y

pool.title: Molecular surface n-doping enables 22% efficient and highly stable inverted perovskite solar cells under 60% humidity.
pool.abstract: The fabrication of inverted perovskite solar cells (IPSCs) under high-humidity air conditions holds great potential for future industrial applications. However, high humidity imposes significant challenges for obtaining high-quality perovskite films, as it increases surface defects, induces nonradiative recombination, and ultimately degrades the performance of IPSCs. Here, we introduced pyridine-2,6-diamide (PDBA) as an n-type semiconductor to enable the fabrication of high-performance IPSCs in ambient air with a relative humidity ∼60%. The PDBA molecule, consisting of a pyridine ring and amide groups, interacts strongly with uncoordinated Pb2+ ions on the perovskite surface lattice, effectively reducing additional p-type defects at the perovskite/air interface, suppressing carrier recombination, and thereby markedly enhancing the device performance. Under this air condition, the PDBA-treated Perovskite Solar Cells (PSCs) achieved a PCE of 22%, maintaining 93% of their initial efficiencies after 800 h aging under the International Summit on Organic Photovoltaic Stability (ISOS) protocols ISOS-L-2I, demonstrating excellent long-term stability. This study presents a molecular surface n-doping strategy that enables efficient and stable IPSCs under high-humidity air conditions, thereby providing a promising pathway toward their practical industrial development.
pool.authors: Wang H, Zhang Y, Que K, Hou J, Fan Z, Zhang G, Chen R, Xu L

metadata.venue: Journal of colloid and interface science

pool.title: Multifunctional molecule interface engineering enables the development of efficient and stable inorganic CsPbI3 perovskite solar cells.
pool.abstract: A multifunctional molecule, methyl 3-formyl-4-hydroxybenzoate (MHBA), was applied as an interface modification layer for inverted inorganic CsPbI3 solar cells. The MHBA enabled strong interactions with undercoordinated species, effectively passivating interfacial defects and stabilizing the surface lattice of CsPbI3 films. Consequently, an enhanced PCE of 21.11% was achieved with a remarkably improved Voc of 1.211 V and retained ∼91% of the initial PCE after ∼1000 h of storage under an N2 atmosphere at 25 °C in the dark without encapsulation.
pool.authors: Guo F, Wang C, Huang F, Chen F, Wu Y, Wang M, Ye J

pool.title: Ordered Crystallographic Orientation of Dion-Jacobson 2D Perovskites for Ultrastable Solar Cells.
pool.abstract: Dion-Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites show great potential in stability but do not meet theoretical expectations for photovoltaics due to the random crystallographic orientation in films. We herein report ordered crystallographic orientation of the DJ 2D perovskite, achieved by modifying the intermediate-phase film with a Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) phase 2D perovskite based on the two-step processing method. The introduction of the RP 2D perovskite lowers the energy barrier for the transition from the intermediate phase to the 2D perovskite phase with the ordered alignment, and this strategy is applicable to various organic diammoniums-based DJ 2D perovskites. Solar cells with oriented DJ 2D perovskite films achieve an efficiency of 21.1% (19.05% for 1 cm2 devices) and exhibit outstanding stability by retaining 98.1% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking at 65°C under continuous 1-sun illumination (ISOS-L-2 protocol) and 98.7% after 2500 h testing at a relative humidity of 85%.
pool.authors: Liu X, Qu J, Tian H, Zhu Z, Guo X, Li C

pool.title: L-histidine-Modulated Self-Assembled Monolayers for Efficient and Mechanically Stable Flexible Perovskite Solar Cells.
pool.abstract: Flexible perovskite solar cells (F-PSCs) based on inverted architectures with self-assembled monolayer (SAM) hole contacts have recently achieved remarkable efficiency improvements, yet interfacial defects and mechanical fragility at the buried SAM/perovskite interface continue to limit both efficiency and operational durability. Here, we demonstrate that L-histidine serves as multifunctional molecular modulator at the buried SAM/perovskite interface. Proton transfer from the phosphonic acid head group of the carbazole-based SAM to the amino group of L-histidine generates strong interfacial dipole that improves energy-level alignment and hole extraction, while π-π stacking between the imidazole ring and the carbazole unit stabilizes the molecular assembly. The amino and carboxyl groups of L-histidine further coordinate with undercoordinated Pb2+ and halide ions to passivate buried interface defects and promote uniform perovskite crystallization. For flexible applications, the compliant aliphatic backbone of L-histidine transforms the rigid SAM/perovskite contact into a mechanically compliant interface, eliminating interfacial voids and relieving residual tensile strain. These synergistic effects yield a best power conversion efficiency of 23.47% for F-PSCs, along with enhanced operational stability (95.56% retention after 548 h) and mechanical durability (95.06% retention after 1000 bending cycles at 5 mm radius).
pool.authors: Guo T, Zhu Z, Duan D, Wang Z, Zhang Y, Li L, Jin J, Tai Q

pool.title: Suppressing faradaic reaction induced surface nonradiative recombination on a perovskite to improve its photovoltaic performance.
pool.abstract: Surface nonradiative recombination in perovskites, which deteriorates the performance of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), is usually ascribed to perovskite surface defects and interface energy level mismatch. In this study, by combining in situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), electrochemical methods and photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy, we find that surface nonradiative recombination is induced by faradaic reactions between Pb2+/Pb2-x and I-/I-1+x on the FAPbI3 surface under illumination. Depositing Tm(NO3)3 on the FAPbI3 surface suppresses the Pb2+ + xe- ↔ Pb2-x faradaic reaction, thereby decreasing the surface nonradiative recombination and boosting the power conversion efficiency of an FAPbI3 solar cell from 20.29% to 23.15%. The finding offers new understanding of surface nonradiative recombination in perovskites, which is helpful for designing and constructing high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.
pool.authors: Wang Q, Qu Q, Bao R, Liu Z, Hu L, Zheng Z, Wang B, Wan C, Jiang D, Zou Z, Luo W

pool.title: Rational Supramolecular Design of Multifunctional Fluorinated Porphyrins for Efficient and Stable Indoor Carbon-Based Perovskite Solar Cells.
pool.abstract: Precise molecular design is essential for controlling interfacial defects in carbon-based perovskite solar cells (C-PSCs), where recombination losses from the perovskite/hole-transporting layer (HTL) interface and grain boundaries (GBs) limit device performance. Herein, zinc pentafluorophenyl porphyrin (ZnPF) derivatives are developed as supramolecular passivators through p-selective nucleophilic aromatic substitution and incorporated into perovskite films via a green anisole-based antisolvent strategy. Systematic variation of the aromatic substituents provided insight into the relationship between molecular structure, supramolecular packing, and defect passivation. In particular, the p-phenoxy substituent in ZnPF-2 balanced steric effects and promoted ordered molecular packing, leading to more effective interfacial passivation. This multifunctional passivation improved perovskite crystallinity and charge-carrier transport while suppressing non-radiative recombination and interfacial leakage currents. Consequently, ZnPF-2-modified devices achieved a remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 34.29% under 1000 lx illumination, while also showing consistent gains under AM 1.5G conditions and in a compositionally distinct perovskite system, supporting the transferability of the strategy. Moreover, the hydrophobic ZnPF modification improved long-term durability, with devices preserving over 90% of their initial efficiency after 1600 h under ambient storage. This work establishes supramolecular fluorinated porphyrins as effective passivators, demonstrating how rational molecular design can contribute to sustainable indoor photovoltaic applications.
pool.authors: Ruengsuk A, Pudkon W, Kanlayapattamapong T, Seriwattanachai C, Chuasaard T, Intharawicha P, Phromma C, Semakul N, Pakawatpanurut P, Kanjanaboos P, Wongratanaphisan D, Ruankham P

pool.title: Applications of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) in perovskite tandem photovoltaics.
pool.abstract: Perovskite tandem solar cells represent a pivotal route to surpass the Shockley-Queisser efficiency limit of single-junction photovoltaics through complementary spectral utilization. However, interfacial energy-level mismatch and severe non-radiative recombination remain critical bottlenecks that restrict performance and stability. Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) possess unique merits including precise regulation of interfacial energy alignment between the perovskite and charge transport layers and optimized charge transfer dynamics. When deployed in single-junction and tandem perovskite solar cells, SAMs effectively enhance both power conversion efficiency and operational stability. With the rapid advancement of SAM design and engineering, perovskite tandem devices have achieved remarkable performance breakthroughs and broader development prospects. This review summarizes the multifunctional roles of SAMs as efficient charge-selective layers and versatile interface modifiers in perovskite tandem solar cells. We focus on representative applications of SAMs in perovskite tandem solar cells and further discuss the key challenges and future research directions toward scalable, stable, and industrial-grade implementation.
pool.authors: Zhou H, Lu Z, Qu W, Gu Y, Yang Y, Zhao Q, Zou G, Ma Y

pool.title: Solid‐State Perovskite Solar Cells: Discovery and Impact
pool.abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have rapidly evolved from a laboratory curiosity into one of the most transformative photovoltaic platforms in renewable energy research. Since the first demonstration of solid‐state PSCs in 2012, the field has witnessed an unprecedented rise in power conversion efficiency from 9.7% to over 28%, now surpassing established photovoltaic technologies. Beyond efficiency gains, halide perovskites have fundamentally reshaped our understanding of semiconductors by demonstrating that structural softness, defect tolerance, and chemical tunability can coexist with exceptional optoelectronic performance. This perspective reflects on the scientific journey underpinning the rise of perovskite photovoltaics, highlighting key breakthroughs in materials chemistry, device architecture, and interfacial engineering that have driven rapid progress. Particular emphasis is placed on the emergence of inverted architectures and their molecular‐level interface control as defining themes of the field. These insights have enabled the transition from proof‐of‐concept devices to scalable technologies. Looking forward, the true significance of PSCs lies in their potential to enable terawatt‐scale solar deployment. Their compatibility with low‐temperature manufacturing, lightweight flexibility, and bandgap tunability positions perovskite photovoltaics as a cornerstone of future energy systems.
pool.authors: Nam‐Gyu Park

pool.title: Fluorine‐Rich Pentafluorophenyl‐Substituted Electron‐Transport Interfacial Materials for Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
pool.abstract: ABSTRACT The strategic design of electron‐transporting materials is crucial for improving charge extraction and stability in perovskite solar cells (PSCs); however, device performance is often limited by poor interfacial compatibility, which leads to inefficient charge transfer and reduced stability. To address these challenges, two new fluorinated electron‐transport interfacial materials ( ETIMs ), namely TFP‐Bp ( 1 ) and TFP‐Pyr ( 2 ), were developed by incorporating hydrophobic fluorinated phenyl ( FP ) substituents onto biphenyl ( Bp ) and pyrene ( Pyr ) cores. Additionally, a non‐fluorinated pyrene derivative, TP‐Pyr (3) , was synthesized as a structural analogue of TFP‐Pyr ( 2 ) to elucidate the influence of fluorine substitution on interfacial properties and device performance. Single‐crystal X‐ray analysis of compounds 1 and 2 reveals that both molecules adopt markedly twisted conformations, which effectively suppress excessive aggregation. In addition, the fluorinated substituents enhance surface hydrophobicity and strengthen interfacial interactions with the perovskite layer, leading to improved film formation. The optimized devices based on TFP‐Bp ( 1 ) and TFP‐Pyr ( 2 ) deliver power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 21.07% and 21.50% for wide‐bandgap PSCs, respectively, under one‐sun illumination. Notably, excellent indoor performance is also achieved, with PCEs of 41.12% for TFP‐Bp ( 1 ) and 43.34% for TFP‐Pyr ( 2 ), demonstrating their strong potential as ETIM for indoor light applications.
pool.authors: Deebakkrishnan Ganesan, Zhong‐En Shi, Yu‐Wei Su, Rajendiran Balasaravanan, Sheng‐Fong Peng, Yi‐Hsin Hu, Ming‐Han Cai, Shao‐Huan Hong, Cheng‐Liang Liu, Ming‐Chou Chen, Wen‐Chang Chen

pool.title: Soft Dopants for a Soft Lattice: Toward Electronic Doping Control in Metal Halide Perovskite Quantum Dots
pool.abstract: Abstract Electronic doping control in semiconductors is essential for engineering optoelectronic properties yet remains elusive for metal halide perovskite quantum dots (MHP QDs). This perspective assesses the current state of aliovalent substitutional doping in MHP QDs and concludes that the softness of the MHP lattice drives both native defect compensation and thermodynamic phase separation, rendering conventional inorganic dopants ineffective. Instead, we propose soft organic dications as a viable new class of persistent donor dopants for MHP QDs. The distinct optical signatures of majority carriers in QDs make optical spectroscopy a powerful screening tool for electronic doping. In a case study of natively intrinsic and self-p-doped MHP QDs, the orthogonal optical responses upon post-synthetic A-site substitution provide first indications for organic dications as viable donor dopants.
pool.authors: Ole F. Dressler, Sure Ceylan, Nicolas Borter, Maksym V. Kovalenko

pool.title: Intermolecular decoupling of C60 suppresses interfacial recombination in perovskite solar cells
pool.authors: Tao Wang, Ran Luo, Jinxi Chen, Jingcong Hu, Xi Wang, Richard Gundermann, Pengshuai Wang, Z.L. Dong, Zhenhuang Su, Zihao Zhu, Xinyi Du, Jia Li, Hao Tian, Xiao Guo, Yuduan Wang, Ming Lin, Zhenxiang Xing, Mengfei Wu, Rong Ji, Zhenrong Jia, Zhizhong Ge, Ruitian Sun, Ling Kai Lee, Qi‐Lin Zhou, Chao Luo, Lin Zhang, Shunchang Liu, Chuanxiao Xiao, Xingyu Gao, Xudong Yang, Felix Lang, Yi Hou

pool.title: Understanding Repulsion‐Governed Adsorption Mechanism for Efficient Surface Passivation in Blade‐Coated Perovskite Solar Cells
pool.abstract: ABSTRACT Surface passivation of perovskite thin‐films via adsorption of amine‐based derivatives plays an important role in minimizing nonradiative recombination. In this work, we developed a novel and efficient amine‐based surface passivation molecule, cystamine dihydrochloride (CH), which possesses a characteristic symmetric structure and exhibits an anomalous passivation mechanism. It is found that the electron‐rich sulfur atoms in central disulfide moiety of CH experience strong short‐range repulsion with surface iodides of perovskites. Consequently, contrary to the conventional attraction‐driven‐based passivation mechanism, the presence of S–I repulsion dictates a unique binding geometry that drives preferential coordination of the two terminal amine groups with undercoordinated Pb 2+ while displacing sulfur atoms away from the surface. This repulsion‐induced interfacial reconstruction effectively suppresses the formation of deep‐trap Pb–Pb dimers and thereby significantly suppresses nonradiative recombination. Eventually, the blade‐coated PSCs with CH‐passivated achieve a champion efficiency of 26.15% compared to 23.64% of the control devices, along with markedly improved operational stability. This work provides new insight into repulsion‐mediated interfacial passivation for high‐efficiency and stable perovskite solar cells.
pool.authors: Mengting Liu, Jian Ma, Hongbing Li, Yi He, Jingjing Kuang, Jin Liu, Haoran Xu, Tingting Shi, Yaohua Mai, Yuying Hao, Fei Guo

pool.title: Photobattery Architectures to Suppress Charge Recombination
pool.abstract: Abstract Integrating solar energy conversion and storage into single-unit photobatteries offers compact energy supplies. However, achieving sufficient photovoltage to charge batteries without external bias remains a critical bottleneck for these devices. Here, we demonstrate that the photovoltage in Zn-ion photobatteries can be modulated and enhanced by selecting and structuring the photoactive materials strategically. Randomly dispersed electrode configurations are easy to manufacture but they can suffer from charge recombination. In our experiments, these yielded a negligible photovoltage of ∼0.01 V. In comparison, our proposed layer-by-layer design, integrating a solid-state dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC) with an optimized spinel Zn–Mn oxide cathode, increased the photovoltage output to ∼1 V under 1-sun illumination. This dramatic performance enhancement is achieved by better control over interfaces and charge transport and establishes a strategy for improving the architecture of future photobatteries.
pool.authors: Kohei Shimokawa, Byung‐Man Kim, Arvind Pujari, Hooman Abbasi, Tetsu Ichitsubo, Michael De Volder

pool.title: Project Genesis: The Living Triadic Triskele Multi-Modal Energy Platform TECHNICAL ENGINEERING MANIFESTO
pool.abstract: This technical manifesto details Project Genesis: The Living Triadic Triskele Multi-Modal Energy Platform, an open-source, biomimetic hardware architecture published under the CERN-OHL-S-2.0 license. The document establishes a blueprint for an integrated, self-healing solid-state engine that merges a Dragonfly Voronoi thermoelectric network (TEG/TEC) with Triboelectric Nanogenerators (TENG) and Multi-Junction Quantum Dot Solar Skins. By using a twisted, tri-rotational triskele lattice printed from a green-chemistry matrix of sugarcane cellulose nanofibrils (CNF) and milk casein, the system maximizes surface-area-to-volume ratio, inducing micro-vortex turbulence to break up thermal boundary layers. The system acts as a strict Thermodynamic Diode Sandwich, sealing energy inside a high-vacuum chamber containing a Xenon-Helium (\(\text{Xe}+\text{He}\)) noble gas hybrid that serves as an acoustic pipeline for N+2 redundant laser telemetry. To eliminate single-point failures and handle extreme thermal gradients up to 1800K, the core features diamond-doped phonon channels, crushed quartz piezo-electric crystals, and dual-mode lithium-sodium basalt power cells tucked into its geometric gaps. Quantum mechanics like the Chiral Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) effect and topological insulator surface states are leveraged to prevent electron recombination and resistance losses. Real-time management is governed by a deterministic Hybrid MPPT logic controller backed by sub-200ns solid-state e-fuses and liquid gallium vascular self-healing networks, ensuring a self-sustaining operational lifespan spanning 300 to 1,000+ years even under severe stress-test constraints. Core Systems: Project Genesis, Triadic Triskele Matrix, Living Thermal Organ, Multi-Modal Harvesting, Thermodynamic Diode Sandwich, Dragonfly Voronoi Mesh. Nanomaterials & Green Chemistry: Sugarcane Cellulose Nanofibrils (CNF), Milk Casein Binder, Diamond Dust Doping, Crushed Quartz, Liquid Gallium Vascular Channels, Vitrimer Self-Healing. Quantum & Metamaterials: Chiral Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS), Topological Insulator Surface States, Phononic Bandgaps, Chiral Metamaterials, Perovskite Quantum Dots, Plasmon-Phonon Coupling. Power & Storage Electronics: Dual-Mode Basalt Cells, Lithium-Sodium Intercalation, Supercapacitor-Battery Hybrid, Dimpled Surface Topography, Hybrid MPPT (HMPPT), Solid-State E-Fuses. Telemetry & Isolation: N+2 Laser Redundancy, Quantum Cascade Laser (QCL), Wavelength Modulation Spectroscopy (WMS), Quartz-Enhanced Photoacoustic Spectroscopy (QEPAS), Xenon-Helium Hybrid Gas, Diamond-Tungsten Vacuum Skin, Spider-Silk Aerogel. Licensing & Governance: CERN-OHL-S-2.0, Open-Source Hardware, Sovereign Hardware Manifesto, Defensive Publication, Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22970544.

pool.title: Enhancing the performance of numerical simulations and Machine learning implementation of Cs2TiI3Br3-based perovskite solar cells with various ETLs
pool.authors: Md. Shamim Reza, CM Ariful Haque Shamim, Md Saiful Islam, Md Ramjan Chowdhury, Avijit Ghosh, Asadul Islam Shimul, Md. Azizur Rahman

pool.title: Perovskite Solar Cells for Emerging Scenarios: Flexible Wearables, Indoor Light Harvesting, and Semi-Transparent Photovoltaics
pool.abstract: Abstract The diversification of photovoltaic applications has exposed the structural limits of crystalline silicon, which is rigid, opaque, and poorly suited for low-light conditions. This review reframes the central question for perovskite solar cells (PSCs) from maximizing single-junction efficiency toward scenario-driven deployment. We focus on three application spaces where PSCs offer a direct mapping between material physics and performance requirements: flexible/wearable devices, indoor weak light harvesting, and semi-transparent photovoltaics. Four intrinsic properties underpin these scenarios: high absorption coefficient enabling sub-300 nm absorbers, soft defect-tolerant octahedral framework for mechanical strain, low-temperature solution processing compatible with polymer substrates, and compositionally tunable bandgap for indoor LED matching. We review the recent progress of PSCs in the three scenarios and also show the effort of our group on efficient and stable PSCs. At last, we identify recurring bottleneck defects, interfaces, stability and outline future directions including scenario-specific protocols, co-design strategies, and parallel advances in cost and recyclability.
pool.authors: Haoyi Sun, Yadi Zhang, Meng Zhang, Guangyao Wu, Yuhong Xu, Wendong Zhu, Rong Xuan, Xinlei Gan, Xiaohui Liu, Like Huang, Jing Zhang, Yuejin Zhu

pool.title: Chemical Functionality Engineering of Anti‐Solvent Additives for Photostable Perovskite Solar Cells
pool.abstract: Metal-halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieve high power-conversion efficiencies but remain susceptible to photo-induced degradation caused by mobile ions and phase segregation. Here, we investigate positional isomers of pyridine-carboxylic acid, namely pyridine-2-carboxylic acid (2-PC) and pyridine-4-carboxylic acid (4-PC), as anti-solvent additives to clarify how functional-group orientation governs defect passivation and photo-induced degradation. Both additives improve film morphology and reduce trap density; however, 4-PC, in which the carboxyl group is positioned opposite the pyridine nitrogen, provides markedly stronger passivation by virtue of its more favorable passivation geometry. As a result, 4-PC suppresses light-induced photoluminescence red shift, reduces trap density by approximately 27%, and enables unencapsulated devices to retain over 88% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h. Spectroscopic and transient analyses further indicate that 4-PC simultaneously passivates Pb-related defects and halide vacancies, thereby suppressing ion migration and halide phase segregation under operating conditions. These findings establish positional-isomer engineering as a practical molecular design principle for developing simple yet effective anti-solvent additives toward improved photo-induced phase stability in perovskite photovoltaics.
pool.authors: Wonjong Lee, Muhammad Adnan, Zobia Irshad, Sunkyu Kim, Siwon Yun, Hyeji Han, Minwoo Lee, Dong Gyu Lee, Hyeonsu Son, Tran Thi Ha Giang, Hyo Sik Chang, Seulki Song, Yen‐Hung Lin, Tae Kyung Lee, Jae Sung Yun, Jongchul Lim

pool.title: Hybrid photovoltaic–thermoelectric generator renewable energy systems-a comprehensive review and bibliometric analysis
pool.abstract: Advancing renewable energy sources is crucial to meeting the growing energy demand. Solar energy conversion systems, such as photovoltaic (PV) cells and thermoelectric generators (TEG), play a significant role in addressing this need. PV systems primarily convert visible and ultraviolet (UV) light from sunlight, while TEGs utilize the infrared (IR) spectrum to generate electrical energy. Combining PV systems with TEGs allows for more comprehensive utilization of the solar spectrum, resulting in improved energy production. Recent research has focused on PV/TEGs hybrid generation systems (HGSs) to boost conversion efficiency. By harnessing the heat released from the PV system, TEGs can enhance the hybrid system’s overall power output and efficiency, potentially leading to superior performance. However, integrating these systems presents challenges due to their differing characteristics. This review aims to explain the fundamental principles of PV and thermoelectric generators, analyze recent research findings in enhancing this hybrid system’s performance, and explore various approaches to optimizing the performance of these hybrid systems. In sum, a review of previous works shows compelling evidence for integration between PV and TEG. For instance, previous works have demonstrated overall efficiency gains of 7.33%–32.09%. Furthermore, reported results confirm that TEG integration can reduce PV operating temperature while generating additional power from waste heat. An assessment of a PV-TEG system using real-world data reveals a 6% improvement in energy output compared to standalone PV systems. In addition, the phase change material can mitigate fluctuating solar irradiation, resulting in an enhancement of daily overall efficiency 25.55%–26.57%.
pool.authors: Hegazy Rezk, Walid Merrouche, Anas Bouaouda, Fatma A. Hashim

pool.title: A Light Management Strategy for Perovskite Solar Cells: One-Step Wet-Chemical Etching of Nanoporous ITO Surface Layers
pool.abstract: Abstract Given the interfacial Fresnel reflection caused by refractive-index mismatch between transparent conducting oxide (TCO) substrates and adjacent functional layers, introducing an antireflection interlayer for light management can provide an effective route to improve the performance of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Here, we present a facile one-step wet-chemical etching strategy using dilute hydrochloric acid to fabricate a nanoporous architecture on indium tin oxide (ITO) surfaces. By tailoring the optical properties of two commonly used ITO substrates with different thicknesses, we obtain a broadband increase in absolute transmittance across the 350–1000 nm wavelength range. When applied to PSCs, the etched ITO substrate introduces a graded-refractive-index transition layer that reduces reflection losses and enhances light absorption, thereby increasing the short-circuit current density (JSC) of the p–i–n devices from 25.00 mA cm–2 and 25.02 mA cm–2 to 25.46 mA cm–2. In addition, the introduction of the nanoporous structure increases the effective interfacial contact area and is accompanied by possible changes in the interfacial chemical states and interactions, leading to an increase in the fill factor (FF) from 84.94% and 84.52% to 86.22%. Overall, the device fabricated on the etched ITO substrate achieves a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 24.90%. This work demonstrates a mild, low-cost, and scalable ITO interface-engineering strategy for light management in PSCs and provides new insight into optical regulation in TCO-based optoelectronic devices, including thin-film solar cells, flat-panel displays, organic light-emitting diodes, and functional windows.
pool.authors: Feiyang Cheng, Yang Gui, Hailong Feng, Siyu Jin, Ming Ruan, Deren Yang, Jingjing Xue, Lei Wang

pool.title: Light as a master switch: a critical review of photonanozymes from design to applications
pool.abstract: Abstract Despite the widespread industrial applications of nanozymes, their usage is often limited by mechanistic factors. They lack reaction control with catalyst fouling, which limits catalytic turnover and makes nanozyme recovery an energy-intensive process at large scale. These mechanistic challenges have been addressed by the evolution of photoresponsiveness into nanozymes called as photonanozymes (PNZs). This research is focused to critically assess the architecure of photonanozymes leading to photoresponsivness. A three domain framework deconstructing photoresponsive mechanism with research road map to guided subsequent investigation constitutes the distinctive contribution of this review. The photoresponsive architechture elucidates the mechanism of light gated catalysis governed by wavelength selectivity and spatiotemporal precison. Thereby, expanding the enzyme mimicking catalysis and its applciations in environmental remediation, theragnostics, cancer therapy, biosensing and biofuel synthesis. Rather than merely describing the operating principles of photonanozymes, rational foundation is build up which determines future design. Challenges impeding photocatalytic mechanisms are critically examined including limited wavelength selectivity, insufficient opertional stability and difficulty of achieving reproducible and scalable synthesis. Presented review strategizes a forward-looking roadmap centered around robust PNZ design, standardized performance, and translation of light-programmable catalysis from laboratory proof-of-concept to practical technology. Through a rigorous and comprehensive examination of inherent complexities, it frames PNZs as a transformative step towards programmable, self-healing nanomaterials with controlled implications, serving as an invaluable resource for those seeking orientation within photocatalysis. Furthermore, it reaches beyond its immediate boundaries, presenting new ideas, evidence-based conclusions, and prospective directions intended to influence the course of future investigations.
pool.authors: Faria Fatima, Syed Saqib Ali Zaidi, Guang Yang, He Huang, Xiao‐Man Sun

pool.title: Rational design of biochar for carbon dioxide capture and catalytic conversion
pool.abstract: The continuous increase in carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions has intensified the need for efficient carbon capture and utilization (CCU) technologies. Biochar has emerged as a promising, cost-effective, and sustainable platform for CCU. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the rational design of biochar for CO2 capture and subsequent catalytic conversion. We first discuss various synthesis methods and activation strategies for tailoring the physicochemical properties of biochar. We then elucidate the mechanisms of CO2 capture, highlighting the roles of pore modification and heteroatom functionalities in enhancing both physisorption and chemisorption. Furthermore, the roles of biochar in thermocatalytic, electrocatalytic, and photocatalytic CO2 conversion are critically examined, with particular emphasis on its function as a multifunctional support for metal nanoparticles, molecular catalysts, single atoms, and nanoclusters. Finally, we outline key challenges and future directions for the rational development of next-generation biochar toward practical carbon-neutral technologies. Accordingly, this review establishes a rational design framework based on application demand, key performance parameters, and targeted synthesis strategies, thereby linking practical CCU requirements with the controlled engineering of biochar porosity, surface chemistry, conductivity, and catalytic functionality.
pool.authors: Joonhee Ma, Jae Hak Kim, Mojtaba Abdi‐Jalebi, Soo Young Kim

pool.title: Design and numerical analysis of antimony trisulfide (Sb 2 S 3 ) solar cell using SCAPS-1D software
pool.abstract: Abstract Abstract This study numerically analyzes an Sb₂S₃ based solar cell with the structure FTO/ETL/Sb₂S₃/SpiroOMeTAD/Au using the SCAPS1D software under the AM1.5G spectrum.The impact of series resistance (Rs), defect density and the effective capture cross-section of charge carriers at the Sb₂S₃/CdS interface were first studied. Alternative electron transport layers (ETLs) including Cd1-xZnₓS, ZnO1-xSx, and TiO₂, were then investigated. The results indicate that optimal band alignment at the ETL/Sb2S3 interface is achieved for a sulfur content of 0.6 in ZnO1-xSx and a zinc contents of 0.5 in Cd1-xZnₓS. Under these conditions, power conversion efficiencies (PCE) of 16.53 % for Cd0.5Zn0.5S, 16.38 % for ZnO0.4S0.6, and 15.67 % for TiO2 were obtained. These improvements are attributed to a reduction in the recombination rate at the Sb₂S₃/ETL interface. Finally, introducing a second ZnO0.25S0.75 buffer layer further increased the corresponding efficiencies to 17.55 %, 17.50 %, and 17.00 % respectively, demonstrating enhanced device overall performance despite a slight decrease in optical transmission to the absorber.The results obtained in this work provide important insights into the optimization of Sb₂S₃ based solar cells.
pool.authors: Soulemani Sangare, Soumaïla Ouédraogo, M.Osias SORY, Yacouba Coulibaly, Raguilignaba Sam, François Zougmoré

pool.title: Plasmon enhanced light management in perovskite/CIGS tandem solar cells using four sided nanopyramids
pool.abstract: This study investigates the effect of plasmonic nanoparticle geometry on the optical and photovoltaic performance of perovskite/CIGS tandem solar cells using three-dimensional finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations and drift–diffusion device modeling. Three nanoparticle geometries—four-sided pyramidal, cubic, and cylindrical—were incorporated within the CIGS absorber to enhance light trapping through localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) and plasmon-assisted scattering. All nanoparticle configurations improved absorption relative to the reference device, with the four-sided nanopyramid providing the most pronounced and broadband enhancement owing to its sharp-edge field localization and efficient scattering pathways; the numerical convergence of the optical results was confirmed through a quantitative mesh-independence analysis. Current–voltage analysis showed that the four-sided nanopyramid produced the highest short-circuit current density, followed by the cubic and cylindrical structures. Optimization of the pyramid dimensions revealed that for a = 75 nm (length, width, and height), the photocurrent approached 18 mA/cm 2 , compared with approximately 12 mA/cm 2 for the reference cell without nanoparticles. Based on the idealized photovoltaic model, this enhancement corresponds to a power-conversion efficiency (PCE) rise from 16.22 % (reference) to 26.27 % (optimized nanopyramid device). To evaluate the physical relevance of this result, drift–diffusion device simulations were additionally performed under ideal and realistic contact conditions. Under ideal-contact conditions, the nanopyramid-integrated device achieved a PCE of 24.80 %, in close agreement with the idealized model, whereas realistic-contact conditions, including series resistance and contact-related losses, reduced the PCE to 20.63 %. Carrier-generation rate distributions confirmed that sharp-tip geometries concentrate electromagnetic fields more effectively than smoother counterparts, producing stronger localized carrier generation.
pool.authors: Hamid Heidarzadeh

pool.title: Accelerated solar light driven photocatalytic degradation of rhodamine B6g using a multicomponent Co3O4/Ag@ZnO/g-C3N4 composite
pool.abstract: This work outlines the design and synthesis of a Co₃O₄/Ag@ZnO/g-C₃N₄ nanosheet composite using a simple hydrothermal method. FESEM-EDX and XPS investigations verified the successful integration of the separate components, and XRD and FTIR data showed that the parent materials’ structural integrity and important functional groups were mostly retained inside the composite. Extended visible light absorption and inhibited charge carrier recombination were found in optical investigations employing UV-DRS and photoluminescence spectroscopy. The composite has a high surface area (83.2 m²/g) and a sufficient pore diameter (5.1 nm), which improves catalytic efficiency. Rhodamine B6g (RhB6g), a less studied model cationic fluorescent dye, was degraded under natural sunlight irradiation in order to evaluate the photocatalytic effectiveness of the produced material. With 40 mg of catalyst, the composite showed exceptional activity, degrading a 30 ppm dye solution at pH 12 up to 98% in 80 minutes. Among the studied materials, the composite photocatalyst showed the highest photocatalytic activity with rate constant of 0.0515 minutes -1 followed by pseudo-first order kinetic module which is attributed to effective heterojunction formation, reduced crystallite size, enhanced surface area and pore volume, extended visible-light absorption, and efficient suppression of photogenerated charge carrier recombination Experiments using radical scavenging revealed that superoxide and hydroxyl radicals are key players in the degradation process. ICP/OES result indicated the limited metal leaching and TOC result showed the partial mineralisation. Furthermore, the composite retained structural integrity and catalytic efficacy after multiple cycles, indicating its potential use in practical wastewater treatment systems.
pool.authors: Debapriya Pradhan, Susanta Kumar Biswal

pool.title: Atomic-level design and device modeling of lead-free Cs2AgSbCl6 double perovskite solar cells through DFT, SCAPS-1D, and predictive algorithms
pool.abstract: Lead-free double perovskite solar cells (DPSCs) have emerged as attractive alternatives to conventional lead-based perovskites because of their superior environmental compatibility, enhanced chemical stability, and reduced toxicity. In this research study, the performance of a solar cell architecture FTO/IGZO/Cs 2 AgSbCl 6 /Cu 2 O are systematically studied by the simulation software known as SCAPS-1D. DFT calculations were performed using WIEN2k package to investigate structural and optoelectronic properties of Cs 2 AgSbCl 6 material to determine its suitability for photovoltaic applications. Afterwards, the photovoltaic performance is comprehensively studied with respect to the absorber thickness (t active ), bulk defect density (N t ), donor and acceptor concentration (N A and N D ), carrier mobility (u n and u p ), operating temperature (T), illumination intensity (I sun ), series and shunt resistance (R s and R sh ) and contact work functions (WFs). The optimized device shows a higher power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 28.53%, open circuit voltage (V oc ) of ~1.068 V, short circuit current density (J sc ) of 32.81 mA cm −2 and fill factor (FF) of 81.38%, which is found better than the initial device having PCE of 24.77%. The improvement in performance mainly has been attributed to the improvement in energy-band alignment (EBA), efficient extraction of the carriers, suppression of the interfacial recombination, and optimization of the electrical transport through the IGZO/Cs 2 AgSbCl 6 /Cu 2 O heterostructure. In addition, the data set created from the above-mentioned SCAPS-1D simulations was used to train six supervised machine learning algorithms including Linear Regression (LR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (xGB), to further accelerate the optimization of the device. The machine-learning analysis accurately estimated the photovoltaic (PV) parameters and defined the major factors that affect the PV performance, such as the carrier mobility, the density of traps, the thickness of the absorber and the illumination intensity.
pool.authors: Ghazi Aman Nowsherwan, Muhammad Azhar, Miraj Ud Din, Hafsa Zafar, Mohsin Khan, Muhammad Rizwan Mahmood, Sadia Sadia, Muhammad Ahmad

pool.title: Low-Temperature Fabrication of Highly Transparent Zr-Doped In2O3 Thin Films by Pulsed Laser Deposition
pool.abstract: Undoped and Zr-incorporated In2O3 nanostructured thin films were fabricated by pulsed laser deposition under ambient-temperature conditions, followed by post-deposition annealing at 250 • C. In this study, the investigation of three different films has been conducted: pure In2O3 (F1), In2O3 doped with 2 at.% of Zr (F2) and In2O3 doped with 5 at.% of Zr (F3).The study of crystal structure using XRD technique confirms formation of bixbyite type of In2O3 with nanocrystalline structure and broadening of diffraction maxima.The calculations of average grain size give the following results: 10.3 nm (pure In2O3), 11.77 nm (2 at.%Zr) and 9.69 nm (5 at.%Zr).FESEM technique shows homogeneous surfaces, absence of cracks and well-developed nanostructure.Improvement in grain interconnections is achieved for 2 at.%Zr.As seen from optical analysis, both absorbance and the absorption coefficient reduce when the content of Zr increases.The increase of transmittance is observed in visible range of spectrum.Thus, AVT values are 44.7% and 61.0% for undoped film and 5 at.%Zr-doped film, respectively.Blue shifts in optical spectra are found in accordance with increasing of Zr concentration.Moreover, optical band gaps increase from 2.9 eV (undoped) to 3.0 eV (2 at.%Zr) and 3.1 eV (5 at.%Zr) according to Tauc plots.Qualitatively, these results can be explained by Burstein-Moss effect due to decreasing of defect states; however, electrical measurements are needed to confirm it.It can be estimated that average film thickness varies from about 200 to 230 nm.The 2 at.%Zr-doped film showed the best structural and morphological balance, whereas the 5 at.%Zr-doped film exhibited the highest optical transmittance.Overall, these results demonstrate the perspective of use of Zr-doped In2O3 thin films as transparent oxides and optoelectronic materials, which were prepared at relatively low temperatures; nevertheless, it needs further investigation of electrical properties.

pool.title: Structural Rigidity Enables Amplified Spontaneous Emission in 2D Alkylammonium Tin Perovskites
pool.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional tin perovskites are attracting increasing attention for coherent light emission, yet the impact of organic cations on their properties remains poorly understood. Here, we compare the Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) butylammonium tin iodide (BA2SnI4) and Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 1,4-diammoniobutane tin iodide (DABSnI4) perovskites to investigate the impact of the two structural types on their photophysical and optical gain properties. Combining X-ray diffraction and solid-state NMR spectroscopy, we reveal the different templating properties of the mono- and ditopic cations on the long-range structural order and local coordination environment, identifying an unreported phase transition for DABSnI4. The constrained molecular motions in the DJ perovskite provide an increased structural rigidity that also suppresses vibrational modes of the inorganic sublattice. The consequent lower exciton–phonon coupling and exciton binding energy, reduced defectivity, and modulation of the exciton recombination dynamics create favorable conditions to stabilize the population inversion and achieve amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) in DABSnI4, in net contrast with BA2SnI4 where ASE could not be obtained. This work highlights that Dion–Jacobson perovskites can create more rigid structural environments with positive feedback on the photophysical properties, providing a simple but effective design strategy for the synthesis of improved materials for optoelectronic applications.

pool.title: Grid-state deformation in a no-jump non-Hermitian bosonic dimer
pool.abstract: Abstract We study the no-jump evolution of ideal grid states in a lossy bosonic dimer with differential decay. The effective non-Hermitian quadratic dynamics induces a complex symplectic flow in phase space that deforms both the primitive lattice vectors and the origin seed. The average decay rate controls common-mode attenuation, while coherent hopping and differential decay control the reduced dimer deformation. For resonant modes, the reduced displacement flow is oscillatory in the elliptic regime, linear at the exceptional point, and exponentially separating in the hyperbolic regime. Although projected lattice areas can change, the deformation comes from a determinant-one complex symplectic flow on the complexified phase space. For a Gaussian regularization of the origin seed in the resonant dimer, we derive the associated complex width matrix and show that the seed remains square-integrable and Gaussian for every positive initial width, all non-negative times, and all physical loss rates. For an initial two-mode qunaught product state, the lossless limit recovers the standard beam-splitter generation of a square GKP+ Bell pair, while the no-jump dynamics produces its non-Hermitian deformation. The full no-jump probability for a normalized finite-energy input sets the postselection cost and depends on its excitation-number distribution and the reduced dimer dynamics.
pool.authors: B. M. Rodriguez-Lara, Hamed Ghaemi-Dizicheh, Shahram Dehdashti, Andreas Hanke, A. Touhami, J. Nötzel

pool.title: Topology-optimized dielectric cavities for enhanced excitonic light emission from WSe2
pool.abstract: Abstract Photonic inverse design and, especially, topology optimization, enable dielectric cavities with deeply sub-diffraction mode volumes and high quality factors, thus offering a powerful platform for enhanced light-matter coupling. Here, we design and fabricate arrays of CMOS-compatible silicon cavities on sapphire with extreme subwavelength transverse mode sizes of only 30–40 nm ( $${{\bf{V}}}{{\boldsymbol{\sim }}}{{{\boldsymbol{\lambda }}}}^{{{\boldsymbol{3}}}}/{{\boldsymbol{2500}}}$$ V ~ λ 3 / 2500 ). These cavities are engineered for deterministic coupling to a monolayer (or few-layer) excitonic material, producing strong near-field localization directly beneath the 2D material. Photoluminescence (PL) measurements show reproducible tenfold raw enhancement relative to bare silicon, which corresponds to a “per-area” normalized enhancement on the order of 10 3 , accounting for the small area of the deeply subwavelength mode volume, consistent with numerical simulations that account for material absorption and fabrication tolerances. Furthermore, time-resolved PL measurements reveal pronounced lifetime shortening and non-exponential dynamics, indicating cavity-mediated exciton-exciton interactions. The optimized cavity geometry enhances the far-field collection efficiency and supports scalable integration with van der Waals semiconductors. Our results show that the arrays of topology-optimized dielectric cavities are a versatile, scalable platform for controlling excitonic emission and interactions, which creates new opportunities in nonlinear optics, optoelectronics, and quantum photonics.
pool.authors: Owen M. Matthiessen, Brandon Triplett, Ömer Yeşilyurt, Davide Cassara, Karthik Pagadala, Morris M. Yang, Andres E. Llacsahuanga Allcca, Hamza Ather, Colton Fruhling, A. B. Solanki, Yong P. Chen, Hadiseh Alaeian, Alexander V. Kildishev, Vladimir M. Shalaev, Federico Capasso, Alexandra E. Boltasseva, Vahagn K. Mkhitaryan

pool.title: Scalable Postselection of Quantum Resources
pool.abstract: The large overhead imposed by quantum error correction is a critical challenge to the realization of quantum computers, and motivates searching for alternative error correcting codes and fault-tolerant circuit constructions. Postselection is a powerful tool that builds large programs out of probabilistically generated sub-circuits, and has been shown to increase the threshold of quantum error correction based on fusing fixed-size resource states or concatenated codes. In this work, we present an approach to lower the overhead of quantum computing using scalable postselection, based on directly postselecting sub-circuits with a size extensive in the code distance using decoder soft information. We introduce a metric, the partial gap, that estimates what the logical gap of a resource state will be after it is consumed, and show that postselection based on the partial gap leads to scalable improvements in the logical error rate. In the specific context of implementing logical gates via teleportation through a cluster state, we demonstrate that scalable postselection provides a $4\times$ reduction in the overhead per logical gate, at the same logical error probability.
pool.authors: J. Wilson Staples, Winston Fu, Jeff D. Thompson

pool.title: Multicarrier electrical and thermal magnetotransport in altermagnetic CrSb
pool.abstract: Chromium antimonide has emerged as a key material platform for studying altermagnetism because of its simple binary composition, high Néel temperature, and semimetallic electronic structure. Here, we investigate electrical and thermal magnetotransport in single-crystalline CrSb using steady- and pulsed-magnetic fields up to 65 T, and complement these measurements with neutron diffraction and magnetization data. We confirm the compensated magnetic structure and observe a large nonsaturating magnetoresistance together with a pronounced nonlinear Hall response at low temperatures. Multicarrier modeling, supported by mobility-spectrum analysis, reveals coexisting electron- and holelike charge carriers with mobilities up to ∼ 3000 cm 2 / Vs and shows that the number of transport channels that can be resolved strongly depends on the accessible magnetic-field range. Thermal-transport measurements further reveal a nonlinear thermal Hall response and a thermal conductivity substantially exceeding a simple Wiedemann-Franz law. The broadly similar field and temperature evolution of electrical and thermal transport point to a dominant electronic contribution, while the remaining deviations indicate additional heat-carrying channels.

Uhlarz, Sven Luther, Tommy Kotte, Michał Baj, Marein C. Rahn, Th.
