pool.title: Ultrastrong-coupling signatures in photon statistics from terahertz Higgs polaritons
pool.abstract: The ultrastrong coupling regime of cavity photons and quantum materials has emerged as a pathway to modify materials properties, however definitive signatures of ultrastrong coupling remain elusive. Focusing on the quantum photon statistics of light transmitted through a cavity-embedded superconductor, we show that a two-photon Higgs polariton at strong coupling realizes a photonic nonlinearity at the single terahertz photon level. We find that as light-matter coupling increases, the photon statistics show pronounced changes due to the formation of a hybrid photon-matter dark-cavity state with finite photon occupancy, producing testable signatures of ultrastrong coupling. We derive a non-Markovian input output relation and study the cavity-embedded superconductor 2H-NbSe2 as it approaches ultrastrong light-matter coupling. Our results reveal a diagnostic for ultrastrong coupling in the two-photon coincidence statistics that is absent in total counts.
pool.authors: Spenser Talkington, Benjamin Kass, Martin Claassen

pool.title: Electrical-circuit simulation of the Uhlmann phase
pool.abstract: The Uhlmann phase extends the concept of geometric phases to mixed quantum states through a parallel-transport condition on purification amplitudes, but its experimental realization has so far required sophisticated quantum platforms with carefully engineered auxiliary degrees of freedom. In this work, we reformulate the Uhlmann parallel-transport condition as a linear matrix differential equation and vectorize it to obtain an effective dynamical generator. This generator can be directly mapped onto the admittance matrix of a classical RC circuit, thereby translating the Uhlmann dynamics into the evolution of circuit node voltages. We illustrate the mapping using the equatorial-loop model and, via a rotating-frame transformation followed by a real decomposition, derive a time-independent, real-valued dynamical system suitable for analog implementation. LTspice simulations of the resulting active RC network faithfully reproduce the Uhlmann geometric phase and its topological transition at the critical purity, demonstrating that classical electrical circuits offer a simple and accessible platform for probing mixed-state geometric phases.
pool.authors: Y Huang, Yu Wang, Jia-Chen Tang, Xu-Yang Hou, Hao Guo

pool.title: Nonlinear circular dichroism reveals the local Berry curvature
pool.abstract: Abstract The transfer of angular momentum between light and crystalline solids during nonlinear optical processes is typically interpreted in terms of angular momentum conservation and the rotational symmetry of the crystal lattice. However, these cornerstone principles rely on macroscopic symmetry arguments, providing little insight into the microscopic origin of angular momentum transfer. Here we show that changes in the spin angular momentum of light in high-harmonic generation processes, which we probe via nonlinear circular dichroism, are directly proportional to the local Berry curvature at a single optical resonance, therefore establishing a link between nonlinear light–matter interactions and the quantum geometry of electronic states. We demonstrate this relationship using second-harmonic generation in monolayer WSe 2 , using circularly polarized light to break time-reversal symmetry and lift the degeneracy between the valleys. The resulting second-harmonic circular dichroism can be controlled through the intensity and helicity of the circularly polarized light, hence offering a method for the control and readout of the optically probed Berry curvature.
pool.authors: Nele Tornow, Paul Herrmann, Clemens Schneider, Ferdinand Evers, Jan Wilhelm, Giancarlo Soavi

pool.title: Network-on-Chip Technology for Chiplet Integration Architecture
pool.abstract: In today's era, the marginal benefits of transistor scaling are continuously decreasing, and Chiplet heterogeneous integration has become the mainstream path for scaling AI chip computing power. Meanwhile, on-chip interconnect performance is increasingly becoming the key factor limiting system computing power and energy efficiency. This paper focuses on on-chip network technology for Chiplet-integrated AI chip architectures, providing a systematic review and analysis of its technical principles, research status, existing limitations, and development directions. The study first breaks down the on-chip network's dual-layer architecture of 'physical architecture layer - protocol mechanism layer,' clarifying the functional roles of each core hardware unit and protocol mechanism and the complete data transmission logic. Next, from the perspectives of topology, routing algorithms, switching mechanisms, and flow control mechanisms, it summarizes the evolution of on-chip network technology and the customized research results for AI computing features and Chiplet heterogeneous scenarios. It then identifies two core current issues—inter-chiplet interconnect performance bottlenecks and lack of cross-layer collaborative design, as well as insufficient dynamic load adaptation and lagging industry standards — and outlines the key paths for future technology optimization. This research can provide clear insights into the technological development path for researchers in the field and offer theoretical support and direction for the interconnect architecture design and industrial implementation of the next-generation highly integrated AI chips.
pool.authors: Tianmiao Zhang

pool.title: WTe2 Weyl semimetal conical microarray enabled quantum-enhanced terahertz photocurrent sensing for organophosphorus toxin detection in simulated body fluid
pool.abstract: As a representative topological quantum system, type-II Weyl semimetals break the fundamental bandgap limitation of conventional semiconductor photodetectors and deliver giant intrinsic nonlinear optical response originating from topologically protected Weyl points and Fermi arc surface states, providing a disruptive material platform for advanced room-temperature terahertz (THz) optoelectronics. Building on this quantum material advantage, we develop a room-temperature THz sensor based on a periodic WTe 2 conical microarray for quantitative detection of the organophosphorus neurotoxin chlorpyrifos in simulated body fluid (SBF). Each microcone measures 80 µm in base diameter and 60 µm in height, arranged with a 100 µm center-to-center pitch on a Si/SiO 2 substrate with Au/Ti electrodes. A 140 GHz continuous-wave THz source illuminates the chip from above, and the photocurrent is read out by a Keithley 2400 digital source meter via two tungsten-carbide microprobes. Leveraging the geometric near-field concentration effect at the cone tips, the proposed architecture synergistically enhances the second-order nonlinear photocurrent rectification originating from the Weyl-point band structure of WTe 2 , as confirmed by CST electromagnetic simulation. The underlying sensing mechanism relies on chlorpyrifos-induced dielectric screening and interfacial charge transfer at the WTe 2 surface, which modulate the THz-to-DC rectification efficiency. Current responsivity (Ra) and noise-equivalent power (NEP) are extracted from illuminated and dark current–voltage (I–V) characteristics as a function of chlorpyrifos concentration over a bias range of 7.0–8.0 V. The sensor achieves a limit of detection (LOD) of 12 ng/mL across a dynamic range of 0.05–100 µg/mL in 0.7% saline SBF, with a logarithmic calibration fit of R 2 = 0.991. Compared with conventional semiconductor and thermal THz detectors, the topological-quantum-material device realizes room-temperature high-sensitivity detection without relying on interband transition or cryogenic cooling, demonstrating fundamentally superior performance stability and broadband adaptability. This work demonstrates that microstructured Weyl semimetal heterostructures enable quantum-enhanced THz biochemical sensing, providing a new device architecture for label-free, reagent-free toxin detection in complex aqueous environments.
pool.authors: Xu Zhang, Mingxin Li, Chunting Wu

pool.title: Connectivity‐Dependent Mechanics of Main‐Chain Oligomers in Side‐Chain Liquid‐Crystalline Polyacrylate Networks
pool.abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid‐crystalline elastomers (LCEs) combine orientational order with polymer‐network elasticity, yet the influence of molecular connectivity on their mechanics across different timescales remains poorly understood. Side‐chain polyacrylate LCEs containing main‐chain liquid‐crystalline oligomers with different end connectivity are investigated: network‐bound diacrylate‐terminated DA‐LCO and non‐network‐bound end‐capped LCO. Both oligomers lower the glass‐transition temperature while preserving nematic order, but their connectivity produces distinct mechanical responses. DA‐LCO maintains a higher rubbery modulus, whereas LCO produces softer, more extensible networks. Both systems exhibit similar strain‐rate dependences at short and intermediate deformation times, indicating that physically confined LCO remains mechanically engaged. At longer times, LCO exhibits an additional terminal relaxation associated with progressive release of physical constraints; no corresponding process is observed in DA‐LCO before fracture. At moderate temperatures, LCO and the PEG‐crosslinked reference network show comparable Arrhenius dependences with apparent activation energies around , while LCO terminal relaxation shifts to shorter times at elevated temperatures. Molecular connectivity therefore acts as a timescale‐dependent design parameter: non‐network‐bound oligomers can provide short‐time mechanical support while enabling additional long‐time stress dissipation. Oligomer end connectivity thus offers a molecular strategy for tuning mechanics and relaxation in nematic polymer networks.
pool.authors: Choi Subi, Zhijun Yang, Eugene Michael Terentjev

pool.title: Fixed-qubit CVaR-VQE and quantum-inspired QUBO sampling for static and dynamic restricted vertex multicut in telecom resilience
pool.abstract: A central question in hybrid quantum–classical optimization is how to assign the classical and quantum components according to the structure of the problem, rather than attempting to transfer the full optimization model to a quantum device. We investigate this question on static and finite-horizon dynamic restricted vertex minimum multicut, an NP-hard network-isolation problem with exponentially many path constraints. A classical row-generation layer handles graph separation, feasibility verification, and constraint generation, while quantum or quantum-inspired samplers are used only for the current restricted optimization problem. We develop two such algorithms: an exact-slack QUBO formulation sampled by simulated annealing, and a fixed-register CVaR-VQE formulation in which generated constraints modify a classical loss without enlarging the static quantum register. Exact MILP row generation provides the certifying reference. Experiments on SNDlib-derived telecom instances show that both approaches can be integrated consistently within this workflow, while classical-sampler controls do not establish a quantum-specific performance advantage. The dynamic study further shows how temporal coupling creates a distinct resource bottleneck, motivating decomposed formulations for larger horizons.
pool.authors: Ali Abbassi, Yann Dujardin, Éric Gourdin, Philippe Lacomme, Caroline Prodhon

pool.title: Broadband and Athermal Infrared Engineering: A Minimalist Meta‐Composite Optical Architecture for a 100°C Temperature Span
pool.abstract: ABSTRACT Hybrid meta‐refractive systems offer a viable pathway to overcome the multi‐dimensional performance trade‐offs of metalenses. However, conventional spatial‐stacking designs struggle to simultaneously achieve minimalism and athermalization. Here, a minimalist meta‐composite optical architecture is proposed based on a full‐field inverse‐design method. By integrating two‐dimensional subwavelength meta‐atoms onto micro‐curved surfaces, this approach precisely regulates the thermal phase response, achieving significant suppression of both thermal and high‐order aberrations. Based on this, we further demonstrate a meta‐composite optical system (MCOS) comprising only two elements, achieving a focal shift of merely ±6.7 µm across the 8–12 µm bandwidth and a 100°C temperature span (from −40°C to 60°C). Meanwhile, the MCOS exhibits a superior modulation transfer function (MTF) and excellent imaging resolution under various temperature conditions. In addition, the athermalization mechanism and the tolerances of non‐ideal structural profiles for meta‐atoms are rigorously derived and analyzed, effectively mitigating temperature‐induced degradation of image quality. By integrating with an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platform, the excellent infrared thermal imaging demonstration of the MCOS has been experimentally confirmed. This work offers a feasible pathway for the development of integrated optics and the deployment of minimalist optical systems.
pool.authors: Ningrui Xiao, He Lin, Yuyao Wang, Yingchi Lin, Jin Qiu, Liucen Wang, Cheng Hui Huang, Xiaoliang Ma, Xiangang Luo

pool.title: Chip-mediated manipulation of photonic quantum skyrmions
pool.abstract: Quantum skyrmions are attracting much interest owing to their topological robustness, which offers a route to address noise and loss in quantum systems. The toolkit for their creation has advanced recently, enabling quantum skyrmions to be generated in bulk systems as entangled states and on chip as single-photon states. However, methods for generating on-chip entangled skyrmions, as well as for their reconfigurable manipulation and controlled interfacing with single-photon skyrmions, remain elusive. Here we demonstrate entangled skyrmions and their manipulation on chip with an integrated silicon nitride nanophotonic platform. The skyrmion topology is coherently encoded in a local single-photon spin-textured quantum state, which is subsequently transferred into a non-local skyrmion topology shared between two entangled photons. Throughout the transfer process, the topology remains preserved under background noise and different types of disturbance, even after the entanglement vanishes. This establishes a quantum-topology-enabled transfer scheme beyond entanglement, which reveals a fundamentally enhanced resilience that outperforms conventional entanglement-assisted quantum state transfer. This approach serves as a step towards building robust quantum interconnects and advancing distributed quantum information technology mediated by topology. Although photonic quantum skyrmions can be generated as entangled or single-photon states, a means to switch between the two is required for quantum information processing. Now, entangled skyrmions and their manipulation on chip is realized.
pool.authors: Haoqi Zhao, Yichi Zhang, Isaac M. Nape, Shuang Wu, Yaoyang Ji, Chenjie Zhang, Yijie Shen, Andrew Forbes, Liang Feng

pool.title: Exceptional-point-like Sensing near Hermitian Transmission Peak Degeneracies
pool.abstract: Abstract Non-Hermitian sensing near exceptional points (EPs), can exhibit a sublinear response to perturbations and thus promises sensitivity beyond conventional Hermitian sensors operating at diabolic points (DPs). Recent studies have further shown that the square-root readout can be attained near transmission peak degeneracy (TPD), where the splitting of spectral extrema rather than the eigenvalues is observed. However, in non-Hermitian platforms, the available sensitivity enhancement is fundamentally constrained by the divergent Petermann factor because of non-Hermitian eigenvector degeneracy, and practically by the system complexity. Here, we experimentally demonstrate TPD-enhanced sensing of refractive-index change in a simple chiral Hermitian cavity. We show that the Hermitian transmission spectrum can also exhibit TPD-induced square-root splitting of spectral extrema while preserving eigenvector orthogonality. As a result, this Hermitian TPD-based sensor retains the response enhancement characteristic of non-Hermitian TPD sensing, yet remains free from the Petermann-factor limit intrinsic to non-Hermitian systems, thereby enabling enhanced sensitivity. This work establishes a Hermitian route toward ultrasensitive sensing that surpasses the conventional DP sensor and provides a sensitivity advantage over non-Hermitian implementations when Petermann-factor-amplified noise is relevant.
pool.authors: Jiangshan Tang, Li Xiao, Haodong Wu, Yuwei Jing, Han Zhang, Yaping Ruan, 刘伍明, Yanqing Lu, Keyu Xia

pool.title: Non-reciprocity preserved non-diffracting propagation of truncated Airy beams in a Hatano--Nelson system
pool.authors: Anli Xiang, Yangjian Cai, Gaofeng Wu

pool.title: Tunable magnetism with emerging quantum phenomena in two-dimensional magnets
pool.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) magnets with atomically thin nature provide an ideal material platform for exploring 2D magnetism, whose physical paradigm is fundamental in science. Their tunable magnetic order in the 2D limit, interplaying with strong fluctuation, correlation, and topology, further brings enormous opportunities to explore exotic quantum phenomena and associated device applications that were previously out of reach. Here, we give a perspective on tuning 2D magnetism with emerging quantum phenomena in 2D magnets. After a summary to the material landscape and probing methodologies of 2D magnetism, we highlight its multidimensional tuning in 2D magnets, via knobs ranging from layer number, light, electrical field, to twist engineering, and so on. We further present how such control can be harnessed for engineering various exotic quantum phenomena, with emphasis on electron tunneling, quantum-geometry-related transport, and spin-exciton interactions. An outlook on challenges and opportunities of 2D magnets is also given to unlock their unprecedented possibilities for both fundamental science and applied technologies.
pool.authors: Chao Zhong, Lifu Zhang

pool.title: Quantum-Enabled Identification of Microbial Subcommunities Associated with Stability and VFA Selectivity in Anaerobic Fermentation
pool.abstract: Abstract Mixed-cultured anaerobic fermentation (AF) is increasingly deployed for resource recovery from waste streams, yet process instability and unpredictable volatile fatty acid (VFA) selectivity limit performance. To identify the influential microbes or multimicrobe relationships affecting AF performance, we use a photonic quantum computing algorithm to identify microbial cliques (e.g., strict subcommunities of co-occurring taxa) from two pilot-scale AF reactors, which differed in the organic loading rate (OLR), stability, and VFA profiles. A greater yield of VFA was recovered from the low-OLR reactor compared to the high-OLR reactor (74.11 g VFA kg–1 total solids (TS) in 33 days compared to 24.85 g VFA kg–1 TS in 37 days, respectively). Using 16S rRNA sequencing data, we constructed Jaccard similarity graphs for photonic quantum computing analysis, which revealed clear differences in community organization and functional capabilities. The high-OLR reactor was characterized by highly overlapping acidogenic cliques, whereas the low-OLR reactor contained fragmented cliques of acidogenic taxa alongside low-abundant methanogenic (Methanosarcina) and syntrophic (Syntrophomonas) microbes. The potential effect of these metabolisms in AF warrants further experimental investigation. This work introduces a quantum-assisted probabilistic clique prioritization model to improve exploratory microbial network analysis as a tool for designing engineering interventions in AF.
pool.authors: Lily Lee, Lucy Oram, Rhys Jon Jones, Yu Shang, Rodrigo Fernández Feito, Jaime Massanet‐Nicolau, Alan J. Guwy, Po-Heng Henry Lee

pool.title: Homochiral Evolution from Self-Assembly of Chiral Block Copolymers
pool.abstract: Abstract A block copolymer containing a chiral block is referred to as a chiral block copolymer, which can form a helical phase (H*) in diblock copolymers and an alternating gyroid phase (GA) in triblock terpolymers with controlled chirality from self-assembly, as evidenced by electron tomography. Polylactide-containing chiral block copolymers can be used as a representative system for the investigation of homochiral evolution from molecular chirality examined by electronic circular dichroism (ECD) to conformational chirality examined by C═O vibrational circular dichroism (VCD), and finally to phase chirality characterized by electron tomography, with C–O–C VCD providing insight into interchain chiral interactions. The intra- and interchain contributions should be evaluated in the context of the specific molecular structure and sample conditions. By taking advantage of noncovalent chirality induction, it is feasible to introduce a chiral bias by associating a chiral dopant with an achiral block, giving H* with controlled chirality from an achiral block copolymer. This Viewpoint highlights the fundamental principles, providing perspectives on the design of chiral soft materials for device applications.
pool.authors: Sheng‐Wei Shao, Rong‐Ming Ho

pool.title: Anomalous Deterministic Localization Driven by Staggered Disorder
pool.abstract: ABSTRACT Disorder scattering occurs broadly in wave‐matter systems, offering vast potential for applications ranging from random lasing to quantum information processing. However, achieving customized control over wave transport and localization in disordered systems remains a significant challenge. Notably, wave transport in the weak scattering regime typically exhibits energy‐dilute diffusion, while in the strong scattering regime, Anderson localization is inherently stochastic and unpredictable in location. Here we report an anomalous phase termed staggered‐disorder induced localization (SDIL) in disordered structure, which achieves robust and deterministic localization in disordered systems. Specifically, the SDIL halts wave expansion along a predefined direction while facilitating orthogonal transport within a 2D structure. The SDIL is found persisting across a wide range of disorder strengths for a finite 2D structure. Remarkably, the transport trajectory is fully configurable by engineering the staggered disorder, providing an attractive mechanism for wave routing in disordered systems. Our quasi‐normal mode analysis reveals a localized phase region, wherein emergent high‐quality modes drive this robust localized scattering. These findings establish SDIL as a missing paradigm in scattering physics, providing a universal framework for achieving deterministic wave localization and routing within disordered systems.
pool.authors: Peilong Hong, Yu Wang, Fuhao Ji, Mingfang Yi, Liwei Zhang, Peng Cheng, Wangping Cheng, Yi Liang, Guoquan Zhang

pool.title: Angular‐Multiplexed Photoluminescence Meta‐Display via Unidirectional Emission Control
pool.abstract: ABSTRACT Metasurfaces have revolutionized the optical field due to their exceptional wavefront shaping capabilities, boosting the multi‐dimensional light‐field manipulation and emission control. However, the incoherent, omnidirectional, unpolarized, and phase‐random nature of fluorescence emission limits the applicability of conventional metasurface multiplexing strategies, posing significant challenges for photoluminescence (PL) encoding and multi‐dimensional light‐emitting metasurface (LEM)‐based display technology. Here, the PL angular‐multiplexing is proposed and experimentally demonstrated based on unidirectional emission control for multi‐dimensional meta‐display. By exploiting the inherent numerical aperture limitation of the detection system and coupling PL into the guided mode via an on‐chip metasurface, the LEM‐empowered precise emission angle control is transferred into the angular‐multiplexed intensity encoding degree of freedom, enabling a dual‐channel PL meta‐display. Furthermore, by incorporating directional multiplexing, the multi‐dimensional LEM achieves four independent PL images corresponding to distinct observation angles and illumination directions. This PL angular‐multiplexing approach, together with the multi‐dimensional meta‐display architecture, significantly expands the multiplexing encoding capability of fluorescence light‐field manipulation, offering promising opportunities for diverse applications, including next‐generation optical display/encryption techniques, biological sensing, and incoherent illumination engineering.
pool.authors: Zejing Wang, Qing Huang, Xinglong Li, Yangyang Shi, Cuiting Wang, Zhongyang Li, Shuai Wan

pool.title: Photonic Klein Tunnelling in Silicon Topological Materials for Terahertz 6G Interconnects.
pool.abstract: Topological photonics enables robust light transport along engineered interfaces, but transport across a potential barrier placed within such an interface, and the range of barrier strengths over which it survives, remain largely unexplored. Here we experimentally demonstrate photonic Klein tunnelling in a Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) compatible silicon valley photonic crystal at terahertz frequencies. A local, inversion-symmetric barrier is introduced into a valley kink channel, with its strength Δ controlled through the geometry of the triangular holes. The barrier strength is calibrated using the local Dirac-frequency shift, establishing a direct relation between photonic crystal geometry and the effective tight-binding potential. We find that transmission remains close to its barrier-free value for Δ below the nearest-neighbour hopping amplitude t, and is strongly suppressed as Δ approaches t. Momentum-space analysis shows valley pseudospin preserved to better than 98% across two cascaded barriers. We further demonstrate Klein-tunnelling transport through multibarrier, Ω-shaped and power-splitter devices, supporting terahertz data transmission at rates up to 100 Gbit s- 1. Our findings underpin a new design framework for resilient and high-capacity terahertz photonic integrated circuits.
pool.authors: Mulla S, Sadhu SK, M AI, Lal S, Kumar A, Vidhyadhiraja NS, Gu Z, Pitchappa P, Szriftgiser P, Ducournau G, Kumar A

pool.title: Self-Assembly of a Colloidal Honeycomb Crystal in Silico for Topological Valley Photonics.
pool.abstract: The quest to employ colloidal self-assembly as a scalable means of fabricating photonic crystals with a complete photonic band gap at optical frequencies has proved challenging throughout the first quarter of the 21st century. Meanwhile, the field of topological photonics has emerged, presenting new, and largely unexploited, functionalities for self-assembled colloidal materials. The robustness of topological photonic properties to defects that are practically unavoidable in self-assembled colloidal structures appears to be especially attractive. Here, the self-assembly of a colloidal honeycomb crystal is demonstrated in computer simulations, with an assembly strategy that not only suppresses the formation of real-space topological defects observed in experiments but also results in topological photonic properties in reciprocal space. This assembly strategy promotes the emergence of long-range order and allows for the breaking of spatial inversion symmetry with two distinct sub-lattices. A sufficient dielectric contrast between the colloidal particles sitting on these two sub-lattices is exploited to realize a valley-Hall topological photonic phase, allowing for unidirectional propagation of circularly polarized light through waveguides composed of the designer crystals. The design rules are tested for their robustness to open the door to scalable fabrication of topological photonic devices via colloidal self-assembly.
pool.authors: Walker A, Neophytou A, Swinkels PJM, Demetriadou A, Schall P, Chakrabarti D

pool.title: Parity-Dependent THz Harmonic Generation in Electrically Pumped Micro-Lasers Exploiting Topological Insulator-Metamaterial Gratings.
pool.abstract: The intersection of topological photonics and nonlinear optics provides new opportunities for compact, tunable light sources. Here, we demonstrate even and odd harmonic generation, in the 6-10 THz range, in electrically driven micro-lasers by integrating a set of different topological insulator (TI)-metamaterials. The unique surface states of TI, characterized by robust symmetry properties, enable enhanced nonlinear interactions when coupled with the tailored dispersion and field confinement of metamaterials. By leveraging the nonlinear susceptibilities of the composite structure by electrical gating, we demonstrate controlled generation of second- or third-harmonic signals of up to 33 µW or 6.4 µW power, respectively, dominated either by the topological surface states or by the bulk. Moreover, by selectively pumping resonant infrared (IR) phonons with the intracavity-generated THz pulses, we induce dynamic lattice distortions that modulate the electronic band structure and further enhance the nonlinear optical susceptibilities. The interplay between phonon-driven lattice anharmonicities and the topologically protected surface states, leads to a pronounced enhancement in nonlinear THz response, offering new mechanisms for nonperturbative light-matter interactions in quantum materials. Our findings establish a novel versatile framework for compact, tunable sources of coherent radiation across multiple frequency bands, so far inaccessible in a solid-state laser, and pave the way for applications in integrated photonics, on-chip frequency conversion, and quantum information processing.
pool.authors: Di Gaspare A, Knox CS, Yagmur A, Ghayeb Zamharir S, Li L, Sasaki S, Davies AG, Linfield EH, Freeman JR, Vitiello MS

pool.title: Highly pure electric-field skyrmions from a zonally modulated metasurface.
pool.abstract: Optical skyrmions are widely investigated in topological photonics, yet generating their vector textures in three dimensions purely within the electric field remains a challenge. Here, we show that a single-layer dielectric metasurface can overcome this constraint through a zonal modulation strategy to decouple focal field control. By using a low numerical aperture (NA) inner core largely governing the transverse field and a high-NA outer ring mainly contributing to the longitudinal field, highly pure Néel-type and Bloch-type electric field skyrmions are successfully generated. This zonal design strategy clarifies how tightly focused vector fields can be decomposed into separate transverse-texture and longitudinal-polarity functions, providing a compact route for generating electric-field skyrmions with flat optics.
pool.authors: Xiao L, Liu P, Wang Y, Zhang Q, Yang Y

pool.title: Multiband topological heterojunctions on the surface nanoscale axial photonics platform.
pool.abstract: Analogue Hamiltonian simulation (AHS) in photonic systems can be an enticing alternative to direct experimental study of complex Hamiltonian systems, leading to the emergence of the field of topological photonics. In this work, we leverage the ultra-low loss operation and sub-angstrom fabrication precision of the Surface Nanoscale Axial Photonics Platform to experimentally demonstrate the first topologically nontrivial SNAP devices by coupling adjacent SNAP microresonators to form Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) lattices. Each axial mode of the microresonator array manifests distinct topological band structures, enabling us to observe behavior close to and far from the topological-trivial phase transition. We further expand the scope of topological SNAP systems to junctions between higher-order, multiband lattices with dissimilar topological phases created by coupling up to 21 well-matched SNAP microresonators. Analyzing these previously unexplored "heterojunctions" necessitated our development of generalized topological polarization methods. We thus demonstrate the exceptional promise of the SNAP platform for AHS of topological insulators.
pool.authors: Fried N, Vitullo DLP, Dutt A

pool.title: Programmable Topological Light via Coherent Beam Combination.
pool.abstract: Topologically structured optical fields exhibit rich physical properties and offer new opportunities for information encoding and light-matter interaction. In this work, we propose a general and scalable framework for generating and reconfiguring topological light using coherent beam combination (CBC). By treating the CBC system as an electronically addressable optical phased array, we demonstrate that the topology of the optical field becomes a programmable parameter. As a representative example, we focus on optical skyrmions and present an experimental demonstration of deterministic and dynamic switching between Bloch-type, Néel-type, and antiskyrmion textures using a 7-channel Yb-doped fiber master oscillator power amplifier CBC system. This approach establishes a scalable and programmable route toward high-power topological vector fields and reconfigurable structured light.
pool.authors: Chernikov F, Kerridge-Johns W, Bobkov KK, Nilsson J, Zervas MN, Mills B

pool.title: Ideal magnetic quadrupole radiators.
pool.abstract: High-purity magnetic quadrupole (MQ) radiation is fundamentally limited by ultralow radiative transition rates and severe mode mixing. Here, we propose a synergistic strategy combining parity-selective mode filtering and anapole engineering to realize ideal MQ radiation. Our design achieves an MQ mode-purity-factor (MPF) exceeding 99.5% under both far-field plane-wave and near-field dipole excitations. Critically, this mechanism enables the direct, contamination-free conversion of fundamental electric dipole (ED) emission into pure MQ radiation. This work establishes a robust paradigm for deterministic high-order magnetic multipole manipulation, with immediate applications in quantum light sources and topological photonics.

pool.title: Sweet artificial intelligence as digital catalysts in infectious diseases: Glycomics and glycoanalysis.
pool.abstract: Glycans mediate microbial adhesion, host-cell entry, immune recognition and immune evasion, but their branching topology, linkage isomerism and context-dependent functions make glycan-centered infectious-disease research difficult to standardize. This review summarizes how artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) are being applied to glycomics and glycoanalysis in infection biology. We first outline major sample sources, analytical platforms and curated databases used to generate glycan data, including mass spectrometry (MS), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), chromatography and glycan/lectin microarrays. We then compare supervised learning, unsupervised learning, graph neural networks(GNNs), sequence models and transformer-informed frameworks for glycan structure analysis, lectin-glycan binding prediction, pathogenicity assessment and biomarker discovery. Representative validated models, including SweetNet and LectinOracle, demonstrate that glycan-aware AI can achieve reproducible predictive performance across independent datasets. Finally, we discuss diagnostic applications, virulence forecasting, vaccine and drug development, and pathogen-related autoimmunity. Current limitations include sparse annotations, batch effects, incomplete structural coverage and limited model interpretability. Standardized datasets and interpretable multi-omics models will be essential for translating AI-driven glycoanalysis into pathogen surveillance and precision immunotherapy. In conclusion, this review summarizes how artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) are being applied to glycomics and glycoanalysis in infection biology.

pool.title: Topology-aware dynamic co-evolution for robust graph learning.
pool.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved remarkable success in learning from graph-structured data. However, recent studies have revealed their vulnerability to adversarial attacks, where imperceptible perturbations to the graph structure can easily mislead predictions. Existing defense methods predominantly rely on global heuristic strategies, which often lead to over-smoothing in deep architectures and fail to capture localized, fine-grained structural anomalies. In this paper, we propose Topology-Aware Dynamic Co-evolution (TADC), a novel framework that reformulates graph defense as a closed-loop optimization process. Unlike static purification paradigms, TADC introduces a closed-loop dynamic co-evolution framework, in which graph topology and model parameters are jointly optimized through validation-guided meta-gradients, enabling continuous and adaptive structural refinement during training. To further ensure the reliability of topology updates, we identify the topology-agnostic limitation of conventional meta-gradients and propose a topology-aware gradient calibration mechanism, which incorporates structural priors to guide gradient directions toward more plausible and semantically consistent graph modifications. Concretely, TADC first localizes vulnerable nodes via a structural-semantic consistency probe and constructs an initialized graph through topology-aware refinement. It then performs structure decoupling to disentangle reliable and potentially adversarial edges into distinct channels. Building upon this decomposition, a fully differentiable attention-based architecture DeepGCN enables end-to-end optimization of the co-evolution process. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that TADC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various attack settings, with particularly pronounced advantages under strong adversarial perturbations and high perturbation rates. Our code is available at https://github.com/robustgcn/TADC.

pool.title: PolyFKAN: Integrating Fourier-KAN layers into graph neural networks for polymer property prediction.
pool.abstract: Graph neural networks have become a central tool for polymer property prediction, but their fixed activation functions can impose a low-pass spectral bias that smooths over the sharp, multi-scale structure-property variations that distinguish chemically similar polymers. We address this limitation with PolyFKAN, a multitask graph-learning architecture that augments the prediction head of a polyGNN backbone with Fourier Kolmogorov-Arnold network layers. PolyFKAN represents edge-wise activations as truncated Fourier series and couples the resulting spectral branch to the standard multilayer perceptron (MLP) pathway through a bounded residual gate, thereby increasing functional expressivity without disrupting the learned graph embeddings. Across 17 polymer properties spanning electronic, thermodynamic, optical/dielectric, thermal, and gas-permeability domains, PolyFKAN achieves statistically significant improvement over a tightly controlled polyGNN baseline on 11 of 17 targets (one-sided t-test, p < 0.05), with one additional target showing marginal improvement. The gains are especially pronounced for multi-scale properties, including more than 15% average root mean squared error reduction for large-penetrant gas permeabilities and more than 15% improvement across optical and dielectric targets. Hierarchical ablation further reveals that optimal Fourier bandwidth is property-dependent: difficult, multi-scale targets require broader spectral capacity with stronger amplitude control, whereas high-fidelity targets benefit from lighter regularization. These results establish Fourier-KAN prediction heads as a minimally invasive and physically aligned inductive bias for polymer informatics.
pool.authors: Li B, Liu J, Yu Q, Yang Z, Zhan Y

pool.title: A cascaded probabilistic framework for stealth-aware MITRE ATT&CK path prediction in active directory adversary emulation
pool.abstract: Abstract Proactive adversary emulation requires anticipating multi-step attack trajectories, yet existing approaches rely on static attack graphs or single-signal models that cannot jointly satisfy coherence, tactical realism, and evasiveness. We propose a cascaded probabilistic framework for MITRE ATT&CK technique-path prediction in Active Directory environments, where exhaustive enumeration is intractable. Its contribution is a three-stage architecture that decouples these objectives instead of blending them. Stage 1, a two-layer unidirectional LSTM trained on observed threat-actor chains, emits a five-candidate pool rather than one technique. Stage 2, an empirical Markov tactic-transition gate, admits only attested transitions, including self-loops and backward moves a strict linear kill chain excludes. Stage 3 re-ranks survivors against a detection-rule corpus, favoring evasive over merely probable techniques. Candidates are masked at inference to Windows-applicable techniques, so outputs are technique chains, not instantiated paths. Under a prefix-disjoint protocol in which no evaluation context occurs in training, the true continuation is retained in the five-candidate pool more often than by a first-order predictor or an exact prefix-lookup table on identical pairs. Because Stage 3 both selects on and is scored by detection-rule density, the chains are re-scored against independently maintained corpora the selector never accesses; the exposure reduction persists there, and it is that transferred result that carries the evasiveness claim. Novel here is that structural admissibility is a hard constraint rather than a soft weight, so tactical realism cannot be traded away for likelihood or stealth. A case study initiated from a single initial-access technique further indicates that all tactic transitions within the returned path portfolio have attested support in the corpus transition matrix, and that no predicted step violates the ATT&CK-declared phase set of its technique.

pool.title: Enerzyme: An Efficient Reactive Neural Network Potential Training Framework for Enzyme Cluster Models with Application to Methyltransferases
pool.abstract: Abstract Quantum mechanical (QM) cluster models provide an effective framework for mechanistic studies of enzymatic reactions but QM calculations remain computationally demanding. Neural network potentials (NNPs) offer a promising route to reduce their cost, but enzymes introduce new challenges not faced by NNPs for small molecules, including large system sizes, the need for inclusion of solvent environments, substantial polarization, and charge transfer. Here, we demonstrate an integrated software framework for efficient training of NNPs for mechanistic study of enzymes, with demonstrations on QM-cluster models of S-adenosyl-l-methionine-dependent methyltransferases (MTases). Our Enerzyme code introduces modular, electrostatics-aware NNP architectures and combines automated QM-cluster construction with reactive dataset generation. The Enerzymette subpackage also automates reaction pathway exploration at both NNP and DFT levels of theory. We show that iterative flexible scans and nudged elastic band calculations impose stricter requirements on NNPs than conventionally employed dataset metrics. Nevertheless, we develop an approach to train NNPs on fewer than 1,000 system-specific data points to reproduce reaction energetics and transition-state structures on MTase clusters containing up to 545 atoms, approaching chemical accuracy with respect to the reference. We show that direct supervision of atomic charges and alignment of dielectric screening with QM-cluster calculations substantially improve simulation stability and accuracy and that multitask-learned atomic charges predict correct charge transfer and polarization trends and provide chemically meaningful descriptors of reactivity. Furthermore, we demonstrate transferability across chemically diverse catechol O-methyltransferase substrates, indicating NNPs learn generalizable reactivity patterns as training data is expanded across multiple enzymes. Together, these results establish a foundation for accelerating enzyme mechanistic studies and provide insights for future NNP development for biomolecular reactivity.
pool.authors: Weiliang Luo, Heather J. Kulik

pool.title: scDGCN: A Graph-Based Deep Clustering Framework for Single-Cell Transcriptomics via Neighborhood-Enhanced Context Representation Learning.
pool.abstract: Self-supervised and context-aware representation learning offers a powerful strategy for extracting robust features from high-dimensional, sparse, and noisy single-cell data. Here, we present scDGCN, a graph-based deep clustering framework for single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis. scDGCN models intercellular similarity as a graph and leverages local neighborhood context to guide expression reconstruction, thereby learning robust cell representations. The method integrates a network enhancement module to denoise the cell similarity graph, a neighborhood-enhanced autoencoder that reconstructs gene expression using topological neighborhood context, and a graph neural network to preserve structural semantics among cells. By embedding each cell's expression profile within its neighbors, scDGCN captures subtle transcriptional variation and identifies cell subtypes without labeled references. Across ten scRNA-seq datasets from diverse human and mouse tissues, scDGCN achieves competitive adjusted Rand index (ARI), normalized mutual information (NMI), and clustering accuracy (ACC), supporting unsupervised identification of cellular subpopulations. These results demonstrate that combining graph denoising, neighborhood-enhanced context reconstruction, and graph-structured representation learning improves unsupervised single-cell clustering and facilitates high-resolution cell atlas construction.
pool.authors: Tang B, Feng Y, Cheng G, Wang J

pool.title: Inverse probability weighting-based mediation analysis for microbiome data
pool.abstract: Abstract Motivation Mediation analysis is an important tool for elucidating causal mechanisms in biomedical research and has recently gained increasing attention in microbiome studies. Motivated by a microbiome study of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, we investigate whether the effect of induction chemotherapy intensity on infection status is mediated through gut microbial taxa. This problem poses substantial methodological challenges due to the high dimensionality, zero inflation, and dependence of microbial mediators, as well as the presence of an exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounder, antibiotic use. Results To address these challenges, we propose a novel nonparametric identification formula for the interventional indirect effect, a causal mediation estimand that remains identifiable in the presence of exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounding. Building on this identification result, we develop an inverse probability weighting estimator and construct standard normal bootstrap confidence intervals for inference. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate effect estimation and maintains appropriate type I error rates and power in finite samples. Application to the AML microbiome study provides evidence of a statistically significant interventional indirect effect of induction chemotherapy intensity on infection risk through alterations in the gut microbiome. Availability and implementation The R code for the simulation studies is available at https://github.com/YX-ZHANG-1/CausalMediationMicrobiome and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21960802.
pool.authors: Yuexia Zhang, Jian Wang, Jiayi Shen, Jessica Galloway-Peña, Samuel A. Shelburne, Linbo Wang, Jianhua Hu

pool.title: Parsing altered brain connectivity in neurodevelopmental disorders by integrating graph-based normative modeling and deep generative networks
pool.abstract: Divergent brain connectivity is thought to underlie the behavioral and cognitive symptoms observed in many neurodevelopmental disorders. Quantifying divergence from neurotypical connectivity patterns offers a promising pathway to inform diagnosis and therapeutic interventions. While advanced neuroimaging techniques, such as diffusion MRI (dMRI), have facilitated the mapping of brain's structural connectome, the challenge lies in accurately modeling developmental trajectories within these complex networked structures to create robust neurodivergence markers. In this work, we present the Brain Representation via Individualized Deep Generative Embedding (BRIDGE) framework, which integrates normative modeling with a bio-inspired deep generative model to create a reference trajectory of connectivity transformation as part of neurotypical development. This will enable the assessment of neurodivergence by comparing individuals to the established neurotypical trajectory. BRIDGE provides a global neurodivergence score based on the difference between connectivity-based brain age and chronological age, along with region-wise neurodivergence maps that highlight localized connectivity differences. Application of BRIDGE to a large cohort of children with autism spectrum disorder demonstrates that the global neurodivergence score correlates with clinical assessments in autism, and the regional map offers insights into the heterogeneity at the individual level in neurodevelopmental disorders. Together, the neurodivergence score and map form powerful tools for quantifying developmental divergence in connectivity patterns, advancing the development of imaging markers for personalized diagnosis and intervention in various clinical contexts.
pool.authors: Rui Shen, Livia Rodrigues, Yusuf Osmanlıoğlu, Drew Parker, Sai Krishna C Annavazala, Darien Aunapu, Benjamin E. Yerys, Birkan Tunç, Ragini Verma

pool.title: From Representation to Enactment: The ABC Framework of the Translating Mind
pool.abstract: Building on the third-wave extended-mind (EM) theory and radical enactivism, this article suggests a novel view on the translating mind. We build on the ABC framework, in which translation is not understood as the manipulation of static interlingual correspondences but an enacted activity, dynamically integrating affective-evaluative, behavioral-enacting, and cognitive-inferential (ABC) processes. Drawing on affordance theory, we argue that the translating mind is a dynamically organized process through which the translator and its environment constitute and transform a landscape of enlanguaged translation affordances that emerges through loops of brain–body–environment interactions. This non-representational account reframes translation as skillful participation in socio-cultural practice, where meaning is co-created in real time through embodied interaction with texts, tools, and contexts.
pool.authors: Michael Carl, Takanori Mizowaki, Aishvarya Raj, Masaru Yamada, Devi Sri Bandaru, Yuxiang Wei, Xinyue Ren

pool.title: Bayesian Ambiguity-Contraction-Based Adaptive Robust Markov Decision Processes for Adversarial Surveillance Missions
pool.abstract: Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCAs) are envisioned to enable autonomous intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions in contested environments, where adversaries may act strategically to deceive or evade detection. These missions pose challenges due to model uncertainty and the need for safe, real-time decision-making. Robust Markov decision processes (RMDPs) provide worst-case guarantees but are limited by static ambiguity sets that capture initial uncertainty without adapting to new observations. This paper presents an adaptive RMDP framework tailored to ISR missions with CCAs. We introduce a mission-specific formulation in which the CCA alternates between movement and sensing states. Adversarial uncertainty is represented by finite threat prototypes defining observation, exposure, and state–action transition models. Our approach incrementally refines policies by eliminating inconsistent threat models, allowing the CCA to move from worst-case protection toward more efficient mission policies while maintaining robustness. We establish fixed-point stability, agreement with nominal planning as credible sets identify the true node-specific threat prototypes, and a conservative expected value guarantee while those prototypes remain credible. Experiments under Gaussian and non-Gaussian threat models across diverse network topologies show higher mission rewards and fewer exposure events compared to nominal and static robust planners.
pool.authors: Jimin Choi, Max Z. Li

pool.title: SPHERE-MS: Hybrid Fragment–Vocabulary Modeling for Accurate and Efficient Tandem Mass Spectra Prediction
pool.abstract: Abstract Identifying known compounds and elucidating unknown chemical structures from mass spectra remains a significant challenge due to the limited size of experimental reference libraries. Enhancing these libraries with predicted mass spectra through computational methods offers an opportunity to resolve unmatched spectra. In this paper, we present SPHERE-MS (Secondary-loss Powered Hybrid Edge Removal Engine for predicting Mass Spectra), a graph neural network model designed to predict mass spectra from molecular structures. The hybrid approach, combining bond-breaking and vocabulary-based strategies, enables SPHERE-MS to efficiently simulate multilevel fragmentation processes without the need to enumerate all possible bond combinations. Evaluations on the NIST-20, MSnLib, CASMI2022, and MassSpecGym data sets demonstrate that SPHERE-MS outperforms baseline models that rely on single fragment generation strategy, showing higher prediction accuracy and library retrieval success rates. Notably, SPHERE-MS also maintains reasonable accuracy even when applied to molecules with low structural similarity to the training set. This strong generalization capability makes SPHERE-MS a valuable tool for mass spectra prediction across large libraries, including those containing uncommon structures.
pool.authors: Yitong Guan, Doudou Lou, Dong Chen, Mengyuan Liu, Yuan Zhu, Shuqiang Zhao, Xiangying Zhang

pool.title: Latent Style-Based Quantum Wasserstein GAN for Drug Design
pool.abstract: Abstract The development of new drugs is a tedious, time-consuming, and expensive process for which the average costs are estimated to be up to around $2.5 billion. The first step in this long process is the design of the new drug, for which de novo drug design, assisted by artificial intelligence, has blossomed in recent years and has revolutionized the field. In particular, generative artificial intelligence has delivered promising results in drug discovery and development, reducing costs and time to solution. However, classical generative models, such as generative adversarial networks (GANs), can be difficult to train and are prone to mode collapse. Quantum computing may be an avenue to overcome some of these issues, providing compact models with far fewer trainable parameters and thereby enhancing the generalizability of GANs. We propose a new latent style-based quantum Wasserstein GAN (QGAN) for drug design, combining a variational autoencoder that maps molecular structures into a latent space with a hybrid quantum GAN. Our pipeline is benchmarked against the classical models of the industry-relevant MOSES suite. Style-based noise reuploading at every rotational gate and a Wasserstein gradient penalty are used to improve trainability and to mitigate mode collapse. Training and large-scale sampling with circuits of up to 15 qubits are performed on noiseless quantum simulators to validate our architecture. We present an inference-only demonstration on a 156-qubit IBM Heron quantum computer using a five-qubit setup, sampling 2,500 new molecules, to investigate the effect of quantum noise. Our default QGAN, using 110 trainable generator parameters, reaches statistically comparable overall performance and statistically significant gains on selected drug-relevant metrics relative to both the MOSES classical latent GAN baseline, which contains about 700,000 trainable parameters for the generator, and a classical latent GAN with matched generator capacity.
pool.authors: Julien Baglio, Y. Haddad, Richard Polifka

metadata.venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

pool.title: Timescale separation enables deep reinforcement learning control of rotating detonation engine mode transitions
pool.abstract: Rotating detonation engines (RDEs) are a promising propulsion concept that may offer higher thermodynamic efficiency and specific impulse than conventional systems, but nonlinear phenomena, including transitions to oscillatory or chaotic propagation modes, can hinder practical operation. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a promising method for controlling complex nonlinear dynamics such as those observed in RDEs. However, the multi-timescale nature of the RDE system makes direct application of DRL challenging. We address this challenge by reformulating the DRL problem in a moving reference frame that follows the detonation-wave pattern, making the wave structure appear quasi-steady to the agent. This reformulation enables scale separation between fast detonation propagation and slower operating-mode dynamics. We train DRL controllers to modulate spatially segmented injection pressure in a one-dimensional reduced-order RDE model and induce rapid transitions between different mode-locked states. Across a range of actuation periods, initial states, and target modes, controllers trained in the moving frame learn more reliably than those trained in a stationary frame and remain effective over a broader range of actuation periods. These results suggest that symmetry-aware moving reference frame formulations may be useful for related multiscale flow-control problems and that scale separation should be exploited whenever possible to enable DRL control of multi-timescale systems.
pool.authors: Kristian Holme, Jean Rabault, Ricardo Vinuesa, Mikael Mortensen

pool.title: Adjoint method versus physics-informed neural networks in PDE-constrained inverse problems
pool.abstract: Inverse problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs) are central to computational mechanics and are commonly solved by adjoint-based optimization, while physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as a flexible alternative. Their relative performance remains difficult to assess because the two approaches are often compared under different formulations, parameterizations, optimizers, and regularization choices. We present a controlled comparison of adjoint optimization and PINNs for PDE-constrained inverse problems. From a common abstract formulation, we instantiate both methods on identical domains, governing equations, observation models, and regularization terms, while matching the optimizer, unknown parameterization, and arithmetic precision wherever applicable. The benchmarks include unsteady Burgers, noisy Darcy permeability inversion, three-dimensional Allen–Cahn reaction identification, and unsteady Navier–Stokes viscosity identification. The results show that the representation of the unknown largely determines the preferred method: grid-based fields favor the discrete adjoint, whereas neural representations are native to PINNs and relevant for closure and constitutive modeling. For time-dependent problems, adjoint inversion can be dominated by trajectory storage and differentiation, while PINNs provide satisfactory reconstructions at lower cost. A PINN-warm-started adjoint strategy then recovers adjoint-level accuracy at about half the cost.
pool.authors: Zhen Zhang, Alessandro Alla, George Em Karniadakis

metadata.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering

pool.title: Lifetime Sample Tracking (LiST): A data platform for materials science
pool.abstract: The 2D Crystal Consortium Materials Innovation Platform (2DCC-MIP) is a NSF supported national user facility focused on advancing the synthesis of 2D materials, monolayers, surfaces, and interfaces. The need for the facility to organize and share data with users led to the development of an internal data management and analysis engine, the Lifetime Sample Tracking platform (LiST). This infrastructure allows the automated capture, curation, analysis, and dissemination of data ranging from experimental materials synthesis parameters and characterization to theoretical first-principles and ReaxFF molecular dynamics modeling [Nayir et al., 2D Mater. 10, 032002 (2023)]. The system currently hosts synthesis and property data (accessible via a REST API) on ∼20 000 samples produced by the 2DCC grown using a variety of techniques from bulk crystal growth to metal-organic chemical vapor deposition and molecular beam epitaxy, among others. Data used in publications can easily be grouped by the system into data packages that are given digital object identifiers for inclusion with each publication. The LiST platform is now being used by groups outside of the 2DCC as a solution for data curation in materials science. Data management tools, such as LiST, support the materials development process by allowing a closed loop iteration between synthesis, characterization, theory, and targeted materials design. This also enables machine learning research, artificial intelligence analysis, and the potential for autonomous synthesis in the future.
pool.authors: R Richardella Anthony, Isaiah A. Moses, Konrad Hilse, Frank Santaguida, Kevin Dressler, Ric Wilburn, Saiyyam Kochar, Wesley F. Reinhart, Adri C. T. van Duin, Nitin Samarth, Vincent H. Crespi, Joan Marie Redwing

pool.title: Better queries, cheaper attention: Adapting transformers for efficient sparse reconstruction
pool.abstract: Abstract Query-based transformer decoders are effective for object reconstruction from sparse scientific sensor measurements, but their scalability to high-multiplicity data is limited by fixed, input-independent query sets and costly decoder cross-attention. We introduce a geometry-aware dynamic-query decoder that couples input-conditioned query construction with structured sparse cross-attention. Decoder queries are initialised from selected encoder-level measurement representations that serve as candidate trajectory seeds, making both query content and query multiplicity input-dependent. Local Strided Cross-Attention (LSCA) exploits the induced geometric ordering by replacing learned mask-gated cross-attention with a geometry-defined local support that restricts attention to physically plausible query--hit interactions and exposes sparsity for block-sparse execution. We study this architecture for charged-particle trajectory reconstruction in a simplified High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider detector, where thousands of trajectories must be reconstructed from tens of thousands of sparse measurements. In the nominal configuration, evaluated for particles with $\pT \geq 1~\mathrm{GeV}$, the dynamic-query (DQ) architecture increases trajectory reconstruction efficiency from $94.1\%$ to $98.1\%$ and reduces the fake rate by more than a factor of two relative to the fixed-query baseline. The DQ+LSCA model reduces end-to-end inference latency by more than $70\%$ and peak allocated inference memory by more than a factor of $10$ relative to the fixed-query baseline.
pool.authors: Philippa Duckett, Samuel Van Stroud, Max Hart, G. Facini, Tim Scanlon

pool.title: Data-driven mitigation of catastrophic forgetting in dynamic physical layer attack detection
pool.abstract: Optical networks are critical infrastructure that underpins global communications, and detecting security breaches that jeopardize them is essential to maintaining worldwide connectivity. As malicious actors continuously evolve their attack techniques, dynamically updated intrusion detection models have become a key component of modern defense mechanisms. By incorporating newly acquired telemetry data, these models can adapt to emerging threats while maintaining high detection performance. However, when previously encountered attacks reappear after a prolonged period of absence, adaptive models may fail to recognize them due to the phenomenon of catastrophic forgetting. In contrast, statically trained models can reliably detect attacks represented in the original training data but lack the ability to adapt to previously unseen attack patterns. Consequently, intrusion detection systems face a fundamental tradeoff between adaptability to evolving threats and long-term retention of previously acquired knowledge. In this work, we propose a data-driven mechanism to cope with catastrophic forgetting in dynamic attack detection systems. Our approach balances the model update datasets by using parts of past attack data. We utilize a threshold-based mechanism to trigger data balancing after accuracy drops due to an active attack change. Applied to an experimental optical network security dataset, the proposed approach reduces the average model adaptation time by 37% compared to its dynamic counterpart that does not employ data balancing. Compared to a baseline from the literature that relies on neural network depth increasing, our approach requires 6% fewer data batches to adapt to changing conditions and regain performance.

pool.title: Physics vs. AI in weather prediction: evaluating GraphCast, AIFS, and FuXi against an observation-corrected WRF model for flash floods
pool.abstract: Abstract. Data-driven artificial intelligence (AI) weather models are increasingly positioned as alternatives or complements to physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems, yet systematic model evaluation studies that compare both paradigms under controlled experimental conditions remain limited. Here we present a structured model evaluation framework applying standardised verification metrics to assess a regional WRF configuration against three publicly available AI models – GraphCast, AIFS Single 1.0, and FuXi – over three high-impact flood events in Luxembourg and the Greater Region (2016, 2018, and 2021), comprising 90 simulation days and over 7300 matched forecast-observation pairs. The WRF model employs a three-dimensional variational (3D-VAR) data assimilation scheme ingesting GNSS Zenith Total Delay and conventional observations on a 6-hourly Rapid Update Cycle. All systems are initialised from ERA5 reanalysis to ensure consistent initial conditions. Categorical precipitation scores at the 1 mm threshold and continuous temperature metrics at surface stations serve as verification targets. Data assimilation measurably improves WRF's categorical precipitation skill (Critical Success Index: 0.306 to 0.341) while leaving near-surface temperature largely unchanged, demonstrating the value of the assimilation scheme. AIFS achieves the highest detection rate (POD 0.765) and net categorical skill (CSI 0.370), GraphCast and AIFS reduce temperature RMSE by ~10 % relative to assimilated WRF, and WRF alone reproduces the observed mesoscale precipitation structure of the catastrophic July 2021 flood. The per-event breakdown reveals no skill degradation for AI models on out-of-sample events, suggesting that meteorological regime rather than training-data overlap governs model performance. These results provide a replicable model evaluation methodology for benchmarking emerging data-driven NWP systems against observation-corrected regional models.
pool.authors: Haseeb ur Rehman, Felix Norman Teferle

pool.title: Beyond pairwise interactions: Accurate forecasting of co-evolutionary spreading on higher-order networks
pool.abstract: Many co-evolutionary spreading processes involve higher-order interactions, yet the consequences of approximating them through pairwise representations remain insufficiently understood. Here, we uncover distinctive prediction failures of pairwise graph neural networks during node-level one-step conditional transition-probability prediction on simplicial complexes. Patterns of bias between Att-GNN predictions and the true transition probabilities show ordered diagonal stratification in homogeneous networks and apparently disordered scattering in long-tailed networks, with bias persisting even at nodes with negligible second-order connectivity. Bias direction depends systematically on the relative numbers of active 1- and 2-simplex transmission channels, which jointly characterize local exposure. We interpret these phenomena as higher-order truncation bias arising from compensatory learning. Omitted simplicial contributions are absorbed into a shared pairwise mapping whose statistical compromise yields excessive or insufficient compensation across local exposure conditions. To address this, we propose Att-HGNN, a topology-adaptive higher-order attention model that explicitly aggregates simplicial interactions through node-specific queries and structure-specific keys and values. Across competitive, cooperative, and asymmetric dynamics simulated on synthetic and empirical contact-derived topologies, Att-HGNN empirically reduces the observed prediction bias. Ten-seed comparisons between matched pairwise and higher-order variants of four GNN families on SC-ER and SC-SF networks show consistent benefits from higher-order aggregation, with Att-HGNN achieving the strongest overall performance among eight models in Pearson correlation and probability MSE.
pool.authors: Wenyao Li, Tao Lin, Wei Wang

pool.title: A Benchmark of Unsupervised Anomaly Detectors for Credit Card Fraud under Two Training Protocols
pool.abstract: Credit card fraud detection is a critical problem in financial security, yet real-world deployment scenarios often lack labeled fraud samples at initial stages, making unsupervised anomaly detection an appealing approach. However, the comparative performance of different unsupervised detectors under varying training data compositions—whether trained exclusively on normal transactions or on mixed data containing unlabeled frauds—remains insufficiently studied. This paper presents a head-to-head benchmark of five unsupervised anomaly detectors—Mahalanobis distance, Isolation Forest, Local Outlier Factor (LOF), One-Class SVM, and Elliptic Envelope—on the publicly available ULB Credit Card Fraud Detection dataset. Each detector is evaluated under two training protocols: novelty detection (trained solely on normal transactions) and outlier detection (trained on the full dataset containing both normal and fraudulent samples). Performance is measured using PR-AUC, Precision@k, and recall at low false positive rates. Results show that Mahalanobis distance and LOF achieve strong performance under the novelty detection protocol (PR-AUC > 0.73) but suffer catastrophic degradation when trained on mixed data, with PR-AUC dropping by 0.57 and 0.72 respectively. Isolation Forest gives solid and reliable results on both two tested protocols, and its PR-AUC score increases slightly from 0.3953 to 0.4432. After parameter adjustment (with parameters set as support_fraction=0.9, contamination=0.01), Elliptic Envelope gets moderate performance (PR-AUC≈0.37) and is almost insensible to protocol changes. The conclusions obtained in this part can provide actual instruction for choosing unsupervised detectors to be used in real fraud detection systems working under various conditions of label availability and data quality.
pool.authors: Ruyu Guo

pool.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Smart Home Systems: Technologies, Applications and Future Challenges
pool.abstract: With the continuous development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, smart home systems have gradually evolved from traditional automated control modes toward intelligent systems with environmental perception, autonomous decision-making, and proactive service capabilities. However, existing smart homes still face problems such as a single mode of interaction, insufficient intelligent proactivity, and limited scene adaptability. Based on relevant research results in recent years, this paper systematically reviews the application progress of AI technology in the smart home field, focusing on key directions such as the Internet of Things (IoT) architecture, multimodal interaction, intelligent decision-making, edge computing, and data security. The review shows that AI technology has effectively improved the perception, interaction, and decision-making capabilities of smart home systems. Among these technologies, large language models (LLMs) enhance natural language understanding and user interaction capabilities, edge computing improves the real-time response efficiency of the system, and technologies such as blockchain provide new solutions for data security. At the same time, smart homes still face challenges in privacy protection, model reliability, cross-device collaboration, and standardization. In the future, modern smart home systems should be further integrated with artificial intelligence technologies, change traditional basic interaction modes, and promote the development of smart homes toward greater intelligence, security, and adaptability.
pool.authors: Ruikang Dong

pool.title: Evolving federated density peak clustering with shuffler-based anonymization
pool.abstract: Abstract In this paper, we present a novel one-shot federated clustering approach based on evolving fuzzy clustering and shuffler-based anonymization. In federated clustering, each round reveals additional model information to the server and can increase the opportunity to infer properties of local datasets, even when raw samples are never shared. Consequently, fewer client–server exchanges and unlinkability are important, so transmitted information cannot be attributed to any single client. Data-stream clustering algorithms, which learn in a single pass over the data, align well with the one-shot federated learning paradigm, where a single communication round can be sufficient. The proposed Evolving Federated Density Peak Clustering (eFDPC) method combines evolving fuzzy data-stream clustering and density peak clustering in a federated setting. Each client independently evolves micro-clusters from private data mini-batches through cluster addition and merging. To limit communication, density peak clustering is applied to the learned micro-clusters and only the selected peaks are transmitted, rather than the full local models. A shuffler-based layer is introduced between the clients and the server to anonymize contributions prior to reconstruction and global peak selection. We consider a peak-only variant, eFDPC- $$\mathcal {P}$$ , as well as eFDPC- $$\mathcal {G}$$ with server-side label propagation. Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmark datasets show that eFDPC outperforms recent federated clustering baselines in one-shot settings and scales to higher-dimensional, non-IID data.
pool.authors: Miha Ožbot, Seiichi Ozawa, Igor Škrjanc

pool.title: CMGL: Confidence-guided Multi-omics Graph Learning for Cancer Subtype Classification.
pool.abstract: Multi-omics integration can improve cancer subtyping, but modality informativeness and noise vary across cancer types and patients. Most graph methods for multi-omics data learn modality contributions within the downstream classification objective, leaving predictive reliability for each patient implicit. As a result, uninformative modalities can weaken the fused representation, while unreliable omics can introduce noisy patient relationships into graph propagation. To address these two problems, we propose CMGL, which produces a separate reliability estimate before fusion and uses consensus patient neighborhoods for graph classification.
pool.authors: Fan B, Yin H, Yi S, Wang Y, Li Z, Zhou L, Lv J, Ju W

pool.title: Leveraging traditional and advanced machine learning for comprehensive oncology data integration and outcome prediction.
pool.abstract: BACKGROUND: Outcome prediction in neuro-oncology remains challenging due to heterogeneity in tumor biology, imaging characteristics, treatment response, and patient-specific clinical factors. Although molecular databases have advanced understanding of brain tumor biology, many datasets lack broader data necessary for generalizable predictive modeling. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly being explored to integrate these heterogeneous data sources and support precision neuro-oncology. METHODS: A narrative review was performed using PubMed and Embase to identify studies evaluating oncology databases, ML models, multimodal data integration, and AI applications relevant to neuro-oncology. Studies published between 2020 and 2026 were preferentially reviewed, with additional landmark studies included when relevant. RESULTS: Traditional ML approaches including regression-based models, random forests, support vector machines, and gradient boosting algorithms have been applied to survival prediction, recurrence classification, treatment response estimation, and molecular biomarker prediction using clinical, imaging, molecular, and population-level datasets. More advanced architectures including natural language processing, large language models, vision transformers, geometric deep learning, and graph neural networks have expanded the ability to analyze unstructured and multimodal data sources including radiology reports, histopathology slides, MRI volumes, molecular datasets, and electronic health records. Multimodal AI systems integrating imaging, molecular, histopathologic, clinical, and socioeconomic data frequently demonstrated improved predictive performance compared with single-modality models. However, widespread clinical implementation remains limited by dataset heterogeneity, limited external validation, interpretability concerns, and inconsistent representation across patient populations. CONCLUSIONS: AI and ML approaches are increasingly capable of integrating complex neuro-oncology datasets in ways that more closely reflect real-world clinical decision-making. Although most current models remain investigational, multimodal AI frameworks may ultimately improve prognostic assessment, treatment stratification, and precision neuro-oncology care. Continued progress will require larger representative datasets, improved data harmonization, external validation, and clinically interpretable models.
