pool.title: Uncovering the Unique Tumor Microenvironment of Ovarian Small Cell Neuroendocrine Carcinoma by Single-cell RNA Sequencing
pool.abstract: Our findings demonstrate that neuroendocrine marker genes and associated gene regulatory networks in SCNECO differ from those observed in pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinomas available in the GEO database, supporting a tissue specific origin for these malignancies. Collectively, this work addresses a critical gap in the understanding of SCNECO and provides valuable insights to guide chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy approaches.
pool.authors: 谢广婷(Guangting Xie)

pool.title: Synthetic Strategies and Emerging Therapeutic Interventions of Isoxazole and its Molecular Hybrids.
pool.abstract: Isoxazole is an important heterocyclic scaffold that has attracted considerable attention in medicinal chemistry because of its wide range of biological activities and favorable physicochemical characteristics. The isoxazole ring's usefulness as a favored scaffold in contemporary drug design and discovery has been highlighted by the production of many bioactive molecules and therapeutically relevant medications through its insertion into various molecular frameworks. This review discusses recent advances in the synthesis, reactivity, and therapeutic applications of isoxazole derivatives. It focuses on modern synthetic methods, such as microwave-assisted synthesis, 1,3- dipolar cycloaddition, visible-light photocatalysis, multicomponent reactions, and transition-metalcatalyzed approaches, which offer effective, regioselective, and sustainable ways to build isoxazole frameworks. In order to increase biological activity, improve selectivity, and broaden therapeutic potential, the isoxazole nucleus is carefully coupled with other pharmacophoric moieties in isoxazole- based hybrid compounds, which are becoming more and more popular. These hybrid compounds have shown a wide range of pharmacological actions, such as enzyme inhibitory, antioxidant, anticancer, antibacterial, and anti-inflammatory effects, underscoring their importance in the hunt for new therapeutic candidates. Structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies are also emphasized to better understand how structural changes affect biological activity. A 4-OEt substituent increased the antiproliferative activity of isoxazole-naphthalene hybrids, while electron-withdrawing substituents like Cl, F, and NO2 enhanced antibacterial activity in isoxazole-acridone hybrids, according to representative SAR investigations. Furthermore, efficacy and selectivity were strongly impacted by linker length, heteroatom inclusion, and molecular hybridization with heterocyclic scaffolds. In order to demonstrate the translational relevance and therapeutic value of this scaffold in modern drug development, the article also briefly examines a few clinically utilized medications that contain the isoxazole moiety. All things considered, this review provides a simple but thorough overview of recent advancements in isoxazole chemistry and hybrid molecule design. It also offers insightful information about the logical design and potential future development of novel therapeutic agents with enhanced and potential clinical relevance.
pool.authors: Gupta M, Kapoor I, Fizanoor, Saini N

pool.title: Thermostable Fibrinolytic Serine Metalloproteases from Bacillus subtilis and Bacillus thuringiensis: Optimized Production, Partial Purification, and Enzymatic Characterization of Thrombolytic Activity".
pool.abstract: Fibrinolytic enzymes of microbial origin are gaining attention as safer alternatives to conventional thrombolytic drugs. In this study, fibrinolytic enzymes were isolated and characterized from Bacillus subtilis and Bacillus thuringiensis derived from soil samples. Process optimization revealed maximum enzyme production at 37 °C and pH 7.0 after 24 hrs of incubation, with inoculum sizes of 1.5% (B. subtilis) and 1% (B. thuringiensis) in media supplemented with glucose/sucrose and yeast extract. Partial purification yielded specific activities of 191.15 U/mg (B. subtilis) and 218.24 U/mg (B. thuringiensis) with recovery yields of 14.39% and 13.89%, respectively. Both enzymes exhibited stability over broad ranges of pH (5.0-9.0) and temperature (10-60 °C). Enzyme activity was enhanced by Mg2+ and Ca2+ but completely inhibited by EDTA and PMSF, confirming that the enzymes are serine metalloproteases. Amidolytic assays demonstrated high activity with a chymotrypsin substrate, while hemolytic activity remained below 5%, indicating therapeutic safety. SDS-PAGE revealed molecular masses of 35 kDa (B. subtilis) and 33 kDa (B. thuringiensis). Kinetic analysis showed Km values of 3.488 mg/mL and 3.125 mg/mL with Vmax values of 232.56 U/mL and 178.57 U/mL, respectively. These findings suggest that fibrinolytic enzymes from both strains were potent, stable, and promising candidates for thrombolytic drug development.
pool.authors: Sahoo SK, Das P, Kerry RG, Sahoo SM, Jena AB, Duttaroy AK, Majhi S

pool.title: Protein inhibitor of retinal membrane guanylyl cyclase rescues photoreceptors from degeneration induced by mutated guanylyl cyclase activating protein.
pool.abstract: Mutations in the GUCA1A gene coding for calcium-sensor protein GCAP1 cause congenital cone and cone-rod degenerations by disabling Ca2+-dependent reduction of cGMP synthesis in photoreceptors in the dark. Engineered protein inhibitor of guanylyl cyclase (PIGCY) effectively prevented in vitro stimulation of retinal membrane guanylyl cyclase (RetGC) by Y99C or E155G GCAP1, most commonly causing GUCA1A retinopathy. However, it was less effective against G86R and L176F GCAP1. PIGCY expressed in transgenic mouse rods (PIGCYTg) did not reverse the abnormal Ca2+-sensitivity of RetGC in mice harboring Y99C GCAP1 (Y99CTg) but reduced the overall cGMP production rate in dark-adapted PIGCYTgY99CTg retinas. PIGCY markedly slowed the progression of photoreceptor degeneration in Y99CTg mice: 84% of photoreceptor nuclei remained after 6 months in PIGCYTgY99CTg compared with only 30% in Y99CTg littermates. The histological layer of rod outer segments in the posterior retina was much better defined in aged PIGCYTgY99CTg mice than in Y99CTg littermates. Electroretinography (ERG) showed that PIGCY also dramatically rescued the light sensitivity of the dark-adapted Y99CTg rods. Whereas scotopic b-wave amplitude (rod ERG) diminished sixfold in Y99CTg compared with the wild type, it remained 80% of normal amplitude in PIGCYTgY99CTg littermates. ERG a-wave amplitude, generated by hyperpolarizing photoreceptors in response to a bright flash, was reduced more than tenfold in Y99CTg but only by 35% in PIGCYTgY99CTg. The results indicate that PIGCY can be considered for prospective gene therapy for some GCAP1 mutations causing dominant GUCA1A retinopathy.
pool.authors: Tan L, Peshenko IV, Olshevskaya EV, Dizhoor AM

pool.title: Consensus on the use of intrathecal gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy.
pool.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intrathecal (IT) delivery of gene therapy is an emerging strategy for Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA), aiming to enhance central nervous system targeting while potentially reducing systemic exposure. The new administration route of Onasemnogene abeparvovec is associated with a distinct safety profile, including dorsal root ganglia toxicity, and requires structured monitoring beyond existing intravenous guidelines, including planning for long-term multidisciplinary follow-up in pediatric and adult care as well as structured transition protocols. METHODS: We expanded the existing intravenous monitoring guideline by incorporating surveillance for potential dorsal root ganglia-related adverse effects. The protocol integrates clinical, laboratory, electrophysiological, imaging, and long-term follow-up recommendations. RESULTS: The protocol defines pre-treatment assessment, peri-procedural management, and longitudinal follow-up in both pediatric and adult care settings, with emphasis on proactive evaluation of dorsal root ganglia function and structured transition of adolescents treated before adulthood to specialized multidisciplinary adult neurology services. CONCLUSIONS: A structured, multimodal monitoring approach-including dorsal root ganglia surveillance, multidisciplinary long-term follow-up, and coordinated transition from pediatric to adult care-is essential for the safe implementation of intrathecal Onasemnogene abeparvovec in SMA.
pool.authors: Blaschek A, Schara-Schmidt U, Petri S, Walter MC, Weiß C, Vill K, Baumann M, Bernert G, Flotats Bastardas M, Von Der Hagen M, Johannsen J, Köhler C, Stettner GMM, Kirschner J, Pechmann A, Hahn A, Weiler M, Hagenacker T, Ziegler A

pool.title: A cross-species AAV platform for precise microglial interrogation.
pool.abstract: Targeting microglia with adeno-associated viruses (AAVs) remains challenging because of inefficient transduction, off-target expression, and inconsistent payload performance. Here, we develop an integrated, Cre-independent AAV platform that combines a compact 446-bp microglia-specific regulatory element (MSRE), a high-yield AAV2/9.m capsid, microRNA-mediated neuronal de-targeting, and a microglia-tailored codon-optimization strategy. Following direct intracranial delivery, the optimized vector achieves robust, long-lasting transgene expression with greater than 90% microglial specificity across multiple mouse brain regions, including in an Alzheimer's disease model. With doxorubicin-assisted delivery, the platform also enables efficient and selective microglial targeting in rats, rhesus macaques, and human ex vivo brain slices. Codon optimization supports the expression of otherwise challenging functional payloads, enabling calcium imaging, chemogenetic manipulation, and CRISPR-Cas9-mediated genome editing. This cross-species toolkit provides a versatile resource for investigating microglial biology and developing microglia-directed therapeutic strategies.
pool.authors: Yu F, Wang R, Di R, Xu K, Gao J, Shang H, Yuan Z, Dai R, Wu W, Weng D, Gao X, Li H, Yu T, Zhang Y, Wang X, Luan G, Zhao F, Luo M

pool.title: Advances in Stem Cell Therapy for Hearing Loss.
pool.abstract: Hearing loss is the most common sensory disorder, causing substantial impacts on language development, literacy, mood, and cognition. Sensorineural hearing loss, caused by injury to the cochlear hair cells, cochlear nerve, or central auditory pathways, accounts for most cases of hearing loss. Existing therapies for sensorineural hearing loss include hearing aids and cochlear implants; however, these modalities have limited efficacy in noisy environments, variable hearing outcomes, and limited frequency discrimination. There are currently no Food and Drug Administration-approved cellular, molecular, or pharmacological therapies available. Stem cell therapy is an emerging and promising approach to treating sensorineural hearing loss through transplanting exogenous stem cells into the cochlea. Stem cell-based inner ear systems have been crucial to studying how stem cells can mimic or restore the function of the inner ear. The two-dimensional culture system has been instrumental in understanding pluripotent stem cell differentiation in the inner ear neuroepithelium. However, they are unable to mimic tissue-specific architecture and specific cellular interactions. Researchers subsequently moved to develop differentiation protocols in three-dimensional inner ear organoids, which more closely resemble in vivo structures. Such approaches are a promising step forward in the development of stem cell therapies focusing on structures in the cochlea that have limited to no ability to regenerate, including hair cells, spiral ganglion neurons, and spiral ligament fibrocytes. Future directions of this field include integrating stem cell therapy with gene therapy approaches and developing novel high-throughput drug screening platforms.
pool.authors: Krishnan PS, Jung D, Morris JA, Tang PC, Liu XZ

pool.title: Otoferlin Gene Therapy: Narrative Review for Ear and Hearing Special Issue: Gene Therapy for Hearing Loss.
pool.abstract: In the last decade, gene therapy has shown promise in treating many genetic disorders. Hereditary hearing impairment represents one of the next promising frontiers. Many initial development efforts have focused on hearing impairment caused by mutations in the otoferlin gene (OTOF), as these mutations cause profound deafness in the setting of preserved auditory outer hair cells, which often remain for many years after birth. Animal models have shown that the target cells for gene delivery, the inner hair cells, are also present and viable, and they reside in a structurally intact organ that is otherwise functional. Recent remarkable successes reported with OTOF gene therapy serve as proof of concept that gene therapy can effectively and safely improve hearing for this and likely other forms of genetic deafness. Here, the authors review the otoferlin protein and its role in hearing, the role of pathogenic variants in OTOF in hearing loss, the natural history of the condition, and the results of preclinical studies and of current human clinical trials of OTOF gene therapy.
pool.authors: Devare J, Lawrence AP, Germiller JA

pool.title: Superconductivity and charge density waves in graphene-based materials.
pool.abstract: Graphene-based materials have emerged as a versatile platform for exploring strongly correlated quantum phenomena, particularly superconductivity (SC) and charge density waves (CDWs), owing to their highly tunable electronic structure, reduced dimensionality, and sensitivity to external perturbations. While pristine monolayer graphene is not intrinsically superconducting and exhibits limited propensity toward charge ordering, a variety of engineered graphene systems have demonstrated remarkable SC and CDW phases through mechanisms involving doping, intercalation, proximity coupling, strain, and moiré superlattice engineering. The discovery of correlated insulating states and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene has revolutionized the field by revealing unprecedented opportunities for studying unconventional pairing mechanisms and competing electronic orders in a purely carbon-based material platform.This review critically examines the current understanding of emergent SC and CDW in graphene-derived systems. We survey the diverse classes of graphene-based superconductors, including chemically doped and intercalated graphene, twisted bi- and trilayer graphene structures, and proximity-induced superconducting heterostructures, emphasizing the role of electron-phonon coupling, flat-band formation, and interfacial effects. Subsequently, we discuss the fundamental origins of CDW formation in graphene, focusing on electron-phonon interactions, Peierls instability, Fermi-surface nesting, defect engineering, doping, heterostructure design, and moiré-induced electronic reconstruction. The coexistence and competition between SC and charge-ordered phases, as revealed by scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), transport measurements, and other advanced experimental techniques are discussed.This review analyzes the principal theoretical frameworks employed to describe these correlated states, including the Holstein model, Eliashberg theory, unconventional pairing scenarios, strain-induced gauge fields, and topological superconductivity. We assess the extent to which conventional electron-phonon-mediated mechanisms can account for experimental observations and discuss alternative strongly correlated and topological descriptions. By integrating experimental discoveries with theoretical developments, this review outlines future directions for both fundamental research and quantum-device applications.&#xD.
pool.authors: Mazumder N, Bhattacharjee S, Roy R

pool.title: Metaproteomic analysis of human sonicate fluid highlights neutrophil extracellular trap formation associated with periprosthetic joint infection.
pool.abstract: UNLABELLED: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication of total joint arthroplasty that can be challenging to diagnose and treat. Neutrophils are a prominent feature in PJI, with neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) known to be present; little is known, however, about the physiology of PJI-associated NETs. Here, the proteomes of PJI and non-infectious arthroplasty failure (NIAF), analyzed using liquid chromatography tandem mass-spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and proximity extension assay (PEA)-based profiling of fluids derived from sonication of arthroplasty components removed from patients who had undergone revision arthroplasty, were compared, with a focus on NET formation. In addition, in vitro effects of synovial fluid components on Staphylococcus aureus-induced NET formation were characterized. LC-MS/MS (PJI n = 85, NIAF n = 26) and PEA (PJI n = 95, NIAF n = 39) showed NET formation and neutrophil degranulation to be associated with PJI, with the complement cascade and platelet activation pathways identified as potential contributors. In vitro studies showed delayed NET formation in artificial synovial fluid compared to standard cell culture media conventionally used to evaluate NETs. Together, these results demonstrate the presence of NETs in PJI, identify potential pathways involved in PJI-associated NETosis, and point to an influence of synovial components on NET formation during PJI. IMPORTANCE: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a major complication of joint replacement, placing a significant burden on patients and the healthcare system. Our research reveals that neutrophils and their antimicrobial "traps" are dominant features of the immune response at the infection joint site. Importantly, we found that the unique environment of the joint delays the formation of these traps, potentially contributing to the pathogenesis of PJI. By establishing a new experimental platform tailored for the infected joint, this work provides a foundational platform for probing these mechanisms and supports the development of improved diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
pool.authors: Garcia E, O'Connor K, Koscianski C, Alvarez Otero J, O'Donnell K, Mangalaparthi KK, Larson NB, Pandey A, Holmes D, Patel R

pool.title: The ternary complex structure as a foundation for structure-guided molecular glue design.
pool.abstract: Molecular glues are opening up new therapeutic areas by turning previously undruggable and intractable proteins into tractable targets through the formation or stabilisation of a ternary complex between two proteins. The present review focuses on how such structures are obtained and leveraged to guide rational design. Ternary complexes can be classified by protein-protein interface architecture and degree of topological constraint, informing the design process towards a given biological outcome. As with conventional small-molecule drug discovery, structural information provides invaluable insights for rational optimisation of glues, but solving a ternary complex structure remains a significant challenge owing to the underlying three-body equilibrium. Biophysical characterisation of cooperativity and ternary complex half-life not only provides optimisation parameters but also provides a means for prioritising the most promising glues for ternary structural studies by X-ray crystallography or cryogenic electron microscopy. Once solved, a ternary structure enables conventional structure-based design, such as scaffold hopping and surface decoration, and increasingly informs computational methods, though these remain most powerful when grounded in experimental validation. Ternary complex structures for canonical glue systems are now available in relative abundance, providing a foundation for both empirical and computational design; expanding this coverage beyond well-studied glue receptors and binding partners will test how broadly these principles generalise.
pool.authors: Cowan AD

pool.title: NA-CDQuant: Quantitative spectral analysis of nucleic acid structure by circular dichroism spectroscopy.
pool.abstract: Understanding the structural conformation and dynamics of nucleic acids in solution is critical for the development of nucleic acid therapeutics involving antisense or mRNA therapies, where controlling stability, efficacy, and manufacturability are important. Circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy allows rapid and nondestructive solution analysis of the spatial arrangements of nucleic acids. While widely used to analyze protein structure, the potential of CD for DNA- and RNA-based pharmaceutical applications has remained largely unrealized because nucleic acid spectra are complex and difficult to interpret quantitatively. We introduce herein a framework (NA-CDQuant) that transforms CD from a qualitative fingerprinting method into a quantitative tool for nucleic acid structure prediction by combining spectral deconvolution with a rigorously curated synchrotron radiation circular dichroism reference library comprising 18 structurally defined conformational families. This systematic classification overcomes long-standing challenges posed by spectral overlap and structural polymorphism, enabling estimation of the fractional composition of coexisting conformations during real-time monitoring of structural transitions in solution. NA-CDQuant provides mechanistic insight into subtle conformational redistributions that may affect molecular recognition and functional performance assisting pharmaceutical development and medical application by facilitating formulation optimization, stability assessment, quality control, and regulatory support of nucleic acid-based therapeutics.
pool.authors: Mosca K, Hoffmann SV, Jones NC, Sinden RR, Wien F, Marco S, Arluison V

pool.title: Cryopreservation induced changes in avian sperm: Molecular and biochemical perspectives.
pool.abstract: Cryopreservation is a pivotal tool for avian semen preservation but imposes detrimental effects on sperm viability and fertility. This review explores the biochemical and molecular mechanisms underlying cryopreservation-induced injuries in avian sperm, particularly in chickens, turkeys, ducks, and geese. Avian sperm exhibit a unique composition, including high polyunsaturated fatty acids, diverse proteins, and limited seminal plasma, rendering them vulnerable to oxidative stress and membrane damage during freezing and thawing. Cryopreservation leads to oxidative imbalance, lipid peroxidation, DNA fragmentation, and changes in antioxidant enzyme activity. Membrane rafts lose sterols, altering membrane fluidity and triggering early apoptotic events. Epigenetic modifications, including altered DNA methylation and RNA methylation, further compromise sperm function. Proteomic and transcriptomic changes, including disruptions in energy metabolism and motility-related proteins, contribute to reduced fertility. This review organizes the evidence around a proposed interconnected cryoinjury cascade; osmotic and ice-crystal stress, membrane damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and DNA/epigenetic damage, converging on reduced fertility, and distinguishes findings demonstrated directly in birds from those extrapolated from mammalian models. Comparative data are presented across chicken, turkey, duck, and goose sperm where available, with gaps identified. More thorough evaluation of cryoinjuries and biomarkers for fertility prediction is made possible by developments in analytical techniques including flow cytometry, metabolomics, and proteomics. Techniques like sterol inclusion, antioxidant supplementation, and cryoprotectant optimization show promise in reducing cryoinjuries. A comprehensive understanding of these intricate biochemical mechanisms is essential for enhancing genetic conservation in avian sperms, improving reproductive efficiency and optimizing semen cryopreservation procedures. This review also discusses potential future developments in integrative omics, nanotechnology, and molecular breakthroughs to maximize cryopreservation efficacy.
pool.authors: Akram S, Sadiq MJ, Sringarm K, Mektrirat R, Sathanawongs A

pool.title: Nonequilibrium noise emerging from broken detailed balance in active gels
pool.abstract: In thermodynamic equilibrium, the fluctuation-dissipation theorem links thermal fluctuations and dissipation. Biological systems, however, are driven out of equilibrium by internal processes that produce additional, active fluctuations. Despite being relevant for biological functions such as intracellular transport, predicting the statistical properties of active fluctuations remains challenging. Here, we address this challenge in a minimal model of an active gel as a network of elastic elements connected by transient crosslinks. The crosslinkers' binding and unbinding rates break detailed balance, which drives the system out of equilibrium. Through coarse-graining, we derive fluctuating hydrodynamic equations including an active noise term, which emerges explicitly from the breaking of detailed balance. Finally, we provide predictions for the stochastic motion of a tracer particle embedded in the active gel, which enables comparisons with microrheology experiments both in synthetic active gels and in cells. Overall, our work provides an explicit link between the statistical properties of active fluctuations and the molecular breaking of detailed balance. Thus, it paves the way toward complementing the fluctuation-dissipation theorem with a fluctuation-activity relation in active systems.

pool.title: Comprehensive Analytical Investigations of Quercetin Dihydrate: Modern Strategies and Future Directions
pool.abstract: Quercetin dihydrate, a naturally occurring flavonoid, has attracted considerable attention due to its extensive pharmacological activities, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer activities.It is plentifully present in dietary sources such as onions, apples, berries, and grapes.It exhibits stronger antioxidant activity in comparison to vitamin C and E, due to its potent free radical scavenging ability.It neutralizes reactive oxygen species and protects the cells from oxidative stress-induced damage.Furthermore, quercetin has demonstrated promising anticancer activity through the inhibition of cancer cell proliferation, induction of apoptosis, and modulation of multiple cellular signaling pathways, including NF-kB, MAPK, and PI3K/AKT pathways.This review highlights recent advances in analytical approaches for the identification, characterization, and quantification of quercetin dihydrate, with particular emphasis on validated HPLC and reverse-phase HPLC methods coupled with diode array and UV detection systems.Critically validated parameters such as linearity, precision, accuracy, robustness, ruggedness, selectivity, sensitivity, and stability have been comprehensively evaluated.

pool.title: Safe and efficient intracellular delivery of functional antibodies into cultured neural cells shows a role for Alzheimer’s-relevant tau phosphorylation in cell integrity
pool.abstract: Introduction Protein proteoforms generated by post-translational modification are increasingly recognized as important regulators of neuronal function and neurodegenerative disease. However, methods for acutely interrogating specific intracellular proteoforms in living neuronal populations remain limited. We evaluated cationic liposomal delivery (CLD) as a strategy for introducing full-length functional antibodies into living neurons and used this approach to investigate the role of a phosphorylated tau proteoform recognized by the monoclonal antibody PHF-1. Methods Cationic liposomes composed of DOPC+ were complexed with antibodies or molecular probes and applied to cultured neuronal cell lines and primary mouse cortical neurons. Intracellular delivery, cellular localization, viability, and biological activity were assessed using fluorescence microscopy and live-cell imaging. Results CLD efficiently delivered full-length antibodies and molecular probes into living neuronal cells and primary neurons without detectable toxicity. Internalized antibodies retained target specificity, producing intracellular staining patterns consistent with the known localization of tau, vinculin, paxillin, and Fyn. Delivery was observed across essentially all cells in treated cultures and remained effective under standard culture conditions. Intracellular delivery of PHF-1 produced a rapid and striking morphological response characterized by neurite retraction and cell-body rounding within hours of treatment. These effects were not observed with heat-inactivated PHF-1, vehicle controls, or other intracellular antibodies, supporting a specific effect of intracellular engagement of PHF-1-reactive tau species. Discussion These findings establish CLD as a practical platform for the intracellular delivery of functional full-length antibodies into living neuronal populations. Beyond validating a delivery technology, the study demonstrates that acute intracellular engagement of PHF-1-reactive phosphorylated tau rapidly alters neuronal morphology, suggesting that this tau proteoform contributes to the maintenance of neurite integrity. CLD provides a versatile approach for probing the function of intracellular proteoforms that are difficult to study using conventional genetic or biochemical methods.
pool.authors: Kirsten L. Viola, Brett A. Chromy, Raghad Nowar, Mary P. Lambert, Klein William L.

pool.title: Self‐Reporting Hierarchical DNA Nanoplatform for Tumor Cell‐Selective Senescence Modulation and Immune Remodeling
pool.abstract: Therapy-induced senescence (TIS) promotes tumor resistance and recurrence through the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), but achieving tumor cell-selective senescence modulation remains a formidable challenge due to limited cellular specificity, insufficient spatiotemporal control, and the complexity of the secretory program. Here, we develop a self-reporting hierarchical DNA nanoplatform (Gal-lipo@S-CHA) that enables selective senescence reprogramming and immune remodeling in TIS tumor cells. In this design, a newly engineered β-galactosidase-responsive charge-reversal lipid carrier establishes the first layer of senescence selectivity by enabling preferential delivery and enhanced endosomal escape of a hierarchically gated catalytic DNA circuit. Subsequent intracellular decoding of GSH and microRNA-21, two tumor-associated and senescence-enriched molecular signatures, provides a second layer of tumor cell selectivity, activating the circuit specifically in pathological senescent tumor cells. The activated circuit simultaneously generates a fluorescence signal for real-time monitoring and assembles an NF-κB decoy to block NF-κB nuclear translocation, thereby suppressing downstream pro-tumorigenic SASP production at the upstream regulatory source. In vivo studies demonstrate that Gal-lipo@S-CHA effectively remodels the tumor immune microenvironment by enhancing natural killer cell infiltration and M1 macrophage polarization. Collectively, this framework establishes a new paradigm for selectively reprogramming pathological senescence, providing a versatile platform to support immunomodulatory cancer therapies.

pool.title: Nanotechnology in Orthodontics: Current applications, clinical implications and future perspectives
pool.abstract: Background: Nanotechnology has emerged as one of the most promising advances in modern healthcare, offering innovative solutions through the manipulation of materials at the nanoscale level.In orthodontics, nanomaterials have demonstrated significant potential for improving the mechanical, biological & antimicrobial properties of orthodontic appliances & biomaterials.Objective: This review aims to critically evaluate the current applications of nanotechnology in orthodontics, with emphasis on orthodontic materials, antimicrobial strategies, drug delivery systems and orthodontic anchorage devices, while highlighting future directions & existing challenges.Methods: A narrative review of the contemporary literature was conducted to assess the role of nanotechnology in orthodontic practice & its impact on treatment efficiency, oral health and patient outcomes.Results: Nanotechnology has contributed to the development of nano-coated arch-wires & brackets with reduced frictional resistance & enhanced corrosion resistance.Antimicrobial nanoparticles, including silver, titanium dioxide, & zinc oxide nanoparticles, have demonstrated effectiveness in reducing bacterial colonization, biofilm formation and enamel demineralization during orthodontic treatment.Nano-reinforced adhesives exhibit improved mechanical properties and bond strength.Furthermore, nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems enable controlled release of therapeutic agents for inflammation control and periodontal support.Surface nanomodification of orthodontic mini-implants has shown potential to enhance osseointegration and implant stability.Conclusion: Nanotechnology represents a transformative approach in contemporary orthodontics by improving material performance, enhancing antimicrobial protection, and facilitating biologically targeted therapies.Despite encouraging laboratory & early clinical evidences, further long-term clinical studies are required to establish the safety, efficacy and cost-effectiveness of nanotechnology-based orthodontic applications before widespread clinical implementation.

pool.title: Programmed cell death in inflammation: interactions and holistic perspective
pool.abstract: Abstract Programmed cell death (PCD) is a major regulatory mechanism that maintains tissue homeostasis and immune balance and strongly influences the initiation, progression and resolution of inflammation. Although apoptosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis and ferroptosis are individual PCD modes that are regulated by different molecular mechanisms, they are not mutually exclusive in inflammatory microenvironments. Instead, these pathways are linked via common signaling mediators and regulatory nodes that enable crosstalk, compensatory activation and context-dependent fine-tuning. It is evident that apoptosis, pyroptosis and necroptosis can be coordinated within defined inflammatory platforms, as exemplified by concepts such as PANoptosis. Pathway-specific modeling is inadequate for inflammatory diseases involving multiple PCD modalities, metabolic and organelle stress, immune-cell interactions and tissue-level changes that molecular models cannot capture. Here, an integrated cell death network (ICDN) paradigm is presented as an organizational schema describing how various types of PCD are coregulated through common regulatory pathways in inflamed tissues. This framework does not identify a new mode of cell death per se but rather integrates pathway compensation following extracellular perturbations, disease-specific inflammatory responses, and susceptibility to therapeutic intervention at common network nodes. This review defines the molecular mechanisms and crosstalk of inflammatory pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis pathways; links recent advances in death modality applications for specific diseases to the ICDN framework; and highlights important current limitations that require further examination, including the need for stronger evidence of dynamic switching across cell death modalities, spatial architecture during inflammation, and reconfiguration at both the multiprotein complex and network levels, such as inflammasome networks.

pool.title: Food ration affects mRNA processing, translation, proteostasis, and cytoskeletal responses during heat shock in Mytilus californianus
pool.abstract: Despite a likely role in setting stress tolerance limits, food ration has received limited attention as an ecological factor affecting the cellular stress response (CSR). To study the interactive effects of food and temperature on the proteomic heat shock response, we acclimated intertidal mussels (Mytilus californianus) to four combinations of nearshore (low) and aquaculture (high) phytoplankton levels, combined with low (20 °C) and high (30 °C) aerial temperatures during daytime low tides. Mussels were then exposed to an acute (6 h), aerial heat stress (33 °C) and allowed to recover for 1 h and 25 h in pre-exposure conditions. Proteomic changes in the gill before and after heat shock were measured using label-free liquid-chromatography-mass spectrometry. Compared to other acclimation treatments, low-food-low-temperature (LTLF) mussels modified more splicing factors, heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoproteins, ribosomal proteins, and translation initiation and elongation factors, suggesting systemic changes to RNA processing, selection, and translation. LTLF mussels also increased chaperones of the actin- and microtubule-associated cytoskeleton and proteins that mature along the endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi secretory pathway. Simultaneously, actin stress fiber formation at focal adhesions and the extracellular matrix, along with anchoring of microtubule-associated cilia, indicate a possible system-wide mechanical breakdown of the cytoskeleton. Signaling proteins causing cytoskeletal changes varied mainly in LTLF mussels and suggest a food-dependent role for prostaglandin synthesis. Overall, the acclimation-dependent proteomic changes show how thermal conditioning and food ration together will shape the CSR of mussels during heat waves.

pool.title: Hot Issues and COOL Rules
pool.abstract: The following discussion focuses on the background and issues involved with country of origin labeling (COOL) and the impacts as they affect the livestock and meat industry, particularly beef and pork. While a review of the available literature will address many of the questions being debated, there are very few definitive answers at this point in time. Instead, the discussion proceeds with an assessment of the key policy questions yet to be resolved.
pool.authors: Bradley Lubben

pool.title: Tensor train compression of molecular orbitals
pool.abstract: This work systematically investigates the tensor train (TT) compressibility of gridrepresented Hartree-Fock and Density Functional Theory orbitals across a range of molecular systems and TT formats (standard, quantized, and z-permuted quantized). To overcome limitations of current TT solvers, we employ a novel orthogonal tensor train cross approximation (TT-Cross-Orth) to decompose Hartree-Fock and DFT orbitals into TTs, enabling the study of large molecules. We find that the approximation error decreases exponentially with TT-rank for all systems studied and identify QTT as the most efficient TT format. Furthermore, we identify quasi-periodic and symmetric structures-including graphene, graphite layers, and polyalanine helices-as particularly favorable candidates exhibiting sublinear rank growth with system size. The tensor train approach automatically compresses quasi-symmetries and systems with symmetry defects, which makes it an attractive approach for materials science applications. TT-Cross-Orth enforces orthogonality during the decomposition, thereby improving stability and reducing the number of function evaluations compared to standard TT-Cross. These findings establish an empirical foundation for the development of scalable tensor network methods for HF and DFT.
pool.authors: Ruslan A. Mallaev, Dmitry I. Morozov, Dmitry A. Zheltkov, Michael Romanovich Perelshtein, Roman Ellerbrock

pool.title: Latent Style-Based Quantum Wasserstein GAN for Drug Design
pool.abstract: Abstract The development of new drugs is a tedious, time-consuming, and expensive process for which the average costs are estimated to be up to around $2.5 billion. The first step in this long process is the design of the new drug, for which de novo drug design, assisted by artificial intelligence, has blossomed in recent years and has revolutionized the field. In particular, generative artificial intelligence has delivered promising results in drug discovery and development, reducing costs and time to solution. However, classical generative models, such as generative adversarial networks (GANs), can be difficult to train and are prone to mode collapse. Quantum computing may be an avenue to overcome some of these issues, providing compact models with far fewer trainable parameters and thereby enhancing the generalizability of GANs. We propose a new latent style-based quantum Wasserstein GAN (QGAN) for drug design, combining a variational autoencoder that maps molecular structures into a latent space with a hybrid quantum GAN. Our pipeline is benchmarked against the classical models of the industry-relevant MOSES suite. Style-based noise reuploading at every rotational gate and a Wasserstein gradient penalty are used to improve trainability and to mitigate mode collapse. Training and large-scale sampling with circuits of up to 15 qubits are performed on noiseless quantum simulators to validate our architecture. We present an inference-only demonstration on a 156-qubit IBM Heron quantum computer using a five-qubit setup, sampling 2,500 new molecules, to investigate the effect of quantum noise. Our default QGAN, using 110 trainable generator parameters, reaches statistically comparable overall performance and statistically significant gains on selected drug-relevant metrics relative to both the MOSES classical latent GAN baseline, which contains about 700,000 trainable parameters for the generator, and a classical latent GAN with matched generator capacity.

pool.title: Incidence and prevalence of hidradenitis suppurativa across spondyloarthritis-related diseases: cohort study using electronic health records
pool.abstract: Objective To describe the recorded prevalence and incidence of HS across pathologically related diseases within the spondyloarthritis (SpA) family, namely psoriatic arthritis (PsA), psoriasis, axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA), uveitis, Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis, and, for context, rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using electronic health records data between June 2006 and June 2026. ICD codes were used to define populations of SpA-related diseases and RA. We estimated recorded baseline prevalence and crude incidence of HS, then separately performed 1:1 propensity-score matched comparisons of each disease with healthcare controls, matching for age, sex, BMI and comorbidities. Results The disease populations ranged from 55,407 to 429,647 individuals. Recorded HS prevalence was highest in psoriasis (0.65%), PsA (0.52%) and Crohn’s disease (0.47%). Crude incidence was highest in Crohn’s (187.4 per 100,000 person-years) and PsA (134.1 per 100,000 person-years). After matching, incidence was higher than in controls for PsA (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 1.63, 95% CI 1.41-1.88), Crohn’s disease (2.02, 1.85-2.20), and ulcerative colitis (1.17, 1.04-1.32). Incidence was lower than controls in axSpA and RA. Conclusions This study highlights a significant epidemiological association between HS and PsA and Crohn’s disease. Clinicians providing care to these patient groups should consider enquiring about HS symptoms, although overall incidence rates are low. Further research is needed into the shared pathophysiology of HS and psoriatic disease.

pool.title: Hydrogel mechanics across application domains: a regime-based framework for rational design
pool.abstract: Hydrogel technologies have rapidly evolved from simple hydrated materials to multifunctional systems for soft robotics, drug delivery, tissue engineering and surgical simulation. As their complexity increases, designing hydrogels for a specific application requires identifying which mechanical phenomena govern material behaviour under the relevant operating conditions, rather than optimizing individual properties in isolation. In this Review, we propose a regime-based mechanical perspective to organize hydrogel mechanics around the physical mechanisms that dominate under different functional scenarios. After introducing a minimal mechanical framework, we examine representative applications to show how elasticity, swelling, solvent transport, viscoelasticity, fracture and mechanical instabilities become alternatively dominant depending on geometry, loading conditions and characteristic timescales. This approach provides a physical framework for identifying the mechanical aspects that should guide material design in different applications, offering a unified strategy for understanding hydrogel behaviour and supporting the rational development of future multifunctional systems.

pool.title: Comparison of the Photodegradation of Pharmaceuticals and Personal Care Products (PPCPs) in Water and Ice
pool.abstract: Abstract Photochemical reactions are prevalent in natural aquatic environments and play a crucial role in aquatic ecosystems. Sunlight-induced photodegradation is particularly effective in degrading various pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs). However, the photochemical behavior of pollutants within surface ice in cold regions remains unclear. This review synthesizes current research advances regarding the photochemical transformation mechanisms and associated environmental risks of PPCPs in ice, highlighting the significance of these transformations in evaluating the environmental impact of PPCPs in such contexts. In ice or snow, PPCPs may undergo transformation pathways (e.g., photolysis and free radical reactions), which differ from those in aquatic environments. Factors including ice crystal structure, pH, dissolved organic matter, and light conditions can influence their transformation efficiency and the resulting degradation products. This review systematically elucidates the photochemical reaction pathways, key influencing factors, and potential ecotoxicological effects of PPCPs in ice. These transformation processes may generate secondary products that are more persistent or toxic than the parent compounds, posing potential threats to aquatic ecosystems and food chains in cold regions. Therefore, there is an urgent need to thoroughly explore the environmental behavior and ecological risks of PPCPs to provide a scientific basis for pollution control and ecological protection in cold environments.
pool.authors: Liu Jiyang, Wantong Ning, Jiunian Guan, Jize Liu, Xinyi Wang, Wei Li, Baole Guan, Wang Dongming, Tonghui Zhu

pool.title: Progress and Challenges in the Application of CAR T-Cell Therapy for Hematologic Malignancies
pool.abstract: With an aging population and changes in environmental and lifestyle factors, the incidence of hematologic malignancies has been increasing worldwide. Diseases such as leukemia, lymphoma, and multiple myeloma are often characterized by rapid progression and high relapse rates, posing a serious threat to human health. Conventional treatment modalities, including chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and transplantation of hematopoietic stem cells, have demonstrated limited efficacy among individuals with relapsed or refractory hematologic malignancies. Drug resistance, low remission rates, and poor prognosis remain major clinical concerns, underscoring the pressing demand for innovative therapeutic approaches capable of addressing the limitations of current treatments. Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR T-cell) therapy is widely regarded as a significant advancement in the field of cancer immunotherapy. Owing to its precise targeting and potent antitumor activity, CAR T-cell therapy has provided a novel treatment option for individuals affected by relapsed or refractory hematologic malignancies. Based on relevant literature review and inductive analysis, this review offers a comprehensive overview of recent progress regarding the clinical use of CAR T-cell therapy for a range of hematologic malignancies. It focuses on the major challenges associated with clinical application, particularly cytokine release syndrome, tumor immune evasion, and high treatment costs. In addition, current technological improvements and clinical optimization strategies are discussed, and future development trends are explored. Existing evidence indicates that, compared with conventional treatment modalities, CAR T-cell therapy provides clinically meaningful benefits for individuals with relapsed or refractory hematologic malignancies. It can improve remission rates and clinical outcomes and therefore has considerable clinical value. However, several limitations remain, including the risk of serious adverse events, tumor immune evasion, and high costs, all of which substantially hinder its clinical translation and widespread application.
pool.authors: Huiyang Li

pool.title: Explaining adherence to tuberculosis treatment through the information-motivation-behavioral skills model: a PLS - SEM study in Indonesia
pool.abstract: Abstract Background Tuberculosis is a serious public health issue because the success of treatment highly depends on adherence. In Serdang Bedagai, 48.87% of patients were reported to take their medication regularly for a period of less than six months. The purpose of this study was to explore the associations between Information, Motivation, and Behavioral Skills within an adapted IMB measurement model among tuberculosis patients in Serdang Bedagai Regency. Method The research uses an explanatory quantitative approach with a cross-sectional survey design. The sample consisted of 230 tuberculosis patients, category 1 as new patients who have never been treated or have taken Anti-Tuberculosis Drugs (OAT) for less than one month, probability sampling with cluster random sampling technique from six community health centers with high, medium, and low case categories. Data were collected using a Likert Scale questionnaire and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM 3). The measurement model consists of three indicators of Information, three indicators of Motivation, and four indicators of Behavioral Skills. All constructs meet the criteria for reliability and convergent validity, with composite reliability ranging from 0.811 to 0.826 and Average Variance Extracted from 0.523 to 0.614. Results The structural model shows no multicollinearity issues, with a VIF of 1.014. Information and Motivation together explain 8.2% of the variation in Behavioral Skills (R²=0.082), with low but positive predictive relevance (Q²=0.029). Information has a significant negative effect on Behavioral Skills (β=-0.226; t = 3.326; p = 0.001), while Motivation has a significant positive effect (β = 0.151; t = 2.049; p = 0.041). The coefficient of Information is greater than that of Motivation, but the direction of their influence is different, so it cannot be interpreted as a stronger positive influence. Conclusion The adapted IMB measurement model provided exploratory evidence regarding the associations between Information, Motivation, and adherence-related Behavioral Skills among tuberculosis patients. The findings should be interpreted as context-specific structural relationships rather than as evidence that the IMB model fully explains tuberculosis treatment adherence.
pool.authors: Nixson Manurung

pool.title: Fibroblast Activation Protein Inhibitors: Structural Evolution, Binding Mechanisms, and Theranostic Applications in Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography Imaging
pool.abstract: α-Fibroblast activation protein (α-FAP) is overexpressed in cancer-associated fibroblasts within the tumor microenvironment of most epithelial cancers, making it an attractive target for cancer-specific imaging and therapy. This article summarizes the structural features, binding mechanisms, radiolabelling strategies, and clinical potential of FAP inhibitors (FAPIs). FAPI molecules generally consist of three functional modules: a quinoline-based core for target recognition, a linker, and a DOTA/NOTA chelator for radionuclide labelling. The interaction between FAPIs and α-FAP is primarily mediated by several amino acid residues, each engaging a specific structural module of the inhibitor, but residues involved are not fixed and may shift with structural variation among FAPI derivatives. The evolution from early boronic acid compounds to UAMC-1110 marks a transition from non-selective dipeptidyl peptidase inhibitors toward FAP-selective warheads, while later modifications (e.g., cyano to α-ketoamide) addressed the need for prolonged target residence. PET/CT is the combination of functional and structural scanning, increasing diagnostic accuracy. The same targeting principle also enables therapeutic applications when labelled with β-emitting radionuclides. The clear specificity of FAPI also helps overcome many limitations of 18 F-FDG.
pool.authors: 鞠传成

pool.title: Somatic Gene‑Editing Potential and Engineering Barriers for Chronic Cardiovascular Disease Management
pool.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are major chronic health conditions, and some patients require long-term medication to control disease progression and associated risks. The need for more durable treatment has therefore significantly increased, leading to importance to find a more long-lasting treatment strategy. This paper examines the potential of somatic gene editing in the foreseeable future, while evaluating the engineering challenges and ethical limitations. Current research demonstrates the potential of somatic gene editing in vivo to modify disease-associated genetic alterations, providing evidence that gene editing could contribute to more durable CVD treatment. However, off-target effects remain the main safety issue, as an accidental change to unintended DNA regions may lead to lethal biological consequences. In addition, safely and efficiently delivering editing agents is an engineering challenge, as precision and capacity have to be both guaranteed. Furthermore, there are ethical issues regarding genetic diversity and social inequalities due to a feasibility of low accessibility to gene editing therapy. Overall, somatic gene editing shows considerable potential to shift the management of selected chronic CVDs towards more durable, mechanism-based treatment, but significant engineering, safety and ethical barriers must be addressed before it can become a reliable alternative to long-term medication.
pool.authors: Ziya Xu

pool.title: Implementation Methods and Effects of Sephora AI Marketing
pool.abstract: Nowadays, using AI technology to improve efficiency is one of the most important research subjects. Researchers found that Sephora use AI and AR technology to improve the efficiency of shopping. However, the reason behind efficiency improvements and their broader implication is not been unified. Therefore, this study collects data, including sales growth and so on, and compare it with initial data to examine how the adoption of these technologies enhancing Sephora's operational efficiency. According to the survey, AI technology has as well as enhanced sales efficiency and the experience of consumers transformed the structure of rights and the relationship between AI and consumers. These positive impacts demonstrate that Sephora must continue to use these technologies and refine them further. Besides, these advanced technologies may lead to data privacy leakage and declining consumer trust issues as well. Therefore, solving these issues has also become part of Sephora's efforts to refine these technologies.

pool.title: Effects of growth media modulation on cytotoxicity, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities of postbiotic metabolites produced by Lactiplantibacillus plantarum I-UL4
pool.abstract: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum I-UL4 produces various postbiotic metabolites with known anticancer and antioxidant activities, but its anti-inflammatory effect remains unclear. In this study, we compared postbiotic metabolites produced by L. plantarum I-UL4 with commercial de Man, Rogosa and Sharpe (MRS) medium (PMM) and a reported refined formulation (PMF) for their volatile compound profiles, cytotoxicity, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects on LPS-stimulated THP-1 leukaemia cells. Volatile compound profiling was performed by GC–MS and cytotoxicity was determined by 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium Bromide assay. Subsequently, antioxidant effects were determined for cellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels (DCFDA assay) and inflammatory responses at the gene (nuclear factor kappa B, cyclooxygenase-2, IL-6, IL-18, TNF-α, IL-1β and IL-10) and protein levels via qPCR and cytokine antibody arrays. GC–MS analysis revealed that L. plantarum I-UL4 produced distinct volatile compound profiles from MRS and refined formulation media. Nonetheless, lactic acid predominating (≈ 89–92% peak area), alongside other unique bioactive compounds in PMM and PMF, as compared to MRS and the refined formulation media. Notably, PMM was more cytotoxic, with the lowest IC 50 (2.57 ± 0.2) at 72 h. Interestingly, both PMF and PMM reduced ROS levels at 48 h. Importantly, PMF showed significantly stronger ( P < 0.05) anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting nuclear factor kappa B and cyclooxygenase-2 and simultaneously modulating both pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokine genes and protein expression compared with PMM, suggesting that PMF could be a promising biotic preparation for modulating inflammation-related diseases. In conclusion, this study reveals how fermentation media affect the volatile composition, bioactivity and functionality of postbiotic metabolites, including cytotoxicity, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities.
pool.authors: Aniqa Rehman, Ming Xuan Cho, Adelene Ai Lian Song, Norazalina Saad, Suet Lin Chia, Teck Chwen Loh, Rina Wu, Hooi Ling Foo

pool.title: Research on Multi-source Data Fusion Quality Risk Prediction Model for Drug Registration Compliance
pool.abstract: Drug registration compliance management faces practical challenges such as complex submission documents, dispersed risk sources, and diversified review stages. Traditional manual review methods have difficulty identifying potential quality risks in a timely manner, especially when cumulative risk is formed by cross source, cross stage, and cross type information. Against this background, a multi source data fusion quality risk prediction model was developed for the drug registration scenario. The model integrated submission and review texts, historical deficiency records, inspection results, manufacturing change information, and regulatory provisions. Unified preprocessing, feature extraction, fusion modeling, and stratified training were then applied to achieve risk level identification. The results showed that the multi source fusion model outperformed single source models in Accuracy, Recall, F1, and AUC. Among them, the fusion XGBoost model achieved the best overall performance and significantly reduced the miss rate of high risk cases. The interpretability analysis further indicated that historical deficiency frequency, regulatory terminology deviation rate, abnormal inspection ratio, and manufacturing change density were the key factors affecting risk judgment. This study provides a computable, verifiable, and early warning oriented technical path for drug registration compliance management, and offers more targeted digital support for enterprise pre review and regulatory assisted assessment.
pool.authors: Zhenzhen Huang, Huan Gao

pool.title: Quantitative systems pharmacology modeling of class I–III BRAF-mutant NSCLC enables subgroup treatment analysis and combination therapy design
pool.abstract: BRAF-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) comprises three functional classes (I–III) with distinct driving mechanisms, yet effective therapies for classes II and III remain limited. To address this, we developed a quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model that mechanistically recapitulates signaling networks and drug responses across all three classes, integrating multiscale preclinical-to-clinical datasets. The model enabled high-throughput prediction of clinical efficacy for monotherapies and combination therapies across diverse dosing regimens, and we identified that combining MEK and ERK inhibition represents a novel strategy for class II/III mutants, validated by original in vivo MiniPDX data using NSCLC patient tumors. Simulations further revealed that only triple blockade of EGFR, IGF1R, and FGFR pathway initiation can potently reduce tumor growth and overcome resistance in these classes. Our work is the first multiscale QSP platform mechanistically addressing class I–III BRAF mutations at the systems level for disease-centric translational combination therapy discovery and precision medicine design.
pool.authors: Jingjing Hu, Qi Rao, Zichun Li, Geli Li, Zhenle Bi, Danyi Wen, Chen Zhao, Guohua Zhou

pool.title: Solarisation of rural primary health centres for reducing healthcare delays in Karnataka India using grounded theory
pool.abstract: The Primary Health Centres (PHCs) are vital for achieving universal health coverage; however, energy poverty remains a critical yet overlooked barrier to the efficiency of primary healthcare services in rural and remote settings. This study explored the community’s perspective on healthcare services before and after solarisation and how it has impacted service availability, healthcare utilisation, and improved health outcomes. We conducted a qualitative study employing the grounded theory methodology in Karnataka, India. Six focus group discussions (FGDs) were conducted among 36 rural community members – 21 women and 15 men. The FGDs were digitally recorded, transcribed and translated into English and analysed using MAXQDA software. A conceptual model was developed using all categories. The findings revealed that solarisation of PHCs acts as a catalyst for reducing healthcare delays. A cascade of better decision-making and improved resource use resulted in actual improvements in service utilisation and care delivery. Key results include faster admission and treatment initiation, a lower risk of complications, and improved patient safety and satisfaction. The use of solar energy in healthcare facilities has increased service quality, accessibility, and community trust, especially in maternal and child health. Solar electrification enhances healthcare quality and community trust, improving service utilisation and health outcomes. Future research should integrate digital health and evaluate cost-effectiveness for scalable, sustainable solar electrification models in rural areas.

pool.title: Mechanisms and Biomedical Applications of Sustained- and Controlled-Release Drug Delivery Systems
pool.abstract: Sustained‑release and controlled‑release drug carriers represent valuable pharmaceutical tools that help boost treatment outcomes while simplifying clinical medication schemes. Unlike conventional immediate‑release tablets and capsules, these systems can moderate or adjust how active pharmaceutical ingredients get released inside organisms. Such features extend therapeutic action durations and lower daily dosing frequencies. This review sorts out core definitions and distinguishing traits of sustained‑release and controlled‑release dosage forms, alongside common product categories and their underlying release mechanisms. Three widely adopted technical solutions are discussed: matrix‑type, membrane‑coated and osmotic‑pump tablet systems. The text addresses their clinical strengths including stable in‑vivo drug levels, reduced dosing frequency and enhanced patient adherence. Real‑world clinical applications covering cardiovascular illnesses, metabolic syndromes and pain management are also summarized. Collectively, sustained‑release and controlled‑release technologies offer feasible pathways to optimize drug delivery and therapeutic performance. Further research into novel excipient materials and delivery techniques is likely to achieve more accurate drug release behaviours and expand the scope of clinical use for such formulations.

pool.title: Inverse probability weighting-based mediation analysis for microbiome data
pool.abstract: Abstract Motivation Mediation analysis is an important tool for elucidating causal mechanisms in biomedical research and has recently gained increasing attention in microbiome studies. Motivated by a microbiome study of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, we investigate whether the effect of induction chemotherapy intensity on infection status is mediated through gut microbial taxa. This problem poses substantial methodological challenges due to the high dimensionality, zero inflation, and dependence of microbial mediators, as well as the presence of an exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounder, antibiotic use. Results To address these challenges, we propose a novel nonparametric identification formula for the interventional indirect effect, a causal mediation estimand that remains identifiable in the presence of exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounding. Building on this identification result, we develop an inverse probability weighting estimator and construct standard normal bootstrap confidence intervals for inference. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate effect estimation and maintains appropriate type I error rates and power in finite samples. Application to the AML microbiome study provides evidence of a statistically significant interventional indirect effect of induction chemotherapy intensity on infection risk through alterations in the gut microbiome. Availability and implementation The R code for the simulation studies is available at https://github.com/YX-ZHANG-1/CausalMediationMicrobiome and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21960802.

pool.title: Integrative analysis reveals gut microbiota-associated host regulatory networks in liver fibrosis
pool.abstract: Background Gut microbiota-derived metabolites may contribute to liver fibrosis by affecting host inflammatory, metabolic, and epigenetic pathways. We aimed to identify microbiota-associated host genes shared across liver fibrosis of different etiologies. Methods Microbiota- and metabolite-associated host genes were obtained from gutMGene v2.0 and integrated with differentially expressed genes from two human liver transcriptomic datasets: GSE84044 for HBV-related fibrosis and GSE49541 for NAFLD-related fibrosis. Shared genes were analyzed using protein–protein interaction and functional enrichment analyses. Selected metabolite–protein interactions were assessed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. Two-sample Mendelian randomization was used to examine potential associations between candidate gene expression and liver fibrosis risk. Results Fourteen microbiota-associated genes were differentially expressed in both fibrosis cohorts, including CCL2, CCL20, CXCL6, PTGS2, HDAC2, HDAC3, ADRA2A, SOD1, PEMT, and GNMT. These genes were mainly associated with chemokine activity, histone deacetylation, and IL-17 and TNF signaling. Molecular docking suggested structural compatibility between phenylacetylglutamine and ADRA2A, while butyrate showed weaker predicted interactions with HDAC2 and HDAC3.Molecular dynamics analysis supported the stability of the ADRA2A–phenylacetylglutamine complex under the simulated conditions. Mendelian randomization identified nominal associations of HDAC3, CCL2, PTGS2, and VCL expression with liver fibrosis risk. Conclusions This study identified shared microbiota-associated host regulatory candidates in HBV- and NAFLD-related liver fibrosis.HDAC3 and ADRA2A may represent potential links between microbial metabolic signals and fibrotic responses, although further experimental validation is required.

pool.title: The Heart Under Viral Attack: From Infection and Vaccination to Myocardial Injury
pool.abstract: Chronic heart failure remains a major global burden, with respiratory viral infections frequently precipitating hospitalisation and mortality.Viral myocarditis has emerged as a significant contributor to cardiac dysfunction, driven by both direct cytopathic effects and immune-mediated pathways.This review synthesises contemporary experimental and clinical evidence on the molecular mechanisms by which cardiotropic viruses-including Coxsackievirus B, herpesviruses (HHV 6, EBV, CMV), parvovirus B19, influenza viruses and SARS CoV 2damage the myocardium, with particular emphasis on the roles of Toll like receptors, viral proteases and the pro inflammatory cytokines TNF α, IL 6 and IL 1β.These cytokines exert negative inotropic actions, promote cardiomyocyte apoptosis and disrupt extracellular matrix homeostasis, thereby contributing to adverse ventricular remodelling and heart failure progression.The review also examines the veterinary legacy of coronavirus vaccine development, which has been largely overlooked in human cardiology.For over half a century, veterinary medicine has confronted coronaviruses as devastating livestock pathogens, accumulating extensive knowledge of vaccine platforms, viral mutation and immune escape mechanisms that proved instrumental in expediting the creation of mRNA vaccines against COVID 19.Importantly, the review appraises the cardiac safety profile of these vaccines, concluding that the incidence of vaccine associated myocarditis-predominantly observed in young males after the second dose-is substantially lower than the risk of myocarditis following natural SARS CoV 2 infection.Although rare, post vaccination cardiac complications warrant ongoing surveillance and mechanistic research.Overall, this comprehensive overview underscores the convergence of infectious disease, immunology and vaccinology in shaping our understanding of virus related heart disease, while highlighting the translational value of veterinary research.Future investigations should focus on identifying individual susceptibility factors and developing targeted strategies to mitigate both viral and vaccine induced myocardial injury, thereby improving outcomes for patients with or at risk of heart failure.

pool.title: A Review of Driver Gene Co-mutations in Prognostic Stratification of Targeted Therapy for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
pool.abstract: EGFR-TKIs have significantly improved the survival outcomes of patients with EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, substantial heterogeneity in treatment efficacy exists among individuals, and conventional single-gene testing has limitations in guiding therapeutic decision-making. This systematic review focuses on the effects of driver gene co-mutations on the prognosis of targeted therapy in EGFR-mutant NSCLC and explores their value in clinical translation. Literature published from 2022 to 2026 concerning co-mutations and prognosis of targeted therapy in EGFR-mutant NSCLC was systematically retrieved from the PubMed database for summarization and analysis. This review found that TP53 is the most prevalent co-mutated gene in EGFR-mutant NSCLC and is strongly associated with poor prognosis under TKI monotherapy. Phase III clinical trials have confirmed that TKI combined with chemotherapy significantly prolongs median progression-free survival compared with TKI monotherapy among patients with EGFR mutations accompanied by tumor suppressor gene co-mutations. NGS multi-gene panels serve as the technical foundation for comprehensive co-mutation assessment. In summary, driver gene co-mutations play a critical role in prognostic stratification for EGFR-mutant NSCLC treatment. Taking co-mutation status into account helps identify high-risk patients who may benefit from intensified treatment, supporting more precise and individualized targeted therapy.
pool.authors: Yun Feng

pool.title: Ultrasound stimulation of hindlimb skeletal muscle is associated with selective differences in splenic metabolites during hindlimb unloading in mice
pool.abstract: Physical inactivity and unloading induce skeletal muscle atrophy and systemic metabolic and immune dysregulation. We examined associations of skeletal muscle ultrasound (US) stimulation with splenic metabolite profiles and explored plasma extracellular particle (EP) characteristics in a hindlimb unloading (HU) model. Male C57BL/6J mice were assigned to control, HU, or HU with US stimulation (HUUS). Blood, gastrocnemius, and spleen were collected for particle analysis, transcriptomics, histology, and metabolomics. HU and HUUS had lower body weight, gastrocnemius weight, spleen weight, and muscle fiber cross-sectional area than control. Exploratory analysis showed numerically higher particle concentrations in polymer-precipitated plasma EP-containing fractions in HUUS than in HU, although the difference was not statistically significant ( p = 0.050). In gastrocnemius muscle, gene sets for endoplasmic reticulum protein processing and proteostasis were positively enriched in HUUS versus HU. In the spleen, HU showed nominally higher upstream glycolytic intermediates and nominally lower flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD), whereas erythrose 4-phosphate (E4P) and GDP were lower and cis-aconitate was higher after FDR correction. Compared with HU, HUUS showed lower glucose 1-phosphate (G1P) after FDR correction and nominal differences in F6P, fumarate, and FAD. Overall, US stimulation under HU conditions was associated with pathway-level transcriptional remodeling and selective splenic metabolite differences.

pool.title: Beyond reconstruction: minimally invasive aesthetic and regenerative medicine in postoperative oral and maxillofacial surgery
pool.abstract: PURPOSE: Oral and maxillofacial reconstruction restores anatomical continuity and function after tumor resection, trauma and congenital deformity, yet patients frequently remain affected by fibrosis, scar tethering, impaired oral competence, asymmetry and altered dynamic facial function. These deficits can impair quality of life, social interaction and body image. Conventional revision surgery carries additional morbidity, and minimally invasive options have emerged as a postoperative adjunct. This article reviews how minimally invasive aesthetic and regenerative medicine can extend reconstructive rehabilitation in oral and maxillofacial surgery. METHODS: Current biological and clinical evidence for polynucleotides (PN), hyaluronic acid (HA) and botulinum toxin A (BoNT-A) was reviewed and integrated with selected, non-consecutive illustrative cases from a dedicated aesthetic and regenerative consultation in an academic oral and maxillofacial surgery department. Clinical applications were illustrated across four patient categories: oncological, congenital, trauma/scar and aesthetic-functional sequelae after surgery. RESULTS: In illustrative cases from different categories, a staged approach of tissue conditioning, structural restoration and dynamic neuromodulation was associated with clinically observed and patient-reported improvements in scar pliability, tissue gliding, oral competence, dynamic symmetry and quality of life. PN were used primarily for regenerative tissue conditioning, HA for reversible structural restoration, and BoNT-A to modulate muscular imbalance and pathological wound tension. As interventions were frequently combined and no validated outcome measures or controls were used, these observations are hypothesis-generating. CONCLUSION: Minimally invasive regenerative and aesthetic treatment may serve as a functional extension of reconstruction rather than a cosmetic adjunct. The central concept is not volumisation, but restoration of tissue quality, dynamic balance and facial function. Prospective studies using validated functional, scar and patient-reported outcome measures are required to define its role in modern oral and maxillofacial surgery.
