pool.title: The Regulation of Adaptive Immunity by Vitamin D and Its Potential Role in Autoimmune Diseases
pool.abstract: Besides regulating calcium and phosphate in the body, vitamin D also has some immunomodulatory effects. Some subsets of immune cells have the necessary parts for Vitamin D signalling, such as the Vitamin D receptor (VDR) and local activation enzymes. Connect the system to adaptive immunity in this paper and cover T-cell differentiation, regulatory T cells, B-cell responses, etc.; also discuss the influence of vitamin D deficiency. Then it will consider the proof of multiple sclerosis (MS), type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Mechanistic and observational studies have shown that vitamin D is associated with the immune system. The clinical supplementation literature is not uniform. All the results of these studies are different, and currently, no particular disease-modifying treatment for deficiency has been found. Good trials still need to be carried out to determine when supplementation is effective, what the suitable dose is, and which patients will benefit most.
pool.authors: Yihan Yu

pool.title: “Our patients deserve better”—roadblocks to optimal care in biliary malignancies
pool.abstract: Biliary tract cancers (BTCs) are associated with poor outcomes, with many patients never receiving any cancer-directed treatment. Population-based registries from England, France, Italy and Spain share a similar picture: emergency presentation, rather than planned referral, accounts for roughly half of diagnoses, and >50% of patients with cholangiocarcinoma in England received neither surgery, systemic therapy nor stenting. This attrition is not exclusive to real-world settings: in PROOF-301 and FIGHT-302, a considerable proportion of eligible or randomly assigned patients never started their allocated treatment. BTC is also no longer a disease confined to older adults, with ∼7% of cases diagnosed in individuals <50 years of age. On top of this, access to reimbursed therapies, molecular profiling and expert multidisciplinary discussion remains markedly uneven across Europe. "Our patients deserve better" and closing these gaps in diagnosis, access to treatment and care delivery is as urgent as developing new drugs for this disease.
pool.authors: Ángela Lamarca, Ismael Macías, Marina Crespo Cruz, Antonella Cammarota, L. Rimassa, John A. Bridgewater

pool.title: mRNA Lipid Nanoparticle Delivery Systems: Composition, Optimization and Advances in Clinical Translation
pool.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNP) represent critical non‑viral carriers for mRNA delivery, capable of encapsulating, protecting mRNA, facilitating cellular uptake and enabling cytosolic release. This review summarizes the composition and delivery mechanisms of mRNA‑LNP. Optimization strategies including ionizable lipid structure, component ratio tuning, endosomal escape improvement and tissue‑targeted modification are analysed in depth. Its applications in vaccines, tumour therapy, protein replacement and gene‑editing are further outlined. Current bottlenecks contain limited endosomal‑escape efficiency, insufficient extra‑hepatic delivery, safety concerns for repeated administration, and consistency challenges in large‑scale manufacturing. Future efforts should focus on lipid‑structure and formulation optimization, alongside improved safety evaluation and quality‑control frameworks to accelerate clinical translation.
pool.authors: Peidong Shi

pool.title: Genetic landscape of paediatric channelopathies and cardiomyopathies in Hong Kong
pool.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cardiac channelopathies and cardiomyopathies are important causes of sudden cardiac death. The genetic background of these conditions in Asian paediatric populations has rarely been reported. This study aimed to report the genetic underpinnings of these conditions in patients treated at a single tertiary paediatric cardiac centre in Hong Kong. METHODS: All patients diagnosed with cardiac channelopathy or cardiomyopathy who underwent genetic testing in our cardiology centre between 2007 and 2022 were included in this cohort study. Phenotype classification, genetic testing methodologies, and results were reviewed. Genetic yields were assessed. RESULTS: In total, 165 probands were identified. Ninety-four probands carried at least one pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variant (57.0%), whereas 27 probands (16.4%) had only variants of uncertain significance (VUS). Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in 58 patients with channelopathy (63.7%) and 36 patients with cardiomyopathy (48.6%), including 22 novel variants (16 P/LP variants and 6 VUS). The yield of P/LP variants was highest in catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (81.8%). The clinical features of selected probands with significant mortality or morbidity were described in relation to variant details. The yield of subsequent cascade genetic screening among first-degree relatives was 27.3%. CONCLUSION: This study describes the genetic landscape of paediatric cardiac channelopathies and cardiomyopathies at a single tertiary paediatric cardiology centre in Hong Kong. The findings facilitated genotype-guided management and enabled identification of at-risk family members for the prevention of sudden cardiac death.

pool.title: Genetic profile of P. falciparum strains in villages around Soum irrigation Dam, Burkina Faso: insights from targeted sequencing of drug resistance markers in Pfkelch13, Pfubp1, Pfcoronin, Pfcrt, Pfmdr1, Pfdhps and Pfdhfr genes
pool.abstract: Abstract Hydro-agricultural settings may sustain high and prolonged malaria transmission and increase antimalarial drug use, potentially intensifying selection pressure on P. falciparum strains. Molecular surveillance in these settings is essential to detect changes in markers associated with resistance to artemisinin, Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (SP), and Artemisinin-Based Combination Therapy (ACT) partner drugs. This study characterized the genetic profile and seasonal distribution of P. falciparum strains circulating in villages surrounding the Soum irrigation dam in Burkina Faso. A prospective monitoring approach was implemented through monthly repeated cross-sectional household surveys in five villages around the Soum dam in the Nanoro health district from March 2022 to February 2023. Dried blood spots from microscopy-positive samples were randomly selected by village and transmission season. Illumina technology was used to sequence molecular markers of partial resistance to artemisinin ( Pfkelch13 , Pfcoronin , Pfubp1 ), Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine ( Pfdhfr , Pfdhps ), and Artemisinin-Based Combination therapy (ACT) partner drugs ( Pfmdr1 , Pfcrt ). Allele and haplotype prevalences were compared across villages, transmission seasons, and age groups using chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests, as appropriate. A total of 712 P. falciparum -positive samples were selected for the sample size for molecular analysis. No validated or candidate mutations associated with artemisinin partial resistance were detected in Pfkelch13 and Pfcoronin. Pfubp1 D1525E and E1528D mutations, suspected to be associated with delayed parasite clearance, were each detected at 18.5% and 19.1%, respectively. Mutant alleles of Pfdhfr , including 51 I (73.7%), 59 R (88.6%) and 108 N (91.4%), were highly prevalent. In Pfdhps , the mutant 437 G allele was highly detected (88.4%), whereas 431 V , 540 E and 581 G occurred at low frequencies (< 2%). No significant variation was found between villages and transmission season for Pfdhfr and Pfdhps ( p > 0.05). The wildtype 86 N allele of Pfmdr1 was predominant (95.2%), while mutant allele 184 F (49.31%) was higher and differed significantly between villages ( p = 0.029) with the highest frequency in Séguédin (57.4%) and the lowest in Soala (40.5%). The Pfcrt wildtype CVMNK haplotype (97.4%) remained dominant. This study found no validated Pfkelch13 mutation and no candidate Pfcoronin mutation associated with artemisinin partial resistance. However, the emergence of D1525E and E1528D mutations of Pfubp1 may suggest early signals adaptation of P. falciparum to artemisinin in the study area. The relatively high and expected frequency of Pfdhfr and Pfdhps without significant variations between villages and transmission period suggests homogeneous circulation of these mutations across the study area and reflects continued pressure of SP. The emerging Pfdhps 431 V and 540 E and high frequency of Pfmdr1 184 F allele reinforced the need for regular surveillance to anticipate any resistance of SP and Lumefantrine.

pool.title: Adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomal miR-22-3p alleviates depression-like behaviors in a rat model via the FURIN/HMGB1 axis
pool.abstract: Background Major depressive disorder (MDD) is characterized by neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis, yet effective brain-targeted delivery strategies remain limited. Exosomes represent promising carriers capable of crossing the blood–brain barrier. This study investigated whether engineered exosomes delivering miR-22-3p by modulating the FURIN/HMGB1 axis. Methods Serum microRNA expression was assessed in patients with MDD. A rat model of depression was established using chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). miR-22-3p-engineered adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell exosomes were administered intranasally. Behavioral tests (SPT, OFT, FST), RT-qPCR, ELISA, HE staining, and TUNEL assays were performed to evaluate neurobehavioral and molecular changes. Results miR-22-3p was significantly downregulated in both MDD patients and CUMS rats (P < 0.01). Intranasal administration of engineered exosomes increased brain miR-22-3p levels and significantly improved depressive-like behaviors (P < 0.05 or P < 0.01). Mechanistically, treatment suppressed FURIN and HMGB1 expression, reduced proinflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α), and attenuated hippocampal neuronal apoptosis (P < 0.05 or P < 0.01). These effects were more pronounced than those of native exosomes. Conclusions miR-22-3p-engineered exosomes exert antidepressant effects by inhibiting the FURIN/HMGB1-mediated neuroinflammatory and apoptotic pathways. This study highlights a novel intranasal exosome-based microRNA delivery strategy for MDD.
pool.authors: Yuxin Xu, 游艳秋, Dekai Wei, Rong Liang, Weiping Liang, Bingzheng Feng, Jibing Chen, Jia Liang, Fujun Li

pool.title: Laboratory Diagnosis of Cancer: Integration of Conventional Methods, Precision Medicine, and Their Impact on Public Health Systems
pool.abstract: Laboratory diagnosis of cancer is a key component of early detection, prognosis assessment, and therapeutic decisionmaking in oncology.In middle-income countries such as Ecuador, limited access to screening programs and advanced diagnostic technologies remains a significant challenge for cancer control, particularly affecting early detection.This study critically reviewed both traditional methods and the most recent tools applied to the diagnosis of breast, prostate, and cervical cancer-neoplasms that account for a significant proportion of national morbidity and mortality.To this end, studies published in both international and national databases were analyzed, including original research, reviews, and clinical guidelines focused on diagnostic performance.The findings show that widely used tests such as mammography, prostate markers, and cervical cytology remain fundamental in screening, although they have limitations in the early stages; in contrast, the use of molecular biomarkers, more advanced imaging techniques, and computational tools has improved the accuracy and identification of clinically relevant lesions.Rather than relying on a single approach, the strengthening of cancer diagnosis in the Ecuadorian context is based on the interaction and complementarity of these tools.

pool.title: Public Service Decline and Support for the Populist Right: Evidence from England’s National Health Service
pool.abstract: The rise of populist right parties is well-studied, but relatively little attention has been given to how public service performance influences voter support. Given that public services are often the primary means through which citizens interact with the state, we argue that declining public services can create grievances that increase the appeal of populist right parties. Focusing on England’s National Health Service (NHS), we combine administrative data on local health facility closures with panel data on public preferences and voting intentions. Using a staggered difference-in-differences design, we find that closures reduce satisfaction with public services and increase support for populist right parties. These effects are moderated by migrant registrations at local health practices, highlighting the interaction between public service performance and immigration concerns in fueling populist right support. Our findings underscore the role of public service decline as a driver of support for populist parties, especially in areas undergoing demographic change.
pool.authors: Z. Dickson, SARA BINZER HOBOLT, Catherine E. De Vries, Simone Cremaschi

pool.title: Giant spin-to-charge conversion by tailoring magnetically proximitized topological Dirac semimetal
pool.abstract: While ferromagnet and topological material bilayers are widely studied to obtain efficient spin charge conversion via topological surface states (TSS), the influence of the magnetic proximity effect (MPE) on the TSS evolution and conversion efficiency remains poorly understood. In this study, we experimentally probe and reveal the behavior of spin momentum locked TSS through spin pumping measurements in heterostructures composed of ferromagnetic Fe and the topological Dirac semimetal alpha Sn. As the alpha Sn thickness (tSn) increases from 9 to 35 nm, the Gilbert damping constant of the Fe layer exhibits a pronounced peak at tSn = 25 nm, followed by a decrease at greater thicknesses. Our rigorous theoretical analysis, combining analytical modeling and first principles calculations, attributes this behavior to the TSS disappearance at the Fe and alpha Sn interface and exchange gap opening on the opposite surface, both induced by the long range MPE and its influence on the spin charge conversion efficiency. At tSn = 25 nm, we demonstrate highly efficient spin charge conversion with an inverse Edelstein length of 3.14 nm, the highest value reported at room temperature for ferromagnet and topological material bilayers. These findings underscore the critical role of tuning TSS properties under MPE for advancing topological materials in spintronic applications.
pool.authors: Masayuki Ishida, Soichiro Fukuoka, Takahiro Chiba, Yohei Kota, Masaaki Tanaka, Lê Đức Anh

pool.title: Emergence of a symmetry-broken Chern insulator near a moire Kondo breakdown
pool.abstract: Moiré semiconductors built on angle-aligned transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterobilayers provide a physical realization of the Kondo lattice model, in which one TMD layer is prepared in a Mott insulating state supporting a lattice of local magnetic moments and the other layer in a metallic state supporting itinerant carriers. The artificial Kondo lattice enables the exploration of exotic states of matter near a continuously tunable Kondo breakdown. Here we report the emergence of a symmetry-broken Chern insulator at a moiré hole filling factor 4/3 in angle-aligned MoTe2/WSe2 moiré bilayers, which realize a chiral Kondo lattice. The symmetry-broken Chern insulator, which exhibits integer quantized Hall conductance at a fractional moiré filling, breaks the translational symmetry of the lattice spontaneously; it also appears only near a magnetic field-induced Kondo breakdown in the mixed-valence regime of the material. We further demonstrate that the magnetic field required to induce the Kondo breakdown and to stabilize the symmetry-broken Chern insulator is twist angle dependent. The results present new opportunities for exploring the subtle interplay between topology and Kondo interactions in moiré semiconductors.
pool.authors: W.B. Tian, Bowen Shen, Lizhong Li, Mingjie Zhang, Feng Liu, Chushan Li, Yaotian Liu, Fan Xu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Peiling Li, Li Lu, Yang Xu, Shengwei Jiang, Tingxin Li, Jie Shan, Kin Fai Mak

pool.title: Hunting dark matter with the Einstein Telescope
pool.abstract: Too light primordial black holes evaporate and are therefore strongly constrained by various bounds, e.g. Cosmic Microwave Background distortion. However, if they are formed strongly clustered, the corresponding haloes may collapse in heavier black holes which may form the entirety of the dark matter of the universe. The indirect signal of such scenario is the production of a flat stochastic background of gravitational waves which is detectable by the Einstein Telescope.
pool.authors: A. J. Iovino, Michele Maggiore, Niccolò Muttoni, Antonio Walter Riotto

pool.title: New operational perspective to identify aerosols and hydrometeors in real-time with a pioneering algorithm (CONIOPOL) based on single-wavelength polarization lidar (CL61)
pool.abstract: Abstract. Air quality monitoring and climate studies require continuous, vertically resolved observations to characterize aerosols and their impact on radiation, cloud microphysics, and atmospheric composition. In this study, we present CONIOPOL (CONIOlogy + POLarization), an automated depolarization-based classification algorithm developed with the polarized Automatic Lidar Ceilometer (ALC), CL61 (Vaisala Oyi, FIN) installed at Uccle, Belgium. The algorithm combines linear depolarization ratio (LDR), attenuated backscatter, and cloud-base height retrievals to distinguish between aerosols, clouds, and precipitation, and to further classify aerosol subtypes. One full year (February 2024–January 2025) of observations was analyzed to retrieve and evaluate the seasonal and vertical distributions of major aerosol categories, with results compared against Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) model forecast outputs. The CONIOPOL algorithm successfully identified different types of aerosol – including dust, smoke, hygroscopic, and mixed aerosols – demonstrating strong temporal and vertical coherence with CAMS simulations. In particular, dust and smoke plumes detected above 1000 m showed a good agreement with it. Despite its spectral limitations, the single-wavelength lidar provides continuous, high-resolution, and climatologically consistent aerosol classification, offering valuable insights into the seasonal evolution of aerosol types over mid-latitude Europe. These findings underscore the potential of depolarization-capable ALCs for long-term aerosol and air quality climatology, bridging temporal gaps between satellite, in situ, and multi-wavelength lidar observations.
pool.authors: Quentin Laffineur, Alexander Mangold, Andy Delcloo

pool.title: Temperate marine macrophytes are highly variable sources of Biogenic Volatile Organic Compounds – a comparative study from the Baltic Sea and NE Atlantic
pool.abstract: Abstract. Biogenic Volatile Organic Compounds (BVOC), emitted by Earth’s ecosystems, affect several chemical processes in the atmosphere that have profound climate impacts. Despite their climate relevance, global BVOC budget estimations are still highly uncertain, with ocean-derived emissions being particularly poorly constrained. Marine macrophytes (i.e. macroalgae and seagrass) are a large and widespread organismal group whose BVOC emission rates are particularly poorly quantified. In this study, we set out to address this knowledge gap by quantifying ex situ the BVOC emission rates of three temperate macrophytes (Zostera marina, Fucus vesiculosus and Ulva intestinalis) with a Vocus proton-transfer-reaction time-of-flight mass spectrometer (Vocus PTR-TOF). To capture and improve our understanding of the variability of macrophyte BVOC emissions, our quantifications were repeated across two contrasting coastal regions: the northeastern Atlantic (Ireland) and northern Baltic Sea (Finland). The three macrophytes emitted a wide range of BVOCs, with a total of 166 different compounds detected. Although many BVOCs were emitted by all macrophytes, significant differences were observed in the total emission profiles, both between and within species. Interestingly, the seagrass Zostera exhibited significantly higher overall BVOC emission rates per unit biomass than the two macroalgae and showed clearly differing intraspecific emission profiles across the two regions. Regarding individual compounds, dimethyl sulfide (DMS) was emitted at the highest rates, but many other compounds (e.g., sesquiterpenes and C10H21O+) also displayed notable emission rates. Although many of the observed BVOCs are commonly investigated compounds (e.g., DMS and terpenoids), our results show that macrophyte BVOC emissions comprise a large number of different compounds, suggesting that future studies would benefit from targeting a wider range of BVOCs than currently considered. Our results highlight macrophytes as highly variable sources of BVOCs, whose better inclusion into marine BVOC budgets should be strived for. However, more robust data are needed, and future research should also focus on investigating the dynamics driving macrophyte BVOC emissions, their variability, and their eventual fate in the environment.
pool.authors: Max L. E. Gräfnings, Yuanyuan Luo, Jian Zhao, Claudia L. Cara-Ortega, Kirsten N. Fossum, Frans Graeffe, Lu Lei, Dagmar Brigitte Stengel, Roseline C. Thakur, Jurgita Ovadnevaitė, Mikael Ehn, Camilla Gustafsson

pool.title: Seismic background mitigation with the Lunar Gravitational-wave Antenna
pool.abstract: Lunar gravitational-wave (GW) detectors relying on the measurement of the response of the Moon to GWs are susceptible to a seismic background, which might pose a fundamental sensitivity limitation. The Lunar Gravitational-wave Antenna (LGWA) was conceived as an array of accelerometers with the idea that data can be processed to distinguish between a GW signal and the seismic background. As a result, the seismic noise of the GW measurement would be mitigated. However, so far, no quantitative assessment of the mitigation of the seismic background has been provided. In this article, we derive the analytical expressions for the optimal squared signal-to-noise ratio considering two seismic stations in an isotropic, random, Gaussian seismic field. Our numerical analysis reveals that the capacity to mitigate the seismic noise critically depends on the distance between the two stations relative to the seismic-correlation length. We demonstrate that optimal placement of the two stations can yield significant improvements in the equivalent seismic noise amplitude spectrum density (ASD), approximately a factor of 2.3 at 0.3 Hz, compared to the measurement with a single station. The equivalent ASD of the seismic noise also exhibits distinct oscillatory and mitigation features arising from the Bessel-function structure of the noise correlation.
pool.authors: Han Yan, Jan Harms

pool.title: Massively Degenerate Coherent Perfect Absorption in Gradient‐Index Fibers
pool.abstract: ABSTRACT Coherent perfect absorbers (CPAs) enable even weakly absorbing materials to achieve complete absorption by exploiting interference. Generalizing this to arbitrary multimode input states remains challenging, because conventional implementations work only for a single or very few input channels. Here, a compact multimode coherent perfect absorber based on a gradient‐index (GRIN) fiber is proposed, in which the self‐imaging property of the fiber replaces the bulky free‐space architecture of previous approaches. Unlike a free‐space self‐imaging cavity, a realistic fiber cannot be exactly degenerate, raising the question of how much modal degeneracy such a device requires. An analytic relation is derived linking the residual modal phase spread directly to the field‐of‐view reflectivity. Absorption survives as long as the modal dephasing remains small compared with the coupling bandwidth of the cavity, so that residual dephasing imposes an upper bound on the usable cavity finesse – a design constraint absent in the free‐space case. Applying this criterion shows that GRIN profiles optimized for minimal intermodal group‐delay dispersion, a condition derived for pulse transport, simultaneously optimize monochromatic modal rephasing, so that commercial graded‐index fibers reach field‐of‐view reflectivities well below . This offers a scalable route toward multimode absorption in fiber‐based and integrated photonics.
pool.authors: Helmut Hörner, Sahin K. Ozdemir, Stefan Rotter

pool.title: Current-driven reduction of topological protection in multichannel superconductors
pool.abstract: We investigate the robustness of topological phases in a Kitaev ladder composed of two coupled superconducting chains under the perturbing influence of a finite charge current. By introducing an effective Hamiltonian depending on the quasiparticle momentum induced by the current, we show that the two-mode topological phase, present in the isolated ladder, is fragile against a finite current flux. To characterize this behavior, we combine bulk topological invariants with real-space diagnostics, including the edge-edge quantum conditional mutual information Iee, which provides an entanglement-based signature of topological order. Our results provide an effective framework to describe how current injection and measurement processes can affect topological protection in superconducting nanostructures.
pool.authors: Alfonso Maiellaro

pool.title: Revisiting spin Hamiltonian parameters in a Kitaev material via Bayesian optimization of magnetization curves
pool.abstract: Determining the spin Hamiltonian of a magnetic compound is crucial for understanding its magnetic properties. A standard approach is to derive model parameters from $ab$ $initio$ calculations based on the crystal structure. However, the resulting Hamiltonian can depend sensitively on methodological details of the $ab$ $initio$ procedure. This issue is particularly evident in $α$-RuCl$_3$, a candidate Kitaev material. Here, we present an alternative, data-driven approach to determine the spin Hamiltonian parameters of $α$-RuCl$_3$ by Bayesian optimization of experimental magnetization curves along the $b$- and $c$-axis directions. We optimize five parameters, namely the Kitaev interaction $K$, off-diagonal interactions $Γ$ and $Γ'$, the Heisenberg interaction $J$, and the $c$-axis $g$-factor $g_c$. The parameter set that minimizes the cost function is $(K,Γ,Γ',J,g_c)=(-6.0,\,7.5,\,-0.3,\,-1.75,\,2.3)$, where the exchange couplings are in meV. We find that the cost function is insensitive to the absolute value of the Kitaev coupling $K$. Thus, the magnetization data alone do not determine its energy scale. The cost function also depends only weakly on $Γ'$ and $J$, while the optimization favors a large positive $Γ$. By computing the static spin structure factor, magnetic susceptibility, and specific heat, we show that these quantities favor the large-$Γ$ scenario over the small-$g_c$ scenario and that the parameter set that minimizes the cost function yields good agreement with experiment. The combination of Bayesian optimization and accurate low-energy solvers provides an effective approach for determining parameters of spin Hamiltonians. This methodology opens a systematic route to determining spin Hamiltonians in quantum magnets from experimental data.
pool.authors: Takahiro Misawa, Ryo Tamura, Kazuyoshi Yoshimi, Youhei Yamaji

pool.title: Topological tricritical Ising universality class in one dimension
pool.abstract: Abstract Quantum critical points can host symmetry-protected topological edge modes even when the bulk is gapless, giving rise to symmetry-enriched universality classes beyond the conventional Landau--Ginzburg--Wilson paradigm. Here we show that the tricritical Ising (TCI) critical point---described by a paradigmatic conformal field theory (CFT) with emergent supersymmetry---admits a topologically nontrivial, symmetry-enriched realization, which we term the topological TCI. We construct this critical point in the cluster O'Brien--Fendley spin chain by applying a symmetry-protected topological entangler to the original O'Brien--Fendley model. The two realizations therefore share the same bulk TCI CFT. Under open boundary conditions, however, the original model exhibits the free conformal boundary condition, whereas the cluster model exhibits a spontaneously fixed boundary condition: an infinitesimal boundary field can select one of the fixed boundary states, yielding spontaneous boundary magnetization. We further show that symmetry enrichment and boundary renormalization-group flow provide two routes to the spontaneously fixed boundary condition. Whereas the free and spontaneously fixed boundary conditions of the original model can be interconverted by tuning a symmetry-preserving boundary term, no such conversion occurs for the cluster model along the boundary deformations studied here, even in the strong-deformation limit. Although they share the same conventional boundary CFT data, including the boundary operator content and boundary $g$-function, the two realizations of the spontaneously fixed boundary condition are distinguished by different time-reversal charges of the disorder field, which impose different symmetry constraints on the allowed boundary conditions under symmetry-preserving boundary deformations. For the tested symmetry-preserving boundary perturbations that lift the exact twofold degeneracy, the finite-size energy splitting is numerically consistent with exponential decay over accessible system sizes, in stark contrast to the algebraic splitting at the symmetry-enriched Ising critical point of the cluster Ising spin chain. We also find that the topological TCI realization persists along a critical line in a two-parameter phase diagram. These results establish a symmetry-enriched TCI universality class and uncover boundary distinctions invisible to conventional boundary CFT data.

pool.title: Grid-state deformation in a no-jump non-Hermitian bosonic dimer
pool.abstract: Abstract We study the no-jump evolution of ideal grid states in a lossy bosonic dimer with differential decay. The effective non-Hermitian quadratic dynamics induces a complex symplectic flow in phase space that deforms both the primitive lattice vectors and the origin seed. The average decay rate controls common-mode attenuation, while coherent hopping and differential decay control the reduced dimer deformation. For resonant modes, the reduced displacement flow is oscillatory in the elliptic regime, linear at the exceptional point, and exponentially separating in the hyperbolic regime. Although projected lattice areas can change, the deformation comes from a determinant-one complex symplectic flow on the complexified phase space. For a Gaussian regularization of the origin seed in the resonant dimer, we derive the associated complex width matrix and show that the seed remains square-integrable and Gaussian for every positive initial width, all non-negative times, and all physical loss rates. For an initial two-mode qunaught product state, the lossless limit recovers the standard beam-splitter generation of a square GKP+ Bell pair, while the no-jump dynamics produces its non-Hermitian deformation. The full no-jump probability for a normalized finite-energy input sets the postselection cost and depends on its excitation-number distribution and the reduced dimer dynamics.

pool.title: Biochar addition enhances soil aggregate stability by modulating soil internal forces: the critical role of readily oxidized organic carbon and particulate organic carbon
pool.abstract: Abstract. Degradation of soil structure and function is a significant obstacle to sustainable agriculture, yet using biochar is known to be an effective way of increasing soil organic carbon and boosting structure. Aggregate stability is greatly influenced by soil internal forces (SIFs), such as van der Waals, hydration, and electrostatic forces. However, it is still not clear which specific organic carbon components play a significant role in the stability of aggregates and the action of soil internal forces. In this study, a field simulation experiment was conducted using maize straw and wheat straw biochars to investigate how biochar addtion affect soil aggregate stability. The findings showed that as the rate of biochar application increased from 0 % to 10 % over 180 day and 365 days, the contents of soil light fraction organic carbon (LFOC), particulate organic carbon (POC), dissolved organic carbon (DOC), readily oxidized organic carbon (ROC), as well as soil specific surface area and surface charge number, increased. The content of different carbon fractions decreased with prolonged incubation time, while soil electrochemical parameters continued to increase throughout the incubation period. Pearson correlation and redundancy analyses showed that soil active organic carbon fractions were strongly correlated with soil surface electrochemical properties, with ROC and POC being the primary factors. Soil aggregate stability increased with higher biochar application rates, and the beneficial effect of biochar on aggregate stability became increasingly pronounced over time. Based on the quantitative estimates of SIFs, the addition of biochar facilitated soil aggregates stability by increasing van der Waals attractive pressure and decreasing electrostatic repulsive pressure, and finally lowering net repulsive pressure between soil particles. The soil aggregate breaking strength increased quickly at initially and then leveled out as the electrolyte content decreased; 10−2 mol L−1 marked the tipping point. The study identified the active organic carbon (ROC and POC) fractions which could mediate the soil surface electrochemical properties and soil internal forces, finally enhance soil aggregate stability. Our research provides a theoretical basis for the targeted use and modifying of biochar to efficiently improve soil structure.
pool.authors: Xiaoshuai Song, Chenyang Xu, Hao Zhao, Jiangwen Li, Wei Du, Wuquan Ding, Zhenghong Yu, Fengbao Zhang, Feinan HU

pool.title: Superconducting proximity effect in a strongly correlated charge-transfer insulator
pool.abstract: Proximity-induced superconductivity in strongly correlated insulators provides a versatile route for engineering quantum states of matter and artificial systems with tailored functionalities. However, microscopic interplay between superconductivity and correlated insulating states remains poorly understood. Here we use ultralow-temperature scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM) to systemically investigate superconducting proximity effects in a charge-transfer insulator. Via STM tip manipulation, atomically sharp lateral junctions composed of superconducting monolayer H-NbSe2 and charge-transfer insulating monolayer T-NbSe2 are constructed, enabling direct access to tunable coupling regimes. In the weak-coupling regime, there is a robust proximity-induced superconducting gap in T-NbSe2, with a reduced gap value relative to that of H-NbSe2. Upon entering the strong-coupling regime, T-NbSe2 exhibits a superconducting gap comparable to that of H-NbSe2, accompanied by pronounced particle-hole-symmetric in-gap bound states, consistent with Yu-Shiba-Rusinov-like excitations. These findings establish monolayer H/T-NbSe2 lateral junctions as a model platform for elucidating superconducting proximity effects in strongly correlated charge-transfer insulators.

pool.title: Low Star Formation Efficiency in M31: Evidence for a Deficit of Bound Gas
pool.abstract: Abstract The Andromeda galaxy (M31) exhibits a systematically low star formation efficiency (SFE) compared to other star-forming galaxies. Star formation is thought to be regulated by the mass of gravitationally bound gas. To investigate whether the low SFE in M31 originates from a scarcity of such bound gas, we analyze the dynamical state of its giant molecular cloud (GMC) population by estimating their virial parameters ( α vir ). Using a James Clerk Maxwell Telescope SCUBA2 850 μ m dust-continuum GMC catalog as the parent sample, we combine it with IRAM 30 m CO(1–0) data to define a working sample of 173 GMCs and derive their kinematic properties. Most analyzed GMCs exhibit high α vir , indicating that they are predominantly gravitationally unbound at the ∼86 pc resolution of our observations. While no statistically significant global correlation is found between SFE and α vir for the full cloud sample, the upper quantiles of the SFE distribution show progressively stronger negative trends with increasing α vir . This upper-tail trend may arise from the combined effects of the virial parameter limiting the upper range of SFE values accessible to the GMC population and feedback-driven disruption reducing the number of high-SFE, high- α vir CO-bright clouds in the observed sample. The substantial scatter in the SFE- α vir plane likely reflects the diverse evolutionary stages of GMCs, the temporal mismatch between gas and star formation tracers, and the limitations of a cloud-averaged virial parameter as a tracer of internal dynamical structure, making a simple one-to-one correspondence between α vir and instantaneous SFE difficult to recover for individual GMCs.

pool.title: A cascaded probabilistic framework for stealth-aware MITRE ATT&CK path prediction in active directory adversary emulation
pool.abstract: Abstract Proactive adversary emulation requires anticipating multi-step attack trajectories, yet existing approaches rely on static attack graphs or single-signal models that cannot jointly satisfy coherence, tactical realism, and evasiveness. We propose a cascaded probabilistic framework for MITRE ATT&CK technique-path prediction in Active Directory environments, where exhaustive enumeration is intractable. Its contribution is a three-stage architecture that decouples these objectives instead of blending them. Stage 1, a two-layer unidirectional LSTM trained on observed threat-actor chains, emits a five-candidate pool rather than one technique. Stage 2, an empirical Markov tactic-transition gate, admits only attested transitions, including self-loops and backward moves a strict linear kill chain excludes. Stage 3 re-ranks survivors against a detection-rule corpus, favoring evasive over merely probable techniques. Candidates are masked at inference to Windows-applicable techniques, so outputs are technique chains, not instantiated paths. Under a prefix-disjoint protocol in which no evaluation context occurs in training, the true continuation is retained in the five-candidate pool more often than by a first-order predictor or an exact prefix-lookup table on identical pairs. Because Stage 3 both selects on and is scored by detection-rule density, the chains are re-scored against independently maintained corpora the selector never accesses; the exposure reduction persists there, and it is that transferred result that carries the evasiveness claim. Novel here is that structural admissibility is a hard constraint rather than a soft weight, so tactical realism cannot be traded away for likelihood or stealth. A case study initiated from a single initial-access technique further indicates that all tactic transitions within the returned path portfolio have attested support in the corpus transition matrix, and that no predicted step violates the ATT&CK-declared phase set of its technique.
pool.authors: Mahmoud Youssef, Nagwa L. Badr, Alshaimaa Abo‐alian

pool.title: Topology-optimized dielectric cavities for enhanced excitonic light emission from WSe2
pool.abstract: Abstract Photonic inverse design and, especially, topology optimization, enable dielectric cavities with deeply sub-diffraction mode volumes and high quality factors, thus offering a powerful platform for enhanced light-matter coupling. Here, we design and fabricate arrays of CMOS-compatible silicon cavities on sapphire with extreme subwavelength transverse mode sizes of only 30–40 nm ( $${{\bf{V}}}{{\boldsymbol{\sim }}}{{{\boldsymbol{\lambda }}}}^{{{\boldsymbol{3}}}}/{{\boldsymbol{2500}}}$$ V ~ λ 3 / 2500 ). These cavities are engineered for deterministic coupling to a monolayer (or few-layer) excitonic material, producing strong near-field localization directly beneath the 2D material. Photoluminescence (PL) measurements show reproducible tenfold raw enhancement relative to bare silicon, which corresponds to a “per-area” normalized enhancement on the order of 10 3 , accounting for the small area of the deeply subwavelength mode volume, consistent with numerical simulations that account for material absorption and fabrication tolerances. Furthermore, time-resolved PL measurements reveal pronounced lifetime shortening and non-exponential dynamics, indicating cavity-mediated exciton-exciton interactions. The optimized cavity geometry enhances the far-field collection efficiency and supports scalable integration with van der Waals semiconductors. Our results show that the arrays of topology-optimized dielectric cavities are a versatile, scalable platform for controlling excitonic emission and interactions, which creates new opportunities in nonlinear optics, optoelectronics, and quantum photonics.

pool.title: The Buffer Illusion: How TRIS and HEPES Enhance Bioactivity of Bioglass 45S5
pool.abstract: Abstract In vitro tests of glass, glass-ceramic, or ceramic biomaterials such as synthetic hydroxyapatite (HA) and β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) are performed using simulated body fluid (SBF), in which the pH is maintained using TRIS buffer (ISO standard 23317:2014; recently updated as ISO standard 23317:2025). When evaluating the experiments, we not only looked at the tested material itself but also analyzed the SBF leachate. We have found out that TRIS buffer, as well as other tested buffers (Good’s buffers), actively interacts with glass and ceramic materials. They significantly accelerate their dissolution (up to 3× higher compared to unbuffered SBF). This increases the local supersaturation of biogenic ions near the surface and promotes the formation of the expected hydroxyapatite (the newly formed hydroxyapatite layer is labeled as HAp). In this work, we focused on bioglass 45S5 to observe the corrosion rate of the glass surface on samples in the form of bulk, in SBF solutions buffered with (i) TRIS and (ii) HEPES, and we used (iii) SBF without any buffer for comparison. The glass corrosion rate and the growth kinetics of the new HAp layer (SEM/EDS, XRD, FTIR) were compared with the results of the leachate analyses (pH, ICP-OES). The concentration of SiIV in the leachates showed the corrosive effects of each of the solutions, while the concentrations of Ca2+ and (PO4)3– confirmed precipitation of a new Ca–P phase. The results confirmed earlier findings and showed that the TRIS and HEPES buffering systems are not inert and are strongly corrosive to bioglass 45S5. Moreover, their parts incorporate into the newly formed Ca–P layer and change its quality and crystallinity. These findings suggest that the current approach to in vitro testing of these materials requires reconsideration.
pool.authors: Tereza Přívracká, Karolína Opavová, Petr Bezdička, Jan Labuta, Dana Rohanová

pool.title: Revisiting mRNA capping in Mononegavirales : a promising, yet underexplored antiviral target
pool.abstract: ABSTRACT mRNA capping is a co-transcriptional, nuclear process in eukaryotes that adds a cap onto the 5' end of RNA to confer stability, efficient translation, and nuclear export. Viruses have evolved diverse strategies by mimicking or subverting host pathways to install an mRNA cap for efficient gene expression and evasion of the host innate immune response. The conventional mRNA capping pathway, employed by many RNA and DNA viruses, is mediated by dedicated RNA 5′-triphosphatase, guanylyltransferase, and methyltransferase enzymes. In contrast, many RNA viruses utilize unconventional capping mechanisms that diverge from the canonical pathway, offering unique opportunities to develop virus family-specific antiviral therapeutics. Among negative-sense RNA viruses, members of the order Mononegavirales harbor a unique capping domain, polyribonucleotidyltransferase (PRNTase), embedded within the viral RdRp large (L) protein. Unlike the conventional guanylyltransferase-mediated mechanism, PRNTase catalyzes mRNA capping through the formation of a covalent L-pRNA intermediate rather than the canonical GMP-enzyme intermediate. The HR motif in PRNTase, involved in covalent linking to mRNA, is highly conserved in non-segmented negative-strand RNA viruses. This review focuses on structural and functional insights into Mononegavirales capping, highlighting the conserved motifs and domain architecture that make it a promising therapeutic target.
pool.authors: Khadijah Khan, Mohammad Ejaz Adil, Monika Antil, Dilip Kumar

pool.title: LP(a)-LOWERING THERAPIES (siRNA / ASO) AND ATHEROSCLEROTIC RISK REDUCTION
pool.abstract: Background: Genetically determined and independent risk factor, High levels of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)].Traditional lipid-lowering drugs like statins and PCSK9 inhibitors are not effective enough to decrease the levels of Lp(a) and leave a considerable amount of cardiovascular risk.New RNA-based treatment approaches, such as small interfering RNA (siRNA) and antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), are currently appearing as the potential solutions, which can significantly reduce the levels of Lp(a) by acting on the expression of the hepatic LPA gene.The purpose of this study was to assess the professional attitudes to the safety, efficacy, and clinical relevance of Lp (a)-lowering RNA therapeutics and their role in reducing the risk of ASCVD.Methods: A cross-sectional survey was carried out quantitatively on cardiology, pharmacology, and molecular biology professionals.A 30-item Likert-scale questionnaire (1 = Strongly Disagree to 5 = Strongly Agree) was designed to gather the data and was given to 263 respondents.The data were analyzed through SPSS 26 in terms of Normality (Shapiro-Wilk), Reliability (Cronbach-alpha), and Validity (KMO and Bartlett's), Inferential Tests (t-test, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis, Chi-square).Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis were also done to test associations and predictive relationships between variables. Results:The distribution of all items was found to be normal (p > 0.05) and had a high reliability (0.978) and a high construct validity (KMO = 0.874, p = 0.001).There were also notable variations by gender, age, and education level (p < 0.05), and this demonstrates that demographic and professional variables have a role in perceptions of RNA-based lipid-lowering therapy.Correlation analysis showed that there were strong positive relationships between all variables (r = 0.680.88,p < 0.01).The significance of the regression model was (R 2 = 0.716, p = 0.001), which indicated that awareness, perceived efficacy, safety, and adoption intention had positive influences on attitudes toward risk reduction of ASCVD.Conclusion: The research supports the hypothesis that healthcare and biomedical professionals have a very favorable opinion of Lp(a)-lowering siRNA/ASO therapies as a safe and effective method of residual cardiovascular risk management.The statistical results indicate a high level of reliability, validity, and predictability, which attests to the high level of professional trust in RNA-based therapeutics.Such results justify the importance of genetic and molecular treatments in the future cardiovascular risk management systems, which would be a significant change towards precision lipidology and personalized medicine.

pool.title: Effect of bacteriophages on cytokine production by human peripheral blood mononuclear cells and their subpopulations
pool.abstract: Introduction Fulfilling a vision that extends beyond their role as antibiotic alternatives, bacteriophages are now recognized as active immunomodulators, a concept aligning with early hypotheses of their biological activity. In addition to their bactericidal action, these properties require detailed investigation. This study aims to characterize the immunomodulatory effects of bacteriophages on pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokine production by human immune cells isolated from healthy blood donors. Methods We assessed the secretion of a comprehensive panel of 11 cytokines (including IFN-γ, IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-10) by peripheral blood mononuclear cells and their isolated subpopulations (B and T lymphocytes, helper and cytotoxic T lymphocytes, natural killer cells, and monocytes). The cells were incubated for 24 hours with purified Escherichia coli phage T4 and therapeutic staphylococcal phage A5/80. Reference cells were incubated with lipopolysaccharide from E. coli B at a concentration corresponding to its activity in the applied phage preparations. For comparison, we also assessed cytokine responses to human adenovirus 5, used as a benchmark for a virus capable of infecting human cells. Results Cell-specific analysis revealed a distinct hierarchy in immune responsiveness: our data suggest that monocytes may act as the primary sensors driving cytokine signatures, while we did not confirm a discernible direct response in B, natural killer, and cytotoxic T cells. Importantly, the magnitude of these responses was markedly lower than the robust inflammatory cytokine secretion triggered by human adenovirus 5, providing context for the phage-induced effects relative to a viral infection of human cells and underscoring the limited inflammatory footprint of therapeutic phages. Conclusion These results improve our understanding of phage–human immune system interactions, which is important for appreciating their broader impact on human homeostasis and for assessing the safety of phage therapy.
pool.authors: Hubert Kasprzak, Monika Kniotek, Katarzyna Zielniok, Maciej Przybylski, Andrzej Górski, Ryszard Międzybrodzki

pool.title: Antimicrobial Activity of Partially Purified Bacteriocin-Like Inhibitory Substance (BLIS) from L. plantarum Against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus
pool.abstract: The current study aimed to evaluate the inhibitory efficacy of partially purified Bacteriocin-Like Inhibitory Substance (BLIS) derived from L. plantarum against clinical bacterial isolates. L. plantarum isolates were isolated from different sources and confirmed via molecular amplification of the species-specific Lplan gene. Gram-positive and Gram-negative isolates included in this study were (10) isolates of E. coli and S. aureus; both species were isolated from patients with urinary tract infection (UTIs). All clinical isolates were identified using 16S rRNA gene amplification. The 16S rRNA gene specific for E. coli gave a positive result at 361 bp, and the 16S rRNA gene specific for S. aureus gave a positive result at 711 bp. BLIS was extracted from the cell-free supernatant (CFS) of L. plantarum under anaerobic conditions at 37 °C for 48 h and partially purified via ammonium sulfate precipitation and ultrafiltration through a 10,000 kDa membrane. The total protein concentration was evaluated by the Bradford assay, revealing 22.0258 µg/mL in each 1g of BLIS extract. Agar well diffusion testing before and after partially purified BLIS showed significant inhibition against Gram-positive S. aureus, compared to Gram-negative E. coli dependence on concentration. Inhibition zones of S. aureus were 19.0 ± 0.71 and 8.2 ± 0.45 in E. coli, and MIC/ was 3.750 mg/mL for S. aureus and 7.500 mg/mL for E. coli. These findings demonstrate that BLIS functions as an antimicrobial agent against both S. aureus and E. coli bacteria that cause UTI infections.

pool.title: Metal-organic and covalent organic frameworks for precision drug delivery: a precision-by-design evidence framework for biologically accountable nanomedicine
pool.abstract: Introduction Metal-organic frameworks and covalent organic frameworks offer a rare opportunity to design drug carriers from molecular building blocks upward. Yet high loading capacity and stimulus-responsive release alone do not constitute precision delivery. Methods We critically synthesized evidence on MOF and COF pore-level cargo interactions, framework and surface engineering, endogenous and externally triggered release, active targeting, biomimetic coatings, nanozyme activity and theranostic integration. Precision delivery was decomposed into five evidence-qualified dimensions: material, spatial, temporal, mechanistic and translational precision. Results The evidence supports the complementary strengths of the two families across small-molecule, protein, nucleic-acid, gas and catalytic therapies. Direct evidence is strongest for individual component technologies, selected antibody-targeted systems and two-component hybrids. Recurrent evidence gaps include incomplete particle characterization in biological media, reliance on total-tissue accumulation rather than cell-specific delivery, and insufficient separation of carrier degradation from drug release. Discussion A framework becomes precise only when it maintains a defined material identity, reaches a biologically justified compartment, releases an active payload at the intended place and time, and does so with measurable improvements in exposure, efficacy and safety. This requires a precision-by-design framework that maps claims to minimum evidence and links material critical quality attributes to biological mechanisms, translational assays and development decisions.
pool.authors: Xinwei Li, Haonan Zhang, Ruidong Ding, Feng Wang

pool.title: Knockout and re-expression system for mutant analysis in primary mouse T cells
pool.abstract: We describe here an efficient method for gene editing in mouse T cells, based on well-established, high-efficiency retroviral transduction protocols. Our platform allows analysis of mutant phenotypes in primary murine T cells in vitro and in vivo . This approach uses a single retroviral vector to simultaneously knockout an endogenous gene and ectopically express its mutant version. This knockout/re-expression vector can be used as the only plasmid to transduce Cas9-expressing T cells, or used together with a Cas9 retroviral vector to transduce T cells from any mouse strain. We validated the system for analysis of murine T cells by targeting key molecules in proximal T cell signaling, i.e. CD3γ and Zap70. We obtain high knockout and re-expression efficiencies in both Cas9-expressing and non-Cas9 T cells. Knockout efficiencies can be further improved by gRNA multiplexing. Endogenous proteins compete with their ectopically expressed mutants or tagged versions for cellular location, protein interactions and cellular functions. Here, we quantified the incorporation of CD3γ-GFP into surface T cell receptor (TCR) complexes. Our data shows that the knockout and re-expression platform improves integration of CD3γ-GFP into the TCR. Therefore, eliminating competition between endogenous and ectopic proteins benefits analyses of protein assemblies and signaling pathways in primary T cells. Furthermore, we validated advantages of our system for mutant analysis using wild-type and mutant Zap70s. Zap70 mutants deficient in TCR binding or kinase activity show their phenotypes only in the absence of endogenous protein, further validating our knockout/re-expression approach. Most importantly, this system can be used to generate gene-edited primary T cells for in vivo studies, such as the quantification of anti-tumor responses. Our knockout and re-expression platform provides a useful gene editing tool for primary T cells in fundamental research and immunotherapy development.
pool.authors: Vasileios Morfos, Meredith C. Frie, Daniel Peschkov, Juliana Wagner, Björn F. Lillemeier, Joanna Brzostek

pool.title: Moderate phosphorus reduction under split drip fertigation maintains maize yield and coincides with closer root–available phosphorus spatial correspondence
pool.abstract: Introduction Phosphorus (P) has low mobility in soil, so crop P acquisition depends on both P availability and its spatial accessibility to roots. We hypothesized that moderate P reduction under split fertigation could maintain maize productivity by improving the coordination between available P and root distribution. Methods A two-year field experiment was conducted in irrigated spring maize in Inner Mongolia, China. Split monoammonium phosphate fertigation was applied at 105 (CP1), 127.5 (CP2), and 150 kg P 2 O 5 ha -1 (CP3), together with a no-P treatment (CP0) and conventional basal diammonium phosphate application at 150 kg P 2 O 5 ha -1 (CK). Root length density and Olsen P were measured in paired soil blocks within the 0–40 cm soil profile at silking, together with plant P accumulation, biomass, grain yield, and P-use efficiency. Results CP2 increased Olsen P availability and root proliferation in the middle and deeper soil layers and showed closer spatial correspondence between root length density and Olsen P at 20–40 cm. These changes were associated with greater post-silking P accumulation and biomass. Reducing P input by 15% maintained grain yield at the level of CP3 and increased yield by 4.07% relative to CK, while apparent P recovery efficiency and P agronomic efficiency increased by 77.36% and 54.62%, respectively. Further reducing P input to 105 kg P 2 O 5 ha⁻¹ decreased P accumulation, biomass, and yield, whereas 150 kg P 2 O 5 ha -1 provided no additional yield benefit. Discussion Under the conditions of this study, moderate P reduction under split fertigation maintained maize yield while reducing fertilizer input and enhancing P-use efficiency, and this response was associated with closer spatial correspondence between root distribution and soil available P.
pool.authors: Changle Liu, Shuping Hu, 马达灵, Liqing Wang, Xiaofang Yu, Julin Gao

pool.title: CHEMICAL MODIFICATIONS OF NUCLEOSIDE ANALOGUES FOR ANTIVIRAL THERAPY
pool.abstract: Background: The role of chemical changes of nucleoside analogues in antiviral treatment is that it provides increased effectiveness of the drug, its greater bioactivity, and resistance to the virus.The changes play significant roles in the production of good antiviral drugs against HIV, hepatitis, and new viral infections.It is significant to understand the degree of knowledge and awareness that students and professionals have to make further research and clinical applications in the area.Objective: The use of nucleoside analogues in the treatment of antiviral therapy was the purpose of the present study, aiming to determine the level of knowledge, awareness and the perception of chemical modifications of the analogues.Methodology: A cross-sectional study design was employed, which was quantitative in nature.A total of 179 respondents were sampled and filled using a structured questionnaire with questions based on demographic, knowledge and opinion.Data analysis was done through descriptive and inferential statistics, which included normality test, reliability test (Cronbach's Alpha), validity tests (KMO test, and Bartletts test), independent samples t-test, one-way ANOVA, Kruskal -Wallis test, chi-square test, correlation and regression test.Results: The findings suggested that the data were normally distributed, reliable (Cronbach's Alpha = 0.91) and valid (KMO = 0.83, p = 0.05).The differences were also significant concerning gender and age (p < 0.05).Education level was also associated with awareness strongly.The Correlation analysis showed that there were positive correlations between knowledge, attitude and awareness.The regression equation demonstrated that the perceptions were largely predicted by knowledge, education, awareness, and attitude and that the equation contributed 62 percent of the variance (R² = 0.62). Conclusion:The research findings conclude that there is a high degree of knowledge and information among the respondents about the nucleoside analogue modification.There is a great impact of education and awareness on antiviral therapy perceptions.Exposure to education and research can also help in enriching the knowledge and making advances in the development of antiviral drugs.

pool.title: Beyond cell replacement: restoring organelle homeostasis as the next frontier of regenerative medicine
pool.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) have traditionally been viewed as disorders driven by individual pathological processes, including protein aggregation, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, impaired autophagy, and neuroinflammation. However, growing evidence demonstrates that these mechanisms are not isolated events but interconnected manifestations of disrupted intracellular organelle communication. Dynamic interactions among mitochondria, the ER, lysosomes, peroxisomes, and other organelles coordinate calcium signaling, bioenergetics, proteostasis, lipid metabolism, and cellular stress adaptation, thereby preserving neuronal homeostasis. Progressive disruption of this communication network represents a fundamental driver of neuronal dysfunction and degeneration, suggesting that restoration of organelle homeostasis may constitute a more effective therapeutic strategy than targeting individual molecular pathways. In parallel, regenerative medicine has evolved beyond the concept of cell replacement toward approaches that enhance the resilience and repair capacity of surviving cells. Among these, mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-derived secretomes and extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as promising cell-free therapeutics owing to their diverse repertoire of proteins, lipids, metabolites, cytokines, growth factors, and regulatory RNAs capable of simultaneously modulating multiple cellular pathways. Accumulating evidence indicates that these bioactive cargos modulate mitochondrial function, alleviate ER stress, improve autophagy-lysosomal activity, reduce oxidative stress and neuroinflammation, and reinforce proteostasis, collectively promoting intracellular homeostasis. Here, we propose organelle homeostasis as a promising focus for regenerative medicine and discuss how cell-free therapies may redefine therapeutic strategies for NDs by restoring the intracellular communication networks that sustain cellular resilience. Finally, we highlight current translational challenges and future opportunities for engineering next-generation cell-free therapeutics targeting complex diseases.
pool.authors: Filipa Ferreira-Antunes, Marta Fernandes Lima, Anabela Moreira, Fernando J. Silva, Belém Sampaio‐Marques, António J. Salgado

pool.title: UV-derived scattering as a high-throughput readout for adeno-associated virus-like particle separation screenings
pool.abstract: Virus-like particles (VLPs), including those derived from adeno-associated virus (AAV), are increasingly investigated for vaccination, capsid engineering, and gene-delivery applications. Although precipitation and aqueous two-phase separation (ATPS) represent promising alternatives to adsorption-based capture, their optimization is limited by the lack of rapid analytical methods suitable for complex process samples. Here, VP3-only AAV5 VLPs produced in Escherichia coli were used as a model system to evaluate UV-derived light scattering as a high-throughput separation readout. Blank-corrected absorbance at 320 nm was used as a relative descriptor of particulate-associated scattering, while scattering-corrected absorbance at 280 nm monitored the soluble biomolecular fraction. During PEG precipitation, A320 showed condition-dependent agreement with anti-AAV5 ELISA, with the closest correspondence for PEG4000 and increasing divergence at lower PEG molecular weights. Capsid-spiking experiments further showed that dispersed intact capsids alone contributed only marginally to A320, indicating that the signal primarily reflects larger scattering-active structures accompanying capsid depletion. The workflow enabled screening and analysis of 170 precipitation and PEG/phosphate ATPS conditions in biological duplicate within 3 days. Low-molecular-weight PEG systems provided stronger separation between soluble biomolecular material and particulate-associated scattering. In PEG400 ATPS, pH altered the distribution of scattering-active material and capsids between the liquid phases and interphase, whereas selected precipitation conditions showed higher recovery of assembled capsids after resolubilization than ATPS, at the expense of lower impurity removal. Overall, UV-derived scattering provides a rapid, scalable first-line readout for comparing separation conditions and reducing the number of samples requiring capsid-specific and structural characterization.

pool.title: Neonatal outcomes and immune reprogramming induced by prenatal opioid and hepatitis C exposure
pool.abstract: Introduction Prenatal opioid exposure (POE) is an escalating public health concern. However, its impact on neonatal immune development remains poorly defined. This study examined how POE, with or without maternal hepatitis C (hepatitis C virus, HCV) infection, shapes neonatal immunity. Methods Umbilical cord blood was collected from pregnancies included uncomplicated term controls (n=38) and deliveries in patients with severe opioid use disorder on medication-assisted treatment, with (n=41) or without HCV (n=34) infection. Flow cytometry was used to characterize cell phenotype and functional response to stimulation. Single-cell RNA sequencing was used to investigate transcriptomics changes. Results POE was associated with smaller birth size, higher rates of congenital anomalies, and longer intensive care admissions. Immune profiling showed a proinflammatory milieu, reduced circulating levels of neuroprotective factors, expanded memory/effector T and B cells, blunted T-cell responses, and markedly reduced natural killer (NK) cell frequency and cytotoxicity, especially in POE HCV+ newborns. Monocytes exhibited inflammatory reprogramming with impaired antiviral and tissue repair pathways and disrupted lymphoid–innate immune cell communication. Discussion These findings suggest that POE-driven immune disequilibrium may underlie adverse early-life outcomes and highlight monitoring and intervention targets.
pool.authors: Brianna M. Doratt, Heather True, Sheridan B. Wagner, Delphine C. Malherbe, Cynthia Cockerham, John O'Brien, Ilhem Messaoudi

pool.title: Recent Advances in the Molecular Mechanisms of Nutritional Biochemistry in Human Health and Disease
pool.abstract: Nutritional biochemistry has evolved from descriptive assessments of nutrient intake to a mechanistic discipline that interrogates how dietary components regulate cellular signaling, gene expression, and metabolic homeostasis.This review synthesizes recent advances in the molecular actions of macronutrients, micronutrients, and bioactive food constituents on key nutrient-sensing networks, including AMPK-mTOR, SIRT1-PGC-1α, PPARs, FXR/TGR5, and Nrf2.Particular emphasis is placed on how these pathways coordinate energy metabolism, redox balance, and immune function, and how their dysregulation contributes to metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and cancer.We also examine emerging data from metabolomics and microbiome research showing that diet-derived metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, and tryptophan indole derivatives act as signaling intermediates at the interface of the gut, liver, immune system, and brain.In parallel, nutrigenomic and epigenetic studies illustrate how vitamins, methyl donors, amino acids, and phytochemicals remodel chromatin and transcriptional programs that shape individual disease risk.Finally, we discuss how integrated multi-omics and systems-biology approaches are beginning to define molecular phenotypes of dietary response, providing a framework for precision nutrition.Remaining challenges, including inter-individual variability, environmental modifiers, and limited large-scale clinical validation, are highlighted as priorities for future research aimed at translating mechanistic insight into targeted, personalized dietary strategies for chronic disease prevention.

pool.title: Deciphering isonicotinylation and mast cell-associated pathogenic patterns in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: evidence from ensemble learning-driven multi-omics and in vitro validation
pool.abstract: Background Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is dystrophin-deficiency skeletal and cardiac muscle disease. Protein post-translational modification (PTM) and aberrant immune cell activation play a key role in its pathogenesis. Objective Our study aims to investigate isonicotinylation (Kinic)-associated signature modulatory patterns in mast cells and DMD pathogenesis. Methods We first performed integrated bioinformatic methods, such as WGCNA, GSVA, and CIBERSORT to identify Kinic and mast cell (KM)-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in DMD patient muscle bulk profiles (GSE38417 and GSE109178). Next, consensus clustering and assembling machine learning pipeline identified KM-associated diagnostic model and molecular subgroups in training the DMD patient muscle bulk set (GSE6011), and then, diagnostic model performance was examined in the independent DMD patient muscle bulk set (GSE32720). In addition, SHAP analysis decoded the main contributor in KM-associated diagnostic model construction, and contributor molecular and immune characters in DMD were estimated in GSE6011 and the DMD mouse muscle single-cell transcriptomic dataset (GSE213925) assisted by computational virtual cells. In addition, the deep learning framework and network pharmacology identified the drug synergy strategy for the treatment of DMD. Finally, the in vitro assay identified expression patterns of the main contributor. Results KM-associated molecular patterns can potentially guide the diagnostic and molecular stratification for DMD patients. USP18 can be considered an upregulated and mast cell-distributed hub gene involved in pathogenesis of DMD. In addition, finafloxacin with BRD-K10482608 can be considered two potential therapeutic candidates for DMD patient clinical applications. Conclusion Our investigation described a novel forecasting and therapeutic model for DMD patients, which potentially enhances DMD patient clinical translation.
pool.authors: Sunrui Yu, Duojia Xu, Yuting Hua, Hangfeng Mo, Yujin Liu

pool.title: Antioxidant properties of chicken feather hydrolysates
pool.abstract: The goal of the research was to study the antioxidant properties of peptides obtained during microbiological fermentation of feather waste with keratinolytic strains of Bacillus licheniformis BAL-1 and BAL-2. The methods. The major 17 peptide sequences identified by LC-MS/MS with a relative content of >1% were analyzed in the BIOPEP-UWM database to predict bioactive profiles. The interaction of promising peptides with the Kelch domain of the Keap1 protein (PDB ID: 2FLU) was assessed using molecular docking (HPEPDOCK 2.0) and calculation of the thermodynamic parameters of the complexes (PRODIGY). Experimental assessment of the total antioxidant capacity (TAC) of the hydrolysates was performed using the FRAP, DPPH, and ORAC methods. The results. According to the in silico -analysis, most of the studied peptides contained fragments with the predicted antioxidant activity and formed stable complexes with Keap1. The highest affinity was demonstrated by the GGGDIPRQPLYPPLPPRPG peptide, for which ΔG = -9.8 kcal mol⁻¹ and Kd = 6.6×10⁻⁸ M were calculated; this peptide interacted with the key residues of the binding site (GLU216, ARG146, GLN239), competing with the endogenous ligand Nrf2. In the FRAP and DPPH tests, the activity of the samples was below the detection limit, which was due to the deficiency of reactive amino acids (Cys, Trp) in the peptide fractions. Whereas, according to the ORAC method, the BAL-1 and BAL-2 hydrolysates exceeded the original feather by 25.5 and 31.3 times, reaching values of 812.68±32.62 and 997.46±66.04 μmol-eq. quercetin/L, respectively. Conclusion. The obtained results confirm the potential of fermented chicken feather hydrolysates as a source of bioactive peptides with a dual mechanism of antioxidant action (direct radical scavenging and Nrf2 pathway activation) for the further development of functional feed additives. The practical significance of the research lies in substantiating the possibility of using the obtained hydrolysates as a component of functional feed additives to enhance the resistance of poultry to oxidative stress factors, thereby reducing the dependence of the industry on synthetic antioxidants.
